151.1: Raag Gauri Guareri, Chaupade and Dupade, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). There is one God, Ik Oankar, the One who pervades all and is ever the same; his Name is Sat (the One who truly is); he is the Creator, the Being who dwells in all, without fear, without enmity, his form beyond time, unborn, self-existent, realised by the Guru's grace. The fear of God is very heavy; its weight is great. The mind's own counsel is light, and (one who follows it) speaks light words. If one walks with (this fear) set upon the head and bears its weight, then, by (God's) glance of grace and his favour, the Guru's wisdom is gained. No one crosses (the world-ocean) without the fear (of God). (Only they cross who,) living in that fear and adorning (their lives) with love, have kept the fear (in the heart). In the fear (of God) the fire within the body blazes, and with that fear it keeps ablaze; in the fear, and adorned through the Shabad, a life of reverent fear is fashioned. Without the fear, what is fashioned is raw, utterly raw: the mould is blind, and blind is the hammer's stroke. In (the self-willed one's) intellect arises a craving for the play (of the world); for all its thousand clevernesses, the heat (of the fear) does not reach it. O Nanak, the speech of the manmukh is (empty as) the wind; his word is blind, idle wind and worthless. ॥3॥

Raag Gauri is sung in several forms, and the heading of each hymn names its form: Gauri Guareri, Cheti, Bairagan, Poorbi, Dakhani, Majh, Mala and others. Dupade (du, two; pad, stanza): hymns of two stanzas.
Sacha here is saancha, the mould into which metal is cast, not sacha, true; sat is the hammer's stroke that stamps it. The image is the minting of a coin, as in the 38th pauri of Japji Sahib.
151.2: Raag Gauri, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Through the fear (of God) one finds the home (within), and in that home dwells the fear; through that fear, (every other) fear departs. What sort of fear is that, if in it some (other) fear still takes hold? (O Lord,) apart from you there is no other place (of refuge); whatever happens is all your will. One would be afraid if there were some other to fear; to live in fear upon fear is only the turmoil of the mind. The soul does not die, nor does it drown or swim across. He who made (all) this does everything. By his Hukam one comes, and by his Hukam one goes; in this world and the next, one abides within his Hukam. Where there is cruelty, attachment, desire and pride, there hunger (craving) runs high, like a river (in flood). The fear (of God) is (the soul's) food and drink, its support; without eating it, the foolish waste away and die. Rare, very rare, is the one who has someone (to call his own); everyone is yours, and you are the one who cares for all. He to whom belong all beings and creatures, all wealth and property: O Nanak, to describe him and to reflect on him is hard. ॥4॥
151.3: Raag Gauri, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Make wisdom your mother and contentment your father, and make truthful living your special brother. There is something to say, but it cannot be said: (O Lord,) the worth of your creation cannot be reckoned. Effort and awareness, these two, have become the parents-in-law, and, O mind, good conduct has been taken as the wife. Union (with the holy) is the wedding day, and parting (from the world) the marriage; truth is the offspring: says Nanak, this is the union (with God). ॥3॥
152.1: Raag Gauri, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). (The body) is a union of air, water and fire, the play of a restless, fickle intellect. (It has) nine doors, and the Tenth Gate: O wise one, understand this thought. He (the Lord) alone is the one who speaks, utters and hears. The one who reflects on his own self becomes truly wise. The body is clay; it is the air (the breath) that speaks. O wise one, understand: who is it that has died? What has died is the awareness (that ran after Maya), strife and pride; the One who beholds (all) has not died. That for which (people) go to the banks of tiraths, that jewel, that treasure, is within the heart itself. Reading and reading, the pandit voices his arguments, but does not know the thing that is within (him). I have not died; what has died is my demon (of mine-ness). The One who pervades all has not died. Says Nanak, the Guru has shown me Brahm (God), and (now) I see no one dying or being born. ॥4॥
152.2: Raag Gauri Dakhani, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). The one who, hearing again and again, understands and accepts the Name, to him I am ever a sacrifice. Those whom (the Lord) himself leads astray find no place, no refuge; (O Lord,) you give understanding, and join (us) in union (with you). May I receive the Naam, that it may go with me; without the Name, all are bound by death. The support of the Name is (my) farming and (my) trade; sin and merit are a bundle of seed (that will sprout). Those within whose hearts lust and anger strike their blows forget the Name and depart with falseness in their minds. True is the teaching of the True Guru: (by it) body and mind are cooled, and the True One is recognised. The mark (of those who receive it) is that they live untouched, like the water-lily and the lotus in water; steeped in the Shabad, they are sweet as the juice of the sugarcane. By (his) Hukam, through the joining (of destiny), the fortress (of the body) with ten gates (is made); in it the five (elements) dwell, joined with the infinite Light. He is himself the goods that are weighed, and himself the trader; O Nanak, through the Name he is the one who adorns (all). ॥4॥
152.3: Raag Gauri, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). How can it be known where (the soul) comes from, where it springs from, and where it goes and merges? How is it bound, and how does it win liberation? How does it merge in the imperishable (state of) Sahaj? One who has the Naam in the heart and the ambrosial Name on the lips through the Name of the Lord (Narhar) becomes, like the Lord, free of desire. (The soul) comes of itself, by the natural order, and of itself it goes; it springs from the mind and merges into the mind. The Gurmukh is free; no bond holds him. Reflecting on the Shabad, he is released through the Lord's Name. On a tree many birds make their home for the night; some happy, some sad, they are ruined by attachment in the mind. As evening passes into dawn, they look to the sky, and fly off in the ten directions; (so beings) run about as their deeds have written. Those joined to the Name (take this world as) a brief halt in a goil (a pasture); (in them) the poisoned pot of lust and anger bursts. Without the goods (of the Name), house and shop (of the heart) lie empty; meeting the Guru, the hard shutters are opened. The Saadh (the holy Guru) is met through destiny from the past; the perfect people of the Lord rejoice in the True One. Giving their minds and bodies, they receive (the Name) in Sahaj and with love; Nanak touches their feet. ॥5॥
153.1: Raag Gauri, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). (In me are) lust and anger, and my mind is in Maya; my mind's love wakes to falsehood and vice; I have gathered a capital of sin and greed. (O Lord, your) purifying Name in the mind is the raft and the boat (to cross over). Wonderful, wonderful are you, O True One; I lean on you (alone). I am a sinner; you alone are pure. Like water set on the fire, (the mortal) seethes and bubbles in his speech; the tongue and each sense has its own craving; the gaze is on vice; there is neither fear nor love (of God). Only by killing self-conceit does one obtain the Name. One who dies through the Shabad does not die again; without dying (so), how can one become perfect? The mind stays caught in the world's show and in duality; Narayan is eternal: whatever he does, that comes to pass. I can board the ship (of the Name) only when my turn comes; those held back from the ship are beaten in the Lord's court. I praise the True One; blessed is the Guru's door. O Nanak, at (the Guru's) door and in the home (of the heart) is the One Creator, Ekankar. ॥4॥
153.2: Raag Gauri, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Reflecting on God (Brahm), the (inverted) lotus (of the heart) has turned upright; in the sky of the Tenth Gate the stream of Amrit flows; the Lord (Murari) himself pervades the three worlds. O my mind, do not wander in doubt; when the mind is won over, the essence of Amrit is drunk. Having won (the game of) life, the mind has accepted death (to self); self-conceit has died, and the mind has come to know (this) from within itself; (the Lord's) glance of grace has fallen, and within one's own home the home (of the Lord) is known. Continence, truthful living, pilgrimage and holy bathing lie in the Name; why should I make a great show (of anything else)? The Lord, Nar Narayan, knows every heart from within. Were I to believe in any other, only then would I go to another's house; of whom should I ask? There is no other place. Through the Guru's teaching, Nanak is absorbed in Sahaj. ॥4॥
153.3: Raag Gauri, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). If the True Guru is met, he shows (one) that death (to self) whose joy, the joy of dying (so) and (truly) living, becomes dear within; casting off pride, one reaches the city in the sky (the highest state of the spirit). (All) have come with death written (for them); no one is to stay (here). By repeating and meditating on the Lord, one finds a lasting abode in the Lord's refuge. If the True Guru is met, duality runs away; the lotus (of the heart) blossoms, and the mind clings to the Lord God; one who dies while living has the supreme joy before him. When the True Guru is met, one becomes pure through the discipline of truth; (climbing) the Guru's ladder, one rises higher and higher; by (God's) grace (this) is found, and the fear of Jam comes to an end. When the Guru is met, one meets (the Lord) and merges in his embrace; in his grace (the Guru) has shown (him) the home, the mansion (of the Lord); O Nanak, (the Guru) has killed his Haumai and united him (with the Lord). ॥4॥
154.1: Raag Gauri, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). What has fallen (to one's lot) from past deeds, no one can erase; what can I know of what lies ahead? Whatever pleased him is what has come to pass; there is no second, no other, who does anything. (O Lord,) I do not know how great your grace is, how great your gift; your Name is my deeds, my dharma and my caste. You are so great a Giver, the One who gives to all; your storehouses of devotion never run short. The pride one takes is of no avail; soul and body, all is in your keeping. You slay and bring to life again; forgiving, you unite (with yourself); as it pleases you, so you have (beings) repeat your Name. You are the Knower, the Seer, the True One over my head; (you) give the Guru's teaching; I rest my trust in you. No filth remains in the body of one whose mind is dyed (in your love); through the Guru's words, through the Shabad, he has recognised the True One. Your strength is (his support), and the glory of your Name (his honour); O Nanak, (he) dwells in devotion, in (the Lord's) refuge. ॥4॥
154.2: Raag Gauri, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). One who speaks of the Unspeakable and has others speak of him, who drinks the nectar (of the Name) and gives it to others to drink, forgets every other fear and is absorbed in the Name. Why should such a one fear? (All his) fear has merged in the fear (of God), (for he) has come to know (the Lord) through the Shabad of the Perfect Guru. The one in whose heart the Lord dwells, whose capital is the Lord (Hari), abiding in Sahaj and in love, receives (the Lord's) approval. Those whom (the Lord) keeps asleep (in Maya) evening and morning, those manmukhs are bound by death, here and hereafter. Those with the Lord in their hearts day and night are perfect; O Nanak, meeting the Lord, they are rid of their doubts. ॥4॥
154.3: Raag Gauri, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). One who loves (Maya of) the three qualities is born and dies (again and again); the four Vedas tell (only) of the visible form; they expound the three states; (but) the fourth state is (union with) the Lord: know him through the True Guru. Through devotion to the Lord and service of the Guru one swims across (the world-ocean); (then) there is no birth again, and no death. Everyone talks of the four great gifts; the Simritis, the Shastras and the pandits have the same on their lips; (but) without the Guru, (their true) meaning and understanding are not found; the gift of liberation is found through devotion to the Lord. The one in whose heart that Lord has come to dwell has received devotion through the Guru. In devotion to the Lord is the bliss of liberation; through the Guru's teaching one finds supreme bliss. Whoever has found (this bliss), the Guru, having seen (the Lord himself), has shown (him) to that one, and has taught him to stay free of hopes while living amid hopes. (That Lord) is the Master of the lowly, the Giver of every comfort; O Nanak, (that one's) mind stays dyed in (love of) the Lord's feet. ॥4॥
The three states (avastha): in the Vedanta's count, waking, dreaming and deep sleep (some read them as the mind's states under the three qualities); the fourth state is turiya (30.2).
154.4: Raag Gauri Cheti, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). The body, (thinking itself) immortal, lives at its ease; (but) this world is (only) a play. (O body,) you practise greed, avarice and much falsehood, and carry a great load (of sin). O body, I have seen you scattered like ashes over the ground. (O soul,) listen, listen to my counsel: only the good you have done will stay (with you), my soul; this turn will not come again. I tell you, O my body, listen to my counsel: you brood on slander of others and carry false tales; you cast your eyes on another's wife, O soul, and you steal and do evil. When the swan (the soul) departs, you (O body) will be left behind, like a deserted wife. O body, you have lived as if in a dream; what deeds have you done? When I stole and brought something home, it seemed good to (your) mind; (so) there is no honour here and no shelter hereafter; the precious (human) life is wasted. (The body says:) I have become most wretched, O brother; O Nanak, no one asks after me now. Horses of Arab and Turki breed, gold and silver, loads of fine clothes: (none of them) has gone along with anyone, O Nanak; they have dropped away (and stayed here), you fool. Rock sugar and dried fruits, I have tasted everything; your Name alone is Amrit. Laying foundation upon foundation, the walls are raised, (but those) mansions (become) a heap of ashes; (one) piles up hoards and gives nothing to anyone; the blind one thinks it is all his own. Lanka of gold, palaces of gold (did not last): wealth stays with no one. Listen, foolish and ignorant mind: his will alone shall prevail. Our Master is the great Banker, and we are his traders; soul and body, all of it, is his capital; he himself slays and he himself brings to life. ॥6॥
In this shabad the soul speaks, now to the body (kaaia), now to itself (jeearre); in the second Rahao the body speaks.
Lanka of gold: the city of Ravan in the Ramayana; its golden palaces did not stay his.
155.1: Raag Gauri Cheti, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). The others (the foes: lust, anger, greed, attachment and pride) are five, and I am one alone; how can I guard my house and home, O mind? Day after day they beat and rob (me); before whom can I cry out, O brother? O mind, utter the Name of Sri Ram (the Lord); ahead of you stands the army of Jam, vast and terrible. (God) built the hut (of the body) and set doors in it, and within it sits the soul-bride; (thinking herself) immortal, the bride revels every day in her pleasures, while those other five go on robbing (her). (Jam's army) pulled down the hut and plundered the temple, and the bride was seized, all alone; Jam's club (struck), the chain fell about her neck, and those five ran away. A wife craves gold and silver; friends crave things to eat; O Nanak, for their sake (a man) commits sins, and will go bound to the city of Jam. ॥4॥
155.2: Raag Gauri Cheti, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). (O yogi,) the (true) earrings are those within the heart; make the body itself your patched coat; bring the five disciples (the senses) under control, O Raval, and make this mind your staff. In this way you will find the way of Yoga: there is one Shabad, and no other; set your mind on that (as your food of) roots and tubers. If by shaving the head the Guru is found, we have made the Guru our Ganga; you do not remember the one Lord, the Saviour of the three worlds, O blind one. Making a show, you win (people's) minds with (mere) talk; your (own) doubt does not leave you at all. If you fix your consciousness on the feet of the One, why would you chase after greed and avarice? With your mind absorbed (in him), repeat (the Name of) the Niranjan; why, O yogi, do you speak so much deceit? The body is crazed and the swan (the soul) a child; life goes by in crying, mine, mine. Nanak humbly prays: when the naked (body) burns, then, afterwards, (the soul) repents. ॥4॥
Raval: a yogi of Gorakhnath's order. The yogi's garb is named here: the large earrings (mundra), the patched coat (khintha), the staff (danda), and roots and tubers (kand mool) for food.
The ਤਾ at the end of ਖਿੰਥਾਤਾ, ਪਾਵਸਿਤਾ and the rest only fills out the tune; it adds nothing to the sense.
156.1: Raag Gauri Cheti, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). O mind, the One alone is the root of all medicine and every mantra, if you make your consciousness firm (in him); take (the Name of) the One who cuts away the sinful deeds of birth after birth. O brother, the Master of the mind is the One alone; (while) your three qualities stay engrossed in the world, the Unseen cannot be perceived. Maya tastes sweet to the body, like sugar; we have taken up (its) bundle; the night is dark and nothing can be seen, and the mouse (of time) gnaws away at the rope (of life), O brother. As much as the manmukhs act (by their own will), so much pain befalls them; the Gurmukh receives honour. What he has done, that alone has come to be; the record of past deeds cannot be erased. Those who are dyed (in the Lord), having given (him) their love, are full to the brim and never run dry; if Nanak becomes the dust of their feet, then (this) fool too may gain something. ॥4॥
156.2: Raag Gauri Cheti, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Since when has (anyone) been our mother, since when our father? From what place have we come? We took shape in the fire (of the womb), from the water (of the seed): for what purpose were we made? O my Master, who knows your virtues? My faults are past telling. How many lives as trees and plants we have seen; how many times we were made beasts; how many times we came among the families of snakes; how many times we were made to fly as birds. (Man) breaks into the town's shops and its solid houses, and having stolen, comes home; he looks ahead and looks behind, (but) where can he hide from you, (O Lord)? We have seen river banks and tiraths, the nine regions (of the earth), shops, towns and bazaars; (at last) the trader took up the scales and began to weigh within his own heart. As full as the ocean is of water, so many are our faults. Show mercy, show some kindness: you have carried sinking stones across. The soul burns like fire; a knife (of craving) cuts within; Nanak humbly prays: (one who) recognises the Hukam has peace day and night. ॥6॥
156.3: Raag Gauri Bairagan, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). You have wasted the night in sleep and the day in eating; this life is (precious) as a diamond, yet it goes in exchange for a cowrie shell. You have not known the Name of the Lord; fool, you will repent afterwards. (Man) buries endless wealth in the earth, (but) the Endless One is not longed for; those who went off longing for endless (wealth) came back having lost the Endless One. If it came to whoever reached out and took it, everyone would be rich; it is settled by deeds, however much everyone may long (for it). O Nanak, the One who made the creation takes care of it; no one can tell the Master's Hukam, to whom he will give glory. ॥4॥
157.1: Raag Gauri Bairagan, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Were I a doe, I would live in the forest, picking roots and tubers to eat, and if by the Guru's grace my Husband (the Lord) met me, I would give myself up to him again and again. I am the Lord's trader; (O Lord,) your Name is my merchandise and my trade. Were I a koel (the Indian cuckoo), I would dwell in the mango tree and reflect on the Shabad in Sahaj; in Sahaj and in love my Husband would meet me, whose sight and form are beyond all measure. Were I a fish, I would live in the water (of the Lord), who takes care of all beings and creatures; my Husband dwells on this shore and on the far shore; I will meet him with my arms spread wide. Were I a she-snake, I would dwell in the earth; (if) the Shabad dwelt (within me), fear would go. O Nanak, they are ever happy soul-brides, whose light merges in the Light. ॥4॥
157.2: Raag Gauri Poorbi Deepaki, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. In the house where (God's) praise is spoken and the Creator is reflected upon, in that house sing the Sohila and remember the Creator. Sing the Sohila of my Fearless Lord. I am a sacrifice to the Sohila by which there is peace for ever. Day after day all beings are cared for; the Giver will watch over (each one). (O soul,) you cannot set a value on his giving; what measure can be taken of that Giver? The year and the day (of my wedding) have been written; gather, (friends,) and pour the oil (of the wedding rite). Give me your blessings, friends, so that I may be united with my Master. To every house this same summons comes; these calls go out every day. Let us remember the One who sends the call; O Nanak, those days are coming (for us too). ॥4॥
157.3: Raag Gauri Guareri, Chaupade, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. When the Guru is met, union with the Lord comes about; that (Lord) himself brings (one) into his union. My God himself knows every way; by his Hukam he unites (one), who then recognises (him) through the Shabad. In the fear of the True Guru, doubt and dread depart; one steeped in that fear merges in the love of the True One. When the Guru is met, the Lord comes to dwell in the mind, of his own loving nature. My God is great; his worth cannot be found. Whoever praises him through the Shabad, him who has no end and no near or far shore, my God, the Forgiver, forgives (that one). When the Guru is met, all wisdom and understanding come; that True One dwells in the mind made pure. When the True One dwells (within), all one's work is true; reflection on the Shabad is the noblest conduct. True service comes from the Guru; through the Guru, some rare one recognises the Naam. The Giver, who bestows all gifts, lives for ever; O Nanak, (by his gift) love for the Lord's Name takes hold. ॥4॥
158.1: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Some rare one receives spiritual wisdom from the Guru; the one who comes to understand from the Guru succeeds. From the Guru come Sahaj and reflection on the True One; from the Guru one finds the door of liberation. By perfect fortune the Guru comes and meets one, and one merges in true Sahaj, in the True One. When the Guru is met, one quenches the fire of craving; from the Guru, peace comes to dwell in the mind. From the Guru come purity, holiness and cleanness; from the Guru, union (with God) comes about through the Shabad. Without the Guru, all (the world) is led astray in doubt; without the Name, it suffers great pain. One who becomes Gurmukh meditates on the Naam; through the sight of the True One, true honour is gained. To whom else should one speak? That One alone is the Giver; when he shows grace, union comes about through the Shabad. Having met the Beloved (Guru), may I sing the True One's praises; may Nanak, becoming true, merge in the True One. ॥4॥
158.2: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). True is that place (the Sat Sangat), where the mind becomes pure; one makes one's dwelling in the True One, and becomes true. The true Bani is manifest through all four ages; the True One is himself everything, of his own self. When (God's) grace comes, he brings one into the Sat Sangat, and, seated in that place, one sings the Lord's praises. Let this tongue burn that is in the love of another, that does not taste the Lord's sweet essence and utters insipid words. Without understanding (that taste), body and mind become insipid; without the Name, the wretched one departs weeping. One whose tongue has tasted the Lord's sweet essence abides in Sahaj and in love; by the Guru's grace, that one merges in the True One. Dyed in the True One, (the tongue) makes the Guru's Shabad its reflection, and (that one) drinks the pure stream of Amrit. That which is a (fit) vessel merges in the Name; in a vessel turned upside down (the heart turned away from God) nothing stays. Through the Guru's Shabad the Name comes to dwell in the mind; O Nanak, that vessel is true which thirsts for the Shabad. ॥4॥
158.3: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Some keep on singing, but their mind finds no relish; they sing in Haumai, and it goes to waste. They truly sing the songs (of praise) who love the Name; (theirs is) the true Bani and reflection on the Shabad. One keeps on singing (his praise) if it pleases the True Guru; mind and body dyed in the Name, (one's life) becomes beautiful. Some sing, and some perform worship (with dance and show), but without love they do not obtain the Naam. True devotion lies in love for the Guru's Shabad; (such devotees) have kept their own Beloved ever enshrined in the heart. Fools perform worship and make a show of themselves; they dance and dance and leap about, and suffer much pain. By dancing and leaping, devotion is not done; the one who dies (to self) through the Shabad, that one obtains devotion. He, the Lover of devotion, himself causes devotion to be done; true devotion is to lose self-conceit from within. My true God knows every way (of all); O Nanak, the one he forgives recognises the Naam. ॥4॥
159.1: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). When one subdues the mind, its wandering dies away; without dying (to self), how can one find the Lord? Rare is the one who knows the medicine by which the mind dies; the mind dies through the Shabad: that one alone understands this. The one whom he forgives, he grants the glory that, by the Guru's grace, the Lord comes to dwell in the mind. When, through the Guru, one practises the conduct worth practising, then one comes to understand this mind. The mind is drunk, like an elephant maddened by wine; the Guru, striking it with the goad, brings it to life. The mind is hard to tame; some rare one tames it. When one consumes what will not yield (the mind's stubbornness), then (the mind) becomes pure. Through the Guru, one has set this mind in order, and casts Haumai and the vices out from within. Those whom he has, from the very beginning, kept joined in his union are never parted (from him); they stay merged in the Shabad. He himself alone knows his own power; O Nanak, through the Guru one recognises the Naam. ॥4॥
159.2: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). In Haumai the whole world has gone mad; in the love of another, it has strayed, lost in doubt. It frets with many anxious thoughts, but has not known its own self; busy with worldly affairs, its every day has slipped away. Remember the Lord (Ram) in your heart, O my brother; through the Guru, let your tongue savour the Lord's sweet essence. One who, through the Guru, has recognised the Lord in the heart, serving the Life of the world, is known through the four ages. Killing Haumai, one recognises (him) through the Guru's Shabad, when God, the Ordainer of destinies, shows his grace. True are those people whom he joins to the Guru's Shabad; he checks their running (mind) and holds it still. They obtain from the Guru the Naam, the nine treasures; through the Lord's grace, the Lord comes to abide in their minds. Repeating Ram, Ram, the body finds peace and calm; when he dwells within, the pain of Jam does not touch one. He himself is the Master, and he himself the minister; O Nanak, serve for ever the Lord, the deep ocean of virtues. ॥4॥
159.3: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Why should he be forgotten, to whom belong our soul and breath? Why should he be forgotten who pervades all, by serving whom one is honoured and accepted in the Lord's court? I give myself in sacrifice to the Lord's Name; if I forget you, that very moment I die. They forget you whom you yourself have led astray; they forget you who are in the love of another. The ignorant manmukhs are cast into births. Those with whom (the Lord) is wholly pleased, he sets to the True Guru's service; those with whom he is wholly pleased, in their minds the Lord makes (himself) dwell. Following the Guru's teaching, they merge in the Lord's Name. Those who have merit in their store reflect on divine wisdom; those who have merit in their store have killed Haumai. Nanak is a sacrifice to those who are dyed in the Name. ॥4॥
160.1: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). You are beyond telling; how can you be told? With the Guru's Shabad as the means that kills (the mind's ego), you come to dwell in the mind. Your virtues are countless; their worth cannot be found. The Bani (of praise) merges in the One to whom it belongs; your untold story the Guru's Shabad has proclaimed. Where the True Guru is, there the Sat Sangat is formed; where the True Guru is, the Lord's praises are sung in Sahaj; where the True Guru is, there the Shabad burns Haumai away. Through the Guru, by service one finds a place in (the Lord's) mansion; through the Guru, one enshrines the Lord's Name within; through the Guru, by devotion one merges in the Lord's Name. The Giver himself bestows the gift, (and that one's) love for the perfect True Guru takes hold. O Nanak, those dyed in the Name are hailed in glory. ॥4॥
160.2: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). From the One come all forms and colours; air, water and fire: all of them are joined together (in every being). The Lord God watches over (his creation of) many different colours. This is a wonder: he alone is the One (in all); rare is the one who, through the Guru, reflects on this. In Sahaj, God pervades every place; somewhere hidden, somewhere manifest: God has fashioned this design. He himself awakens those who sleep. His worth has never been found by anyone; everyone speaks and speaks, describing him. One who merges in the Guru's Shabad comes to understand that Lord. Hearing (all) again and again, he watches over them and joins (them) to the Shabad; great glory is gained through service of the Guru. O Nanak, those dyed in the Name merge in the Lord's Name. ॥4॥
160.3: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). The manmukh lies asleep in attachment to Maya, in love with her. The Gurmukh stays awake, dwelling on the knowledge of (God's) virtues. They alone are awake who are in love with the Naam. In Sahaj such a one stays awake and never falls asleep (in attachment), whoever comes to understand through the perfect Guru. The unsaintly one, set in his stubborn ways, never understands. He talks (of wisdom), yet stays entangled, struggling with Maya. The blind, ignorant one never succeeds. In this age, deliverance comes through the Name of Ram. Some rare one gains this understanding through the Guru's Shabad. He crosses over himself, and saves all his family lines as well. In this Kalyug no ritual or religious observance (avails). Kalyug is born in the house of the chandal. O Nanak, without the Name no one is liberated. ॥4॥
Kalyug here is a state of the mind more than an age: it is born in the heart of the chandal, the doer of evil.
161.1: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). True is (his) command; true is the King. Those whose minds are dyed in the True One, the Lord who needs no one, dwell in the True One's mansion and merge in the True Name. Listen, my mind: reflect on the Shabad. Repeat (the Name of) Ram, and cross over the ocean of the world. In doubt one comes, and in doubt one goes; this world is born in the love of another (than God). The manmukh does not remember (the Lord), and keeps coming and going. Has (this being) strayed of itself, or has God himself led it astray? This soul has been set to serve what is not its own; it earns great pain, and wastes its life in vain. When (God), in his grace, brings (one) to the True Guru, that one remembers the one Name, and does away with doubt from within. O Nanak, such a one repeats the Naam, and obtains the Name, which is (to him) the nine treasures. ॥4॥
161.2: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). I go and ask those who have meditated (on the Lord) through the Guru; by serving the Guru the mind is won over. They are the wealthy who earn the Lord's Name; this understanding is gained from the perfect Guru. O my brothers, repeat the Name of the Lord, Har Har. The labour of service done through the Guru, the Lord accepts. One who recognises his own self, his mind becomes pure; he is liberated while yet alive, and finds the Lord. One who sings the Lord's praises, his understanding becomes sublime, and with ease he merges in Sahaj. In the love of another, (the Lord) cannot be served; (such a one) eats the deadly poison of Haumai and Maya. Through son, family and home, Maya has bewitched (him); the blind manmukh keeps coming and going. The one to whom (the Lord) gives the Name of the Lord, Har Har, is (his) servant; through the Guru's Shabad his devotion goes on night and day. Through the Guru's teaching some rare one understands (this); O Nanak, that one merges in the Naam. ॥4॥
161.3: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Service of the Guru has held good in all four ages; some perfect person carries out this task. Inexhaustible is the wealth of the Lord's Name; there is never any shortage in it. (With it) there is lasting peace here, and glory at (the Lord's) door. O my mind, have no doubt (of this); by service through the Guru, drink the essence of Amrit. Those who serve the True Guru are the great beings of the world; they are saved themselves, and carry all their family lines across. They keep the Lord's Name enshrined in the heart; dyed in the Naam, they cross the terrifying world-ocean. Those who serve the True Guru are ever servants at heart; killing Haumai, (their heart-) lotus blossoms. The Anhad (Shabad) plays (within them), and they dwell in their own home; dyed in the Naam, they stay detached while living in the home. Those who serve the True Guru, their word is true (and lasting); in every age the devotees have uttered it and made it known. Night and day they repeat (the Name of) the Lord, Saringpani. O Nanak, dyed in the Naam, they become pure and free of desire. ॥4॥
162.1: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). (The one who) meets the True Guru by great fortune and by destiny's union has the Naam in (his) heart, and ever enjoys the Lord's sweet essence. The mortal who meditates on the Lord's Name through the Guru wins this human life, and gains the profit of the Naam. The Guru's Shabad is wisdom and meditation (to one who finds it) sweet; (but) by the Guru's grace some rare one alone has tasted (it) and seen. (People) carry out many rites and ceremonies and religious observances; without the Name, cursed, cursed is (such) pride. Tied in bonds, (the mortal is caught) in Maya's noose; O servant Nanak, he is set free (only) by the light the Guru gives. ॥4॥
162.2: Raag Gauri Bairagan, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). As the cloud rains down upon the earth, is there not water within the earth (as well)? Just as water comes forth within the earth, (so the same water) the footless (clouds) go about raining. O brother, in this way dispel (your) doubt: as (the Lord) makes anyone, so that one becomes, and that is the way beings go and are absorbed. Born woman or man, what deeds can they do (of themselves)? (O Lord,) the many forms are ever yours, and they merge in you alone. Through so many births (beings) lay astray; when (you) were found, they strayed no more. He whose work (the world) is, he alone knows it well; (this is seen) if (beings) merge in the Guru's Shabad. (O Lord,) yours is the Shabad, your command; you alone are (all) yourself; where then is doubt? O Nanak, (those whose) essence has merged with the Essence do not come into birth again and again. ॥4॥
The image: the water hidden in the earth and the water the clouds rain down are one water; so all forms are the one Lord's.
162.3: Raag Gauri Bairagan, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). The whole world is in the power of death, bound by the love of another. Doing their deeds in Haumai, the manmukhs receive punishment. O my mind, fix your attention on the Guru's feet. Through the Guru take the treasure of the Naam; it will set (you) free in the Lord's court. (Beings) wander through the eighty-four lakh (forms of life); by the mind's stubbornness one comes and goes. (One who) has not recognised the Guru's Shabad falls into wombs again and again. One who has recognised his own self through the Guru, the Lord's Name has come to dwell in his mind. Dyed in devotion night and day, he stays merged in peace in the Lord's Name. When the mind dies through the Shabad, faith takes root, and one gives up Haumai and the vices. O servant Nanak, the treasures of the Lord's Name and of devotion are obtained only by (his) grace. ॥4॥
162.4: Raag Gauri Bairagan, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). In the parents' home (this world) the stay is four days; so the Lord, Har Har, has written it. Honoured is the (soul-) bride who has sung (his) praises through the Guru. (She who) gathers virtues in her parents' home finds a dwelling in her in-laws' home (the world hereafter). Through the Guru she stays merged in Sahaj, and the Lord, Har Har, is dear to her mind. The Husband dwells in the in-laws' home and in the parents' home; say, by what means is he found? He himself is stainless and beyond knowing; he himself unites (one with himself). You, God, yourself give the understanding, (and then) the Lord's Name is meditated on. By great fortune the True Guru is met, and Amrit is put into the mouth. Haumai and duality perish, and with ease one merges in peace. He himself, himself alone, pervades all; he himself attaches (one) to the Name. The manmukhs, in their pride, have not found (him); they are ignorant and childish. They do not serve the True Guru, and they repent again and again. They are given a dwelling in womb after womb, and in the womb itself they rot away. So it pleases my Creator: the manmukhs go wandering astray. The one on whose forehead my Lord God had the perfect writ written from the beginning has meditated on the Name of the Lord, Har Har, on meeting the Guru, the hero. The Lord's Name is my father and my mother; the Lord is my kinsman and brother. O Lord, Har Har, O God, forgive (me) and unite (me with you); servant Nanak is (your lowly) worm. ॥4॥
163.1: Raag Gauri Bairagan, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). When wisdom was obtained from the True Guru and the Lord, the essence (of all), was reflected on, the soiled understanding grew bright, repeating the Name of Murari. Shiv (the Lord, the source of good) has wiped out Shakti (Maya), and the darkness has ended. Those on whose foreheads (this) was written from the beginning hold the Lord's Name dear. O Sants, by what means is the Lord found, seeing whom I live? Without the Lord I cannot live for a moment; bring me to the Guru, so that I may drink the Lord's sweet essence. I sing the Lord's praises and ever hear (of) the Lord; the Lord, Har Har, has raised me to the highest state. From the Guru I have obtained the Lord's sweet essence; my mind and body are absorbed (in it). Blessed, blessed is the Guru, the true Being; he has given (me) devotion to the Lord. The Guru from whom I have found the Lord, that Guru I have made my own. The Lord King is the giver of virtues; we are full of faults. Sinners sinking like stones the Lord carries across through the Guru's teaching. You are the pure giver of virtues; we are full of faults. O Lord, (we have come) to your refuge: save (us); you have carried even fools and dullards across. Through the Guru's teaching there is ever Sahaj and bliss, when the Lord, Har Har, is meditated on in the mind. When the Lord God, the Friend, is found, songs of joy are sung in the home (of the heart). O Lord, O God, show mercy; (this is my) prayer: make me remember (your Name), Har Har. Those who have found the True Guru: servant Nanak begs for the dust (of their feet). ॥4॥
163.2: Raag Gauri Guareri, Chaupade, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. The pandit reads the Shastras and the Simritis; the yogi calls out, Gorakh, Gorakh; I, a fool, have learned only to repeat (the Name of) the Lord, Har Har. O Ram, I do not know what my state will be. O my mind, worship the Lord and cross the terrifying world-ocean; (the Lord's Name) is the boat. The sannyasi smears ashes and so adorns his body; he gives up other men's women and lives as a celibate; O Lord, I, a fool, have hope in you alone. The Khatri does deeds (of valour) and wins renown for bravery; the Shudra labours in the service of others, and the Vaish at (his) trade; me, a fool, the Lord's Name (alone) sets free. (O Lord,) all creation is yours; you yourself pervade it. O Nanak, (the Lord) bestows glory through the Guru. I, the blind one, have made the Lord my support. ॥4॥
Gorakh (Gorakhnath): the teacher revered by the Nath yogis.
Brahmin, Khatri (Kshatriya), Vaish and Shudra are the four varnas: by the Shastras the Khatri's duty is war, the Vaish's trade and farming, and the Shudra's the service of the other three.
164.1: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). The Lord's story (the telling of his praise) is a story beyond the three qualities (of Maya). Join the company of the holy, (the Lord's) servants, and worship him; hear the story of the Lord, which no words can tell, and cross the fearful world-ocean. O Gobind, unite (me) with the Sat Sangat, so that (my) tongue may taste the Lord's sweet essence and sing the praises of Ram. Those who meditate upon the Name of the Lord, Har Har: make me, O Ram, a servant of their servants. To serve (your) servant is the highest work. The one who tells (me) the story of the Lord, Har: that person is dear to my mind and my heart. Only one of great good fortune obtains the dust of the feet of (the Lord's) servant. Love for the Sants takes firm root in those who have received the writ (of grace) written for them from the beginning; such people, O Nanak, merge in the Naam. ॥4॥
164.2: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). The mother delights when her son eats; the fish delights in bathing in the water; (so) the True Guru delights in putting (food) into a Gursikh's mouth. O Lord, unite me with those beloved servants of the Lord by meeting whom my sorrows leave me. As the cow, meeting her calf, brims over with love, (as) the wife delights when her husband comes home, (so) the Lord's servant delights when he sings the Lord's praise. The chatrik delights when the rain pours down in streams; the king delights in seeing the spread of his wealth; (so) the Lord's servant delights in repeating (the Name of) the Formless One. Mortal man delights in earning riches and wealth; the Gursikh delights when the Guru meets him with an embrace; servant Nanak's delight is to kiss the feet of the holy. ॥4॥
Preet in this hymn and the next is the delight love takes in what it loves (Sanskrit priti: pleasure, joy, affection).
164.3: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). The beggar delights on receiving alms from a master (of plenty); the hungry man delights in eating food; (so) the Gursikh's delight is to meet the Guru and be filled. O Lord, grant (me) the sight of you; O Lord, my hope is in you. Show mercy and fulfil my longing. The chakvi delights when the sun comes before her eyes; (then) she meets her beloved and leaves all her pain behind; (so) the Gursikh delights when the Guru comes before his eyes. The calf delights in taking milk into its mouth; seeing its mother, it blossoms in its heart; (so) the Gursikh delights when the Guru draws him face to face (and favours him). All other love is attachment to Maya, and it does not last; it perishes; it is false, a show like the glitter of glass. For servant Nanak, the True Guru is delight and contentment. ॥4॥
165.1: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Service of the True Guru has proved fruitful, for through it, meeting (the Guru), one meditates on the Name of the Lord, the Master. Following those who have repeated (the Name of) the Lord, a great many are set free. O Gursikhs, my brothers, utter (the Name of) the Lord; as (the Name of) the Lord is uttered, every sin is washed off. When the Guru was met, the mind came under control; the five (senses), running wild, came to rest, and the Lord was meditated on; day after day, in the town (of the body), the Lord's praises were sung. Those who have put the dust of the True Guru's feet on their foreheads have given up falsehood and fixed their attention on the Lord. In the Lord's court their faces are bright, O brother. Service of the Guru pleases the Lord himself; Krishna and Balbhadra (too) meditated (on him), falling at the Guru's feet. O Nanak, through the Guru the Lord himself carries (them) across. ॥4॥
Balbhadra (Balram) was Krishna's elder brother; by the Puranas both studied under the sage Sandipani and served him as their guru.
165.2: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). The Lord himself is the yogi who bears the staff; the Lord, Banwari, himself pervades (all); the Lord himself sits in deep trance and practises austerity. Such is my Ram: he fills (every place); he dwells close by; the Lord is not far. The Lord himself is the Shabad; he himself is the attention and its absorption; the Lord himself watches, and himself rejoices; the Lord himself has (others) repeat (his Name), and the Lord himself repeats it. The Lord himself is the chatrik, and (himself) the stream of nectar; the Lord is the nectar, and himself the one who gives it to drink; the Lord himself creates, and himself brings (all) safely across. The Lord himself is boat and raft, and he who ferries (us) over; the Lord himself, through the Guru's teaching, brings (us) across; O Nanak, the Lord himself takes (us) to the far shore. ॥4॥
165.3: Raag Gauri Bairagan, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). O Master, you are our Banker; such capital as you give, that we take. With love we would trade in the Lord's Name, should you yourself, being merciful, give (that capital). We are Ram's traders; the Lord gives (us) capital and has (us) trade, O brother. (The one who) has earned this profit, the wealth of the Lord's devotion, has pleased the mind of the Lord, the true Banker. (The one who), repeating the Lord's Name, has loaded the Lord's merchandise: Jam, the toll-collector, has not come near him. The traders who deal in other trade (suffer) pain in the endless waves of Maya; to whatever trade the Lord has set them, such is the fruit they have received. That person alone trades in (the Name of) the Lord, Har Har, to whom God, in his kindness, gives (it). O servant Nanak, (the one who) has served the Lord, the Banker, is never again called (by him) to account. ॥4॥
165.4: Raag Gauri Bairagan, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). As a mother nurses (the child in) her womb, hoping for a son, (thinking) he will grow up and earn money and give it, so that (we) may enjoy comfort and pleasure, so the Lord keeps his servant's love alive, himself giving (him) the support of his hand. O my Ram, O Lord, O my Master, protect me, a fool. Your servant's praise is your own glory. There is bliss in the temple, in the home (of the heart), when the praise of the Lord, Har Har, pleases the mind; all sweet flavours fill (his) mouth when he sings the Lord's praises; the Lord's servant is guardian and support to twenty-one generations; he sets the whole world free. Whatever has been done, the Lord has done; (all) is the Lord's glory. O Lord, the beings are yours, and you are at work (in them); the Lord (himself) has (his) worship done. The Lord lets (us) find the treasures of devotion, and himself hands them out. What cleverness can a slave bought in the market (show)? If (the Lord) seats him on a throne, he is (still) the Lord's slave; even the grass-cutter the Lord makes to utter the Lord's Name. Servant Nanak is the Lord's slave; (this is) the Lord's glory. ॥4॥
Twenty-one generations (ikih kul): an old way of saying a person's whole line, the generations before and after.
166.1: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). The farmer tills the land and longs (for the crop) with all his heart; he yokes the plough and toils, (thinking,) my son and daughter will eat; so the Lord's servant repeats (the Name of) the Lord, Har Har, and at the end the Lord sets him free. Raise me, a fool, to the highest state, O my Ram; O Lord, set me to the work of serving the Guru, the True Guru. Taking horses, the merchant hurries off to trade; he earns wealth, hopes (for more), and increases his attachment to Maya; so the Lord's servant utters (the Name of) the Lord, Har Har, and uttering the Lord finds peace. The shopkeeper sits in his shop and plies his trade, hoarding poison; the attachment is false, the display is of falsehood, and he clings to the false; so the Lord's servant has gathered the wealth of the Lord, and takes (the Name of) the Lord with him as provisions for the journey. This family is attachment to Maya, a noose in the love of another; through the Guru's teaching that person crosses over who is the servant of (the Lord's) servants. Servant Nanak has meditated on the Naam; through the Guru, the light has dawned (within). ॥4॥
166.2: Raag Gauri Bairagan, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Always, day and night, (man) is greedy, and wanders, led astray (by Maya); (like) the man pressed into forced labour, who goes about at his unpaid toil with a load lifted on his head. The one who serves the Guru the Lord has set to the work of (his own true) home. O my Ram, break the bonds of Maya and set (us) to the work of (our true) home, that we may ever sing the Lord's praises, merged in the Lord's Name. A man serves a king, the lord of men, all for the sake of wealth; (the king) either puts him in chains, or exacts a fine, or the king (himself) dies. Blessed, blessed is the True Guru's service, and fruitful, for through it, repeating the Name of the Lord, Har Har, one has found the Lord's peace. Every day, in many ways, trade is done for profit, for the sake of Maya; when it yields a profit, there is joy in the mind; at a loss one dies (of grief). The one who goes into partnership with the Guru in virtues finds peace for ever and ever. However great the hunger for other pleasures and tastes, just so great a hunger strikes again. The one on whom the Lord himself shows grace sells his head to the Guru. O servant Nanak, (the one who is) filled with the Lord's sweet essence feels no hunger again. ॥4॥
167.1: Raag Gauri Bairagan, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). In my mind and heart, O Lord, is ever this hope: how may I see the sight of you, O Lord? He who kindled this love knows it: to my mind and heart the Lord is very dear. I am a sacrifice to my Guru, who has united me, the one cut off, with my Creator. O my Ram, I, a sinner, have sought (your) refuge, (fallen) at your door, O Lord, in the hope that, bestowing your grace, you may some day unite me, without virtue, (with yourself). My faults are many, very many; (committed) again and again, O Lord, they are beyond counting. You, O Lord, Har Har, are full of virtue and merciful; you yourself forgive, O Lord, when it pleases you. Me, a wrongdoer, (the Lord) has kept safe in the Guru's company; he has given the teaching, and the Lord's Name sets free. What virtues of yours can I tell, O my True Guru? When I utter (the word) Guru, I am lost in wonder. Would anyone else protect wrongdoers like me, as the True Guru has protected and freed me? You, the Guru, are my father; you, the Guru, alone are my mother; you, the Guru, are my kinsman, my friend and helper. The state I was in, O my True Guru, that state, O Lord, you yourself know. I wandered about, cast aside, and no one asked after me; through the company of the Guru, the True Guru, this worm has been raised to honour. Blessed, blessed is the Guru of servant Nanak, meeting whom all sorrows and torments have ended. ॥4॥
Mat here means perhaps, in the hope that; it is not mat(i), the intellect.
167.2: Raag Gauri Bairagan, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). My soul is lured by gold and woman; attachment to Maya is sweet (to me). In houses, mansions and horses (I take) delight; my mind is fixed on other pleasures. The Lord God does not come to (my) mind; how can I be set free, O my Lord King? O my Ram, such are my lowly deeds, O my Lord. O Lord, Har Har, full of virtue and merciful, show grace and forgive all my faults. I have no beauty, no caste, no good ways. With what face shall I speak? I am without virtue, and I have not repeated your Name. I, a sinner, have been saved in the Guru's company; (this is) the True Guru's goodness. (God) has given all: soul and body, mouth and nose, and water to use; he has given grain for food and cloth for wear, and countless pleasures to enjoy; the one who gave them does not come to mind; I, a beast, take it all to be my own doing. All that happens is your doing; you know the inner heart (of all). What can we poor creatures do? All is your play, O Master. Servant Nanak, bought in the market, is a slave of the Lord's slaves. ॥4॥
168.1: Raag Gauri Bairagan, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). As a mother gives birth to a son, then rears him and keeps him within her sight; indoors and out, she feeds him by the mouthful and fondles him every moment: so the True Guru keeps the Guru's Sikh in the Lord's love, with affection. O my Lord, we are children of the Lord God, and know nothing. Blessed, blessed is the Guru, the True Guru, the teacher, who gave us the Lord's teaching and made us wise. As the (crane) clad in white feathers wheels and flies about in the sky, yet keeps her mind on the young she has left behind, and always holds them close in her heart: so the True Guru gives his Sikh the love of the Lord, Har Har, and the Guru holds the Sikh as dear as his own life. As there are the shears of the thirty-two teeth, and within them (the Lord) keeps the tongue of flesh and blood (safe): one may think it lies in the hands of the flesh or of the shears, but all is in the Lord's power. So, though people slander the Sants, the Lord keeps the honour of his servant. O brother, let none of you think that anything lies in anyone's hands; all is what (the Lord) does and causes to be done. Old age, death, fever, headache and curse: all are in the Lord's power; nothing can strike unless the Lord makes it strike. Meditate always, in mind and in consciousness, on such a Name of the Lord, O servant Nanak, which sets one free at the very last moment. ॥4॥
168.2: Raag Gauri Bairagan, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). He whose meeting brings bliss to the mind is the one to be called the True Guru: the mind's double-mindedness is destroyed, and the Lord, the supreme state, is attained. How may I meet my beloved True Guru? Every moment I bow (to him): how may I meet my Perfect Guru? In his grace the Lord has united me with my Perfect True Guru. The longings of (his) servant are fulfilled, taking the dust (of the feet) of the True Guru. One should meet that True Guru who makes devotion to the Lord firm (within), and with whom one hears of devotion to the Lord. (With him) no loss ever comes; the Lord's profit is made firm every day. (The Guru) in whose heart there is blossoming, and no love of another: O Nanak, meeting that Guru one is saved, and (such people) sing the Lord's praises. ॥4॥
168.3: Raag Gauri Poorbi, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). The merciful Lord God has shown mercy: the Lord's word (of praise) is in my mind, my body and my mouth. Through the Guru, the colour has become very deep; the bodice (of my heart) is soaked in the Lord's colour. I am the handmaid of my Lord God. When my mind came to accept the Lord, he made the whole world my servant, unbought. Reflect and discern, O Sants, O brothers: search your hearts, look, and seek. All is the form of the Lord, Har Har; (his) light is in all creation; the Lord dwells near, the Lord is close by. The Lord, Har Har, dwells near the whole world, the infinite, immeasurable Being. The Perfect Guru has made the Lord, Har Har, manifest (within me); for a price, I have sold the Guru my head. O dear Lord, you are within and without; I have come to your refuge; you are the great Being, the greatest of all. Servant Nanak sings the Lord's praises night and day, having met the True Guru, the Guru, the go-between. ॥4॥
The go-between (vichola) arranges a marriage and brings the bride to the bridegroom; the Guru unites the soul-bride with the Lord.
169.1: Raag Gauri Poorbi, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). O Life of the world, boundless Master, Lord of the universe, all-pervading Being, Creator: on whatever path you prompt us, Master, on that path we go. O Lord, my mind is steeped in the Lord. Joining the Sat Sangat, we have found the Lord's sweet essence, and we stay merged in the Name of the Lord. The Name of the Lord, Har Har, is the one medicine in the world; the Name of the Lord, Har Har, brings peace. All the sins and faults of those are destroyed who, through the Guru's teaching, savour the Lord's sweet essence. Those on whose foreheads the writ was written from the beginning bathe in the Guru, the pool of contentment. All the filth of evil-mindedness is gone from those who are dyed in the colour of the Lord's Name. O Lord, you yourself, you alone, are God and Master; no other giver is as great as you. Servant Nanak lives when he takes the Naam; the Lord is meditated on by the Lord's grace. ॥4॥
169.2: Raag Gauri Poorbi, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Show grace, O Life of the world, O Giver, that my mind may stay absorbed in the Lord. The True Guru has given me (his) most pure word; repeating Har Har Har, my mind rejoices. O Lord, the True Lord has pierced my mind and body (with his love). Death, in whose mouth the whole world is seized: through the word of the Guru, the True Guru, O Lord, we have been saved (from it). Those who have no love for the Lord are Saakats, foolish and frail men. For them birth and death are a very heavy load; dying again and again, they rot in filth. You are merciful, the protector of those who come to your refuge: give me this gift, Lord; I beg it of you. Make me a slave of the Lord's slaves, and let my mind dance and dance (in delight). God, the Master, is himself the great banker; we are his traders. My mind, body and soul, all this capital, are yours, O God, the true banker of servant Nanak. ॥4॥
169.3: Raag Gauri Poorbi, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). You are merciful, the destroyer of all pain: hear one prayer of mine, and give it your ear. Unite me with that True Guru, my very life, through whom you, Lord and Master, are known. O Lord, I have taken the True Guru to be the Supreme Lord. I was foolish, ignorant, of impure mind; through the word of the Guru, the True Guru, I have come to know the Lord. Of all the tastes and other delights I have tried, every one is insipid, utterly insipid. Meeting the True Guru, I have tasted the Lord's Name, the nectar; it is sweet as sugarcane juice. Those whom the Guru, the True Guru, has not met are Saakats, foolish and crazed. A lot without grace was set for them from the beginning; like (moths) seeing the lamp, they burn in attachment. Those whom you, in your mercy, unite (with the Guru) are set to the service of the Lord, Har Har. O servant Nanak, repeating Har Har Har they shine forth; taking the Guru's teaching as their understanding, they merge in the Naam. ॥4॥
170.1: Raag Gauri Poorbi, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). O my mind, that God, the Master, is always with you; say, where can one run from the Lord? The Lord, the True God, himself forgives; when the Lord himself sets free, one is set free. O my mind, repeat Har Har Har; let him be repeated within the mind. O my mind, hurry to the True Guru's refuge; one is set free by following the Guru, the True Guru. O my mind, serve that God, the giver of all peace, by serving whom one dwells in one's own home (within). Through the Guru, go and find your own home; let the Lord's praise be rubbed, as sandalwood is rubbed. O my mind, the praise of the Lord, Har Har Har Har Har, is sublime; earning the Lord's profit, one rejoices in the mind. When the Lord, Har Har, himself in mercy gives (it), then the nectar, the Lord's essence, is tasted. O my mind, those who, without the Naam, are attached to another are Saakats, and are throttled by Jam. Those Saakats who have forgotten the Naam are thieves; O mind, do not go near them or touch them. O my mind, serve the unseen, stainless Lord, Narhari, by serving whom the account is cleared. O servant Nanak, those whom the Lord God has made complete do not fall short by a masa's weight, not for an instant. ॥5॥
170.2: Raag Gauri Poorbi, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). God, my very breath is in your hands; my soul and body, all of it, is yours. Be kind, Lord, and grant me the sight of you; my mind and body yearn for it deeply. O Lord, my mind and body yearn to meet the Lord. When the merciful Guru showed a little grace, my Lord God came and met me. Master, whatever passes in my mind and heart, that state of mine, Lord, is known to you yourself. May I repeat the Naam night and day and find peace; I live ever in hope of you, Lord. The Guru, the True Guru, the Giver, pointed out the path; my Lord God came and met me. Bliss abides night and day, by great good fortune; every hope of (his) servant has been fulfilled. O Master of the world, Ruler of the universe, Creator: all is in the Lord's power. Servant Nanak has come to your refuge: O Lord, guard your servant's honour. ॥4॥
170.3: Raag Gauri Poorbi, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). This mind, chasing many pleasures, does not stay still even for a moment; it runs and runs in all ten directions, wandering. By great good fortune I have found the Perfect Guru; he gave me the Lord's mantra, and the mind has come to rest. O Lord, I am called the True Guru's slave. On my forehead (his) mark has been branded; I have run up a great debt to the Guru. He has done me great kindness and good; he has carried me across the world-ocean, so hard to cross. Those in whose hearts there is no love for the Lord only tie knots that are false. As paper falls apart in water, so the manmukhs waste away in the womb (of birth after birth). We have known nothing, nor do we know what lies ahead; as the Lord keeps us, so we stand. O Guru, we err and fall short: show us your grace; servant Nanak is called your dog. ॥4॥
171.1: Raag Gauri Poorbi, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). The city (of the body) is filled to the brim with lust and anger; meeting the Saadh (the Guru), these are smashed to pieces. By the writ of the past the Guru has been found, and loving absorption (liv) in the Lord is set like a jewel in the mind. Join your palms before the Saadh: this is a great merit. Lie stretched out before him in prostration: this is a great merit. The Saakats (those who have turned from God) have not known the taste of the Lord's sweet essence; within them is the thorn of Haumai (ego). The further they walk, the more it pricks and they suffer pain, and they bear the rod of Jamkaal (death) upon their heads. The Lord's servants remain merged in the Name of the Lord, Har Har; they have cut away the pain of birth and death in the world. They have found the imperishable, all-pervading Supreme God, and great is their glory across the lands and universes. We are poor and meek, God, and we are yours; save us, O Lord, save us: you are the greatest of the great. Servant Nanak's support and prop is the Naam; in the Lord's Name alone has peace been found. ॥4॥
171.2: Raag Gauri Poorbi, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Within this fortress (of the body) is the Lord, the Sovereign Ram; but the stubborn one finds no taste (of him). When the Lord, merciful to the meek, showed his favour, the Lord was tasted and seen through the Guru's Shabad. O Lord, the Kirtan of the Lord, with attention fixed on the Guru, is sweet. The Lord is beyond reach, beyond the senses, the Supreme Lord; (he is found) by meeting the True Guru and holding to (him), the intermediary. Those to whose hearts the Guru's words are pleasing: before them (the Lord) is brought and served. The manmukh's heart is very hard; within them is blackness, pitch black. Give a snake ever so much milk to drink: search it and turn it over, and poison comes out. O Lord God, bring and unite me with the Guru, the Saadh, that I may grind the Shabad as the Garur (antidote) and take it into my mouth. Servant Nanak is the Guru's bondsman and servant; joined to the Sangat, what was bitter has turned sweet. ॥4॥
Garur: a remedy against snake venom, named after Garuda, the bird who is the enemy of snakes; it was ground on a stone and taken by mouth.
171.3: Raag Gauri Poorbi, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). I have sold my body before the Perfect Guru, for the sake of the Lord, Har Har. The True Guru, the Giver, has made the Naam firm within me; on my face and forehead good fortune has dawned. O Lord, through the Guru's teaching, attention is fixed on the Lord. The beautiful Lord, the Sovereign Ram, pervades every heart; through the Guru's Shabad, through the Guru, attention is fixed (on him). I would cut up my mind and body and give them to the Guru; by the Guru's words my doubt and fear are put to flight. Into the darkness (the Guru) has brought and lit lamps; through the Guru's wisdom, through the Guru, attention is fixed (on him). The darkness of ignorance is utterly destroyed; the treasure is found in the home (within), and the mind is awake. The Saakats are hunters, clinging to Maya; Jam keeps them in his sight. They have not sold their heads before the True Guru; those wretched ones come and go. Hear my prayer, God, my Master: I beg for the refuge of God, the Lord. The Guru is servant Nanak's honour and standing; he has sold his head before the True Guru. ॥5॥
172.1: Raag Gauri Poorbi, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). We were proud, our minds full of pride and ignorance; meeting the Guru, self-conceit has been lost. The disease of Haumai is gone, and peace is found; blessed, blessed is the Guru, the Lord and King. O Lord, through the Guru's word the Lord is found. In my heart is love for the Sovereign Lord; the Guru has shown me the road, the path. My soul and body, all, (I have placed) before the True Guru, who has brought me, separated as I was, into the Lord's embrace. Within me arose the love to see (him); the Guru has shown (him) to me, right there with my heart. The bliss of Sahaj has arisen in my mind; I have sold myself before the Guru. I committed many offences and sins; doing wicked deeds, I stole like a thief. Now Nanak has come to your refuge: O Lord, keep his honour, as it pleases you, Lord. ॥4॥
172.2: Raag Gauri Poorbi, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Through the Guru's teaching the unstruck Shabad resounds; through the Guru's teaching the mind sings (his praise). By great good fortune I have had the sight of the Guru; blessed, blessed is the Guru, who fixes (our) attention (on the Lord). Through the Guru, one fixes loving attention on the Lord. My Master is the Perfect True Guru; my mind does the Guru's work. I wash the feet of the Guru, rubbing them again and again, who tells (me) the story of the Lord, Har Har. In the heart, through the Guru's teaching, is the Lord, the home of all delights; the tongue sings the Lord's praises. Relishing and relishing, the mind is sated with the Lord's essence, and hunger never strikes again. One may try countless ways, very many, but without (his) grace the Naam is not found. On servant Nanak the Lord has shown grace; through the Guru's teaching he makes the Naam firm in (his) understanding. ॥4॥
172.3: Raag Gauri Majh, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). O dear soul, through the Guru meditate on the Name: this is the deed (for you to do). Make the (Guru's) wisdom your mother, make that wisdom your life, and keep the Name of Ram on your lips. Make contentment your father, and the Purakh who is never born your Guru. O fortunate one, (so) meet Ram. I have met the Guru, the Yogi (joined to God), the Purakh, and I delight in his love. The Guru is steeped in the Lord's love, ever free of all desire. O fortunate one, meet him, (the Guru,) skilled and all-wise. My mind and body are drenched in the Lord's love. Come, O Sants, let us gather and meditate on the Name; in the Sangat, ever reap the profit of the Name. Serving the Sants, let us put the Amrit (of the Name) into our mouths. Meet (the Lord), by the grace written for you from his court of old. In Sawan the cloud has spread over the world with its Amrit (of rain); the peacock of the mind calls out sweetly, having taken the (Guru's) Shabad into its mouth. The Lord's Amrit has rained down within, the Lord, the King, has been met, and (the mind of) servant Nanak is dyed in love. ॥4॥
Sawan (mid-July to mid-August) is the month of the monsoon rains, when the peacock cries out with joy at the sight of the clouds.
173.1: Raag Gauri Majh, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Come, my companion, let us make virtues our charms (to win the Husband Lord), and, joining the Sants, enjoy the love and delight (of his union). (Those in whose) minds the lamp of the Guru's wisdom ever burns, have met him, melting (with love), since the Lord was pleased. Love for the Lord, my darling, has taken hold of my mind and body. May the True Guru, the go-between, unite me with my Friend. I would give my mind to the Sants, (that they) may unite me with my God. To the Lord I am ever a sacrifice. Dwell, my beloved; dwell, O my Govind; O Lord, show your grace and dwell in my mind. I have received the fruit my mind longed for, O my Govind; seeing the perfect Guru, (my mind) has blossomed. The happy wife has received the Lord's Name, O my Govind; in her mind are bliss and gladness day and night. The fortunate ones have found the Lord, O my Govind; ever reaping the profit (of the Name), their minds laugh with joy. The Lord himself creates (beings), the Lord himself watches over (them), the Lord himself has set (them) to their tasks. Some eat of his gifts, which never run short; to some (he) has given but a pinch. Some sit on thrones as kings, ever at ease; some (he) has made to beg for alms. Everywhere (your) one Word, (your Hukam,) is at work, O my Govind; servant Nanak has meditated on the Name. ॥4॥
Kaaman: the charms a woman was believed to use to win her husband's love; here the virtues are those charms.
173.2: Raag Gauri Majh, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Within my mind, within my mind, O my Govind, within my mind I am dyed in the Lord's love. The Lord's love is with (each one), yet it is not perceived, O my Govind; the perfect Guru makes the unseen (Lord) seen. (In whom) the Name of the Lord, Har Har, has shone forth, O my Govind, all (their) poverty and pain are gone. (Those who) have attained the supreme state of the Lord, O my Govind, the fortunate ones, remain absorbed in the Name. With the eyes, my beloved, with the eyes, O my Govind, only some rare one has seen the Lord God with the eyes. My mind and body are deeply sad (in longing), O my Govind; without the Lord, (I,) the bride, have withered. Meeting the Sants, I have found (him), O my Govind, my Lord God, my friend and companion. The Lord, the Life of the world, came and met (me), O my Govind; now (my) night (of life) goes by in peace. O Sants, unite me with my Lord God, my friend; a hunger (for him) has seized my mind and body. I cannot live without seeing (you), my Beloved; the Lord has set the pain of separation within me. The Lord, the King, is my dear friend; (when) the Guru unites (me with him), my mind comes alive. The hope of my mind and body is fulfilled, O my Govind; meeting the Lord, my mind is full of rejoicing. A sacrifice, O my Govind, a sacrifice, my beloved: I am ever a sacrifice to you. In my mind and body is love for the Beloved, O my Govind; O Lord, keep this capital of mine safe. Unite me with the True Guru, the go-between, O my Govind, who will guide me and unite me with the Lord. By (your) kindness I have received the Lord's Name, O my Govind; servant Nanak is in your refuge. ॥4॥
174.1: Raag Gauri Majh, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Maker of wondrous plays, O my Govind; maker of wondrous plays, my beloved: my Lord God works wondrous plays. The Lord himself brings Kanh into being, O my Govind; the Lord himself is the gopi who searches (for him). The Lord himself enjoys (the world through) every body, O my Govind; he himself is the one who relishes and the one who enjoys. The all-wise Lord does not go astray, O my Govind; he himself is the True Guru, the Yogi (untouched by pleasures). (The Lord) himself creates the world, O my Govind; the Lord himself plays in many colours. Some (he) gives pleasures to enjoy, O my Govind; some go about naked, utterly bare. (The Lord) himself creates the world, O my Govind; all beg of him, and the Lord gives his gifts. The Name is the support of the devotees, O my Govind; they ask the Lord (only) for the Lord's sublime story. The Lord himself (moves his devotees to) worship him, O my Govind; the Lord fulfils the longing in his devotees' minds. (The Lord) himself is at work in the water and on the land, O my Govind; he pervades (all), and is not far. Within and without is the Lord himself, O my Govind; the Lord himself fills (every place). The Lord, the all-pervading Ram, has spread out (this world), O my Govind; the Lord himself watches over it, ever present. Within (all), the Lord, as the breath, is the instrument, O my Govind; as the Lord himself plays it, so it sounds. Within (all) is the treasure of the Lord's Name, O my Govind; through the Guru's Shabad the Lord God resounds (within). (The Lord) himself brings (beings) to his refuge, O my Govind; the Lord is the guardian of his devotees' honour. O fortunate one, join the Sangat, O my Govind; O servant Nanak, through the Name (life's) task is accomplished. ॥4॥
175.1: Raag Gauri Majh, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). The Lord has set in me the longing of separation for the Lord's Name. (Only if) my friend, the Lord God, meets me do I find peace. O my mother, it is by seeing the Lord God that I live. The Lord's Name is my companion and my brother. Dear Sants, sing the praises of my Lord God. Through the Guru, meditate on the Name, dear ones: (this is) great good fortune. The Name of the Lord, Har Har, is my very breath of life. (With it) there are no more rounds in the ocean of the world. How may I see the Lord God? (This) yearning fills my mind and body. Dear Sants, unite (me) with the Lord; love (for him) has taken hold of my mind. Through the Guru's Shabad the Lord, the beloved King, is found. O fortunate one, meditate on (his) Name. In my mind and body is a great hope for God, Govind. Dear Sants, unite (me) with the Lord, with God, Govind, who is close at hand. Through the True Guru's teaching the Name ever shines (within). The hope in servant Nanak's mind has been fulfilled. ॥4॥
175.2: Raag Gauri Majh, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Only when I meet the Name, the beloved I am parted from, do I live. Within the mind is the Amrit; through the Guru's teaching I take in the Lord's (Amrit). (My) mind is dyed in the Lord's love; I ever drink the Lord's nectar. Having found the Lord in my mind, I live. My mind and body are struck by love, the Lord's arrow. The Lord, the all-wise Purakh, is my beloved, my friend. The Guru, the Sant, unites (me) with the Lord, skilled and all-wise. I am a sacrifice to the Name. I ask for word of the Lord, Har Har, my friend, the Lord my companion. Tell me of the Lord, dear Sants; I am searching for the Lord. (When) the True Guru, well pleased, shows the way, I find the Lord, and merge in the Lord's Name, in the Name alone. The ache of love, the pain of separation from the Lord, has struck me. O Guru, fulfil my heart's wish, that I may put the Amrit (of the Name) into my mouth. O Lord, be kind, that I may meditate on the Lord's Name, and (I,) servant Nanak, may receive the Lord's nectar. ॥4॥
175.3: Raag Gauri Guareri, Chaupade, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. By what means does true well-being come, my brother? How is the Lord, Ram, our helper, to be found? There is no well-being in the household, nor in (holding that) all this wealth is mine, nor in lofty mansions and lovely shade. In false greed (for these, one) has wasted this life. (One) is delighted at the sight of elephants and horses, gathers armies, (keeps) deputies and royal attendants, (yet) round (his) neck is the rope, the noose of Haumai. (One) holds sway over all (the earth) in the ten directions, enjoys revels and pleasures and many women; (but it is) like a king who becomes a beggar in a dream. The True Guru has shown me the one (true) well-being: the Lord's devotees are glad of whatever the Lord does. O servant Nanak, (the devotee) kills Haumai and merges (in the Lord). In this way true well-being comes, my brother; thus is the Lord, Ram, our helper, found.
Rahao Dooja: the second Rahao (Pause) of this shabad, which answers the question asked in the first.
176.1: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Why should one wander in doubt? What is there to doubt, when he alone pervades the water, the land and the sky? Delivered are the Gurmukhs; the manmukhs have lost their honour. The one whom the merciful Lord, Ram, himself protects, no other can come up to. In all, the one Infinite (Lord) is at work; so sleep in peace, free of care. He knows all that happens. The manmukhs, who thirst for what is other (than God), are dead (within). They wander through many births, as written from the Lord's court by (their) deeds. As (they) sow, so shall (they) eat. Beholding (the Lord), (my) mind has blossomed; everywhere I have seen God (Brahm) shining forth. The Lord has fulfilled servant Nanak's hope. ॥4॥
176.2: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
