In many births (you) were a worm and a moth, in many births an elephant, a fish, a deer, in many births (you) became a bird and a snake, in many births (you) were a horse and an ox under the yoke. Meet the Master of the world: (now) is your turn to meet him. After a very long time this (human) body has been given (to you). In many births (you) were made rocks and mountains, in many births (you) were lost from the womb before birth, in many births (you) were brought forth as plants; (so you) were made to wander through the eighty-four lakh forms of life. (Now) you have been granted (human) birth: in the Saadh Sangat do seva, and by the Guru's teaching dwell on the Lord, Har Har. Give up pride, falsehood and arrogance. If (you) die while living, (you) will be accepted in the Lord's court. Whatever has been (and is to be) comes from you, (O Lord); there is no other able to do anything. You are met only when you unite (one with yourself). Says Nanak: sing the virtues of the Lord, Har Har. ॥4॥
Brikh here is the ox (Sanskrit vrisha), not a tree; like the horse, it is yoked.
176.3: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (O brother), in the field of deeds (this human life) sow the Naam, and your task (in life) will be fulfilled. You will gain the fruit that the fear of Jam is ended, (if) you sing day after day the virtues and praise of the Lord, Har Har. Enshrine the Name of the Lord, Har Har, within your heart, and set your affairs right without delay. Be ever alert, with your mind on your God; then you will receive honour in the Lord's court. Give up all clever arguments and cunning, and fall at the feet of the Sants. He in whose hands all beings are is never parted (from anyone); he is with all. Leave (other) devices and take hold of his shelter, and in an instant you will be set free. Know him to be ever near, and accept God's command as true. By the Guru's word, erase your self-conceit. O Nanak, repeat the Name of the Lord, Har Har; repeat this chant. ॥4॥
177.1: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The Guru's word is ever imperishable. By the Guru's word, the noose of Jam is cut. The Guru's word stays with the soul; by the Guru's word one remains steeped in the Lord's love. (O brother), what the Guru has given is of use to the mind; hold what the Sant (the Guru) has done to be true and lasting. The Guru's word is unshakeable; nothing can pierce it. By the Guru's word, doubt and the sense of separateness are cut away. The Guru's word never goes anywhere (it never fails); by the Guru's word one sings the virtues of the Lord. The Guru's word goes along with the soul; the Guru's word is a master to those who have none. By the Guru's word one does not fall into hell; by the Guru's word the tongue savours the Amrit (of the Name). The Guru's word is manifest in the world; by the Guru's word one does not come away defeated. To the servant on whom (the Lord) himself is kind, O Nanak, the True Guru is ever merciful. ॥4॥
177.2: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). He who made (me) a jewel out of dust, who took care to keep (me) safe in the womb, who gave (me) glory and greatness: on that God I meditate at all hours. O all-pervading Lord, (grant that) I may obtain the dust of the feet of the holy, and, meeting the Guru, meditate on my Master. He who made (me) a speaker out of a fool, who gave (me) understanding where there was none, by whose grace I obtain the nine treasures: that God does not leave my mind. He who gave a place to (me), the homeless, who gave honour to (me), the dishonoured, who fulfilled my every hope: him I remember day and night, with every breath and every morsel. He by whose grace (my) noose of Maya is cut, (and) by the Guru's grace the bitter poison has become Amrit: says Nanak, nothing can be done by this (mortal) of himself; I praise (him), the Protector. ॥4॥
177.3: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). In his refuge there is neither fear nor sorrow; nothing will happen outside his power. I have given up cleverness, (pride in) strength and intellect, and vice; (God) is the protector of his own servant. Repeat, O my mind, the Lord's Name, Ram Ram, with love; at home and abroad he is ever with you. Keep his support in your mind; taste the Guru's Shabad, the sweet essence of Amrit. Tell me, of what use are other efforts? God himself, in his grace, saves (one's) honour. Tell me, what is a mortal? What is his power? All the clamour of Maya is false. The Master is the one who does and causes all to be done; he knows the inner being of every heart. Of all comforts, this is the true comfort: take the Guru's teaching into your mind. The one whose loving attention is held on the Lord's Name, says Nanak, is blessed, and greatly fortunate. ॥4॥
178.1: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Hearing the Lord's story, (those who) have washed off (the mind's) filth have become most pure, and (gained) a mountain of peace. By great good fortune (those who) have found the Saadh Sangat have been dyed with love for the Supreme Lord. (The Guru) has saved the servant who repeats the Name of the Lord, Har Har; the Guru has carried (him) across the ocean of fire. Singing Kirtan, (their) minds have been cooled; the sins of birth after birth are gone. (They) have seen all the treasures within (their own) mind; why would they now go searching (outside)? When their own God became merciful, the servant's toil bore its full fruit. Cutting (their) bonds, (God) made (them) his own servants, through remembering, remembering, ever remembering the treasure of virtues. The One is in (their) mind; the One is in every place; the Perfect One is filling all places. The perfect Guru has dispelled all (their) doubt. Remembering the Lord, O Nanak, (they) have found peace. ॥4॥
178.2: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Those who died before are left behind (forgotten); those who survive stand with their loins girded (for the race after Maya). The affairs in which those (dead) were entangled, to the Maya of those same affairs these (living) cling twice as tightly as they did. That hour (of death) never comes to (the mortal's) mind; he clings to that very thing which is bound to perish. The fool's body is bound by hopes; he is wrapped up in lust, anger and attachment. Dharam Raj stands over (his) head, (yet) he eats the poison (of Maya), taking it to be sweet. (He says:) I will bind (my enemy), I will settle my score; who dares set foot on my land? I am a pandit, I am shrewd and wise. (But) the ignorant one does not know the Creator. (God) alone knows his own state and his own extent; what can anyone say? What can one describe in words? (O Lord), to whatever you attach (beings), to that they must be attached; everyone must ask for his own good. (O Lord), everything is yours; you are the Creator; you have no end, no near shore and no far one. Grant your servant this gift: that Nanak may never forget the Naam. ॥5॥
178.3: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). By countless efforts, release (from Maya's hold) does not come; much cleverness only heaps on a heavier load. (The one who) serves the Lord with pure love (goes) with honour to God's court. O my mind, take hold of the shelter of the Lord's Name, and the hot wind (of suffering) will not touch you. As a ship (carries one) in the fearful ocean, as lamps give light in the dark, as fire takes away the pain of cold, so, repeating the Naam, peace comes to the mind. The thirst of your mind will be quenched, every hope will be fulfilled, your mind will not waver; repeat the Amrit Naam through the Guru, O friend. Only that person obtains the medicine of the Naam whom (the Lord) himself, in his grace, causes to receive it. The one in whose heart the Name of the Lord, Har Har, dwells, his pain and suffering, O Nanak, run away. ॥4॥
179.1: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Amassing great wealth, the mind is not sated; beholding many beauties, it is not satisfied. (The mortal) is entangled in sons and wife, thinking them his own; (but) that (wealth and beauty) perishes, and they (sons and wife) become a heap of ashes. Without worship of the Lord, I see (people) wailing. Cursed is the body and cursed the wealth of those imbued with Maya. As bags of money are set on the head of a man pressed into forced labour: they go to the master's house, and he bears only the pain. As in a dream one becomes a king and sits (on the throne), (but) when he opens his eyes, his affairs come to nothing. As a watchman (keeps guard) over another's field: the field belongs to its owner, and the watchman gets up and goes. For that field the watchman frets and worries, (yet) nothing of it comes into his hands. The kingdom is his (God's), and the dream too is his; he who gave Maya has also attached the craving for it. He himself destroys, and he himself sets right. Nanak's prayer is before God. ॥4॥
179.2: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). I have seen Maya of many colours in many ways; clever things have been written with pen and paper; being a chief, a king and a khan has been tried and seen; (yet) by these the mind is not satisfied. O Sants, tell me of that peace by which (my) thirst may be quenched; satisfy (my) mind. Riding horses swift as the wind and elephants, perfume and sandalwood, and the bed of a beautiful woman, the plays of actors and the songs sung on the stage: in these (too) the mind has found no contentment. A throne, the adornments of a royal court, and carpets, fruits of every kind and lovely gardens, the taste for hunting and the pastimes of kings: (with these too) the mind is not at ease; all this striving is a deception. In their kindness the Sants have told (me) the truth: all comforts and this bliss are found (thus), by singing the Lord's Kirtan in the Saadh Sangat. Says Nanak, (this) is found by great good fortune. One who has the wealth of the Lord (in the heart), he alone is at ease; by God's grace (one) comes to meet the Saadh Sangat. ॥12॥
179.3: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The mortal thinks this body is his own, and clings to it again and again. (While) the noose of children, wife and household (is around his neck), one cannot become a servant of the Lord (Raam). What is that way by which (one) may sing the Lord's virtues? What is that understanding by which (one) may cross over this Maya? What is for his good, he takes to be bad; if (anyone) tells the truth, he takes it to be like poison. He does not know victory from defeat: such is the way of the world of the Saakats. The madman drinks what is deadly poison, and takes the Amrit of the Name to be bitter. He does not come near the Saadh Sangat, (and so) he wanders through the round of the eighty-four lakh (forms of life). (The Lord) has snared the birds (the beings) in the one net (of Maya); relishing and relishing, they indulge in pleasures of many kinds. Says Nanak, the one to whom (the Lord) has become kind, his snares the Perfect Guru has cut. ॥4॥
180.1: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (O God,) by your grace the path (of life) is found; by God's grace the Naam is meditated on; by God's grace (one's) bonds are loosed; by your grace Haumai is broken. When you yourself attach us, then we take to your service; by ourselves nothing can be done, O Divine Lord. If it pleases you, I sing the Bani (of your praise); if it pleases you, I utter the True (Name); if it pleases you, the True Guru's mercy (comes); all comforts, O God, lie in your kindness. What pleases you is the pure deed; what pleases you is the true dharma. All treasures and virtues are with you alone. You are the Master; (your) servant prays to you (alone). In the Lord's love mind and body become pure; in the Sat Sangat I obtain every comfort. (That) the mind stays dyed in your Name: this Nanak has known to be (true) bliss. ॥4॥
180.2: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (O tongue,) all the other tastes you have tasted have not taken away your thirst for even an instant. If you taste the flavour of the Lord's sweet essence, tasting it you will be lost in wonder. O dear tongue, drink the Amrit; steeped in this taste, you will be satisfied. O tongue, sing the virtues of the Lord (Raam); every moment meditate on the Lord, Har, Har, Har. Let us listen to no other (talk), and go nowhere else; the Saadh Sangat is found by great good fortune. At all hours, O tongue, worship the Supreme Lord, the unfathomable Master. (So the tongue) is ever at ease, here and hereafter; singing the Lord's virtues, the tongue becomes priceless. (Though) the vegetation is in bloom, with fruit and flowers on the branches, (the tongue) steeped in this taste never leaves it again. No other tastes and flavours can equal it. Says Nanak, the Guru has become (my) helper. ॥4॥
180.3: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The mind is a temple, and the body has been made (its) fence. Within this very (temple) is the infinite treasure (of the Name); within this very (temple) the Banker (the Lord) is heard to dwell. Who is the trader who has credit there? Whoever is a dealer in the jewel of the Naam takes the Amrit for his food. I offer (him my) mind and body, and serve (him); (I ask:) what is that way by which (the Lord) is pleased? Giving up mine and yours, I fall at (his) feet. Who is that servant (of the Lord) who will strike (for me) the bargain (of the Name)? By what means can (one) reach the Banker's mansion? What is that way by which (the Banker) calls (one) within? (O Lord,) you are the great Banker, with millions of traders. Who is that giver who will take (me) and bring (me to you)? Searching and searching, (I) have found (my) own home; the priceless, lasting jewel has been shown (to me). When in his grace the Banker united (me with himself), says Nanak, (it was) on the Guru's credit. ॥4॥
The Shah here is the banker who gives traders capital on credit (visah): God is the Banker, the soul a trader in the Name, and the Guru its surety.
181.1: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (The one in the Guru's refuge) stays in the love of the One night and day, and knows God to be ever with (him). He has made the Master's Name (the thing of) his daily use; by the sight of the Lord he is fulfilled and content. Those steeped in the Lord, their minds and bodies flourish; they have fallen into the refuge of the Perfect Guru. The lotus feet (of the Lord) are the support of (their) soul; they behold the One alone, and obey (his) command. the one (Name) alone is (their) trade; in the one (Name) alone they deal; they know none other but the Formless One. They are free of both joy and sorrow; ever unattached (to Maya), they are joined (to the Lord) and live by the right way. They are seen among all, (yet) they stay apart from all; they keep their attention fixed on the Supreme Lord. What glory of the Sants can I describe? (Their glory) is unfathomable, beyond understanding; I know nothing of its measure. O Supreme Lord, be gracious to me, and grant Nanak the dust (of the feet) of the Sants. ॥4॥
181.2: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (O Lord,) you are my companion, you alone my friend; you are my beloved; with you is my love. You are my honour, you alone my ornament; without you I cannot live even for an instant. You are my darling, you are my very life; you are my Master, you are my Khan (my lord). As you keep (me), so I am to live; what you say, that I am to do. Wherever I look, there you dwell; with my tongue I repeat your fearless Name. You are my nine treasures, you (my) storehouse; you are (my) joys and delights, you the support of (my) mind. You are my glory; (my attention) is absorbed in you; you are my shelter, you are my mainstay. Within mind and body I have meditated on you alone; your secret I have obtained from the Guru. From the True Guru the One, the One alone, has been firmly implanted (in me); servant Nanak (now) leans on the Lord, Har, Har, Har. ॥4॥
181.3: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (Maya) takes hold through the spread of joy and sorrow; it takes hold through births in heaven and hell; it takes hold of the rich, the poor, and (those who) look on (their own) glory; as greed, the root of (all) ills, it takes hold. Maya takes hold in many ways; O God, the Sants live by your shelter. (Maya) takes hold of one drunk with the ego-mind; it takes hold of one dyed in (love of) children and wife; it takes hold through elephants, horses and fine clothes; it takes hold of one drunk with the wine of beauty and youth. It takes hold of landowners, of paupers and of revellers; it takes hold through songs and music heard in company; it takes hold through beds, mansions and adornments; as the five foes (lust and the rest) it takes hold in the darkness (of attachment). It takes hold of one who does (his) deeds caught in Haumai; it takes hold of the householder, it takes hold of the renunciate; through ritual conduct, dealings and this (pride of) caste it takes hold; it takes hold of everything, save (those) steeped in the Lord's love. The Lord, the King, has cut the bonds of the Sants; how can Maya take hold of them? Says Nanak, the one who has obtained the dust (of the feet) of the Sants, Maya does not come near him. ॥5॥
182.1: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Gazing at another's (beauty) with a corrupt eye is the sleep of the eyes; the ears lie asleep, listening to talk of slander; the tongue lies asleep in greed for sweet tastes; and the mind lies asleep, spellbound by the marvel of Maya. In this house (of the body) only a rare one stays awake; he finds his own treasure (of life) whole and intact. All the companions (the senses) are drunk on their own pleasures; they have no awareness of their own house. The five plundering highwaymen (lust, anger, greed, attachment and pride), swindlers all, have fallen on the deserted town. Neither father nor mother protects (one) from them; neither friend nor brother protects (one) from them. Neither wealth nor cleverness holds them back; it is in the Saadh Sangat that those wicked ones are subdued. Show me grace, O Saringpani: the dust (of the feet) of the Sants is all treasures (to me). In the True Guru's company the capital stays whole; Nanak keeps awake in the love of the Supreme Lord. Only that one stays awake on whom God is gracious; this capital of his, his wealth and goods, stays whole. ॥20॥
182.2: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (God,) under whose sway are khans and sultans, under whose sway is the whole world, by whose doing all that happens comes about: there is no one outside him. (O brother,) make your plea before your own True Guru; he will carry your tasks through to the end. He whose court stands highest of all, whose Name all his devotees lean on, the perfect Master, present in all, whose splendour graces every heart: (remember him). The One, remembering whom the camp of sorrows is pulled down, remembering whom Jam says nothing (to one), remembering whom the withered turn green, remembering whom sinking stones float across: (remember him). Glory for ever to the assembly of the Sants; the Name of the Lord, Har Har, sustains the life-breath of his servants. Says Nanak, my prayer has been heard; by the grace of the Sant (the Guru), I have been given a dwelling in the Naam. ॥4॥
183.1: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Through the sight of the True Guru the fire (of craving) is put out; on meeting the True Guru, Haumai is slain; in the True Guru's company the mind does not waver; through the Guru, one speaks the Bani that is Amrit. When (we) are dyed in the True One, the whole world (is seen as) the True One; through the Guru God is known, and there is coolness and calm. By the Sant's grace one repeats the Lord's Name; by the Sant's grace one sings the Lord's Kirtan; by the Sant's grace every sorrow has been wiped away; by the Sant's grace one has been freed from the bonds (of Maya). By the Sant's kindness attachment and doubt are gone; bathing in the dust (of the feet) of the Saadh is every deed of dharma. When the Saadh is kind, Govind is merciful; this life of mine (dwells) among the Saadhs. When I meditate on the merciful (Lord), the treasure of mercy, then I find a place to sit in the Saadh Sangat. On me, without virtue, God has shown mercy; in the Saadh Sangat Nanak has taken up the Naam. ॥4॥
183.2: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). In the Saadh Sangat we have repeated (the Name of) the Lord God; the Guru has given the Naam alone as the mantra. Giving up pride, we have become free of enmity; (O brothers,) worship the Guru's feet at all hours. Now (our) evil intellect, which kept (us) strangers (to God), has perished, ever since (we) heard the Lord's praise with (our) ears. The treasure of Sahaj, peace and bliss, the Protector, saves (us) at the last. Pain and suffering, fears and doubts have perished; in his grace he has stopped (our) coming and going. (God) himself sees, speaks and hears in all; O mind, repeat (the Name of) him who is ever with (you). By the Sant's grace the light has dawned (within); the One alone, the treasure of virtues, (is seen) filling all. Pure become those who speak, holy those who listen, who sing the virtues of Govind day after day. Says Nanak, (O Lord,) the one to whom you are gracious, that servant's every labour bears its fruit. ॥4॥
183.3: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (The Guru) breaks (one's) bonds and has (one) utter (the Name of) Ram; (then) the mind settles in true, steady contemplation; troubles are erased, and one lives at ease. Such a giver is the True Guru said to be. He (the Guru) is the giver of peace who has (us) repeat the Naam, and in his grace unites (us) with him (God). (God) himself unites (with the Guru) the one to whom he is merciful; (such a one) obtains all treasures from the Guru. Giving up self-conceit, (his) coming and going ends; in the company of the Saadh (the Guru) he recognises the Supreme Lord. God has become merciful to his servant; the servant's mainstay is the One, Gopal. (his) attention rests on the One alone, and in (his) mind is love for the One alone; for the servant, the Lord's Name is all treasures. (His) love is bound to the Supreme Lord; (his) conduct is pure, (his) way of life true. The Perfect Guru has wiped out the darkness; Nanak's God is beyond all, and without limit. ॥4॥
184.1: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). That person crosses over (the world-ocean) in whose mind (God) dwells; (God) is attained by his own grace. No pain, disease or fear grips (that one) at all, (who) repeats the Lord's Amrit Naam in his heart. Let us meditate on the Supreme Lord, the Supreme God; this understanding is received from the Perfect Guru. The merciful (Lord) does and causes all to be done; he sustains all beings and creatures; he is inaccessible, beyond the reach of the senses, for ever without end: O mind, remember (him) through the Perfect Guru's teaching. He whose service is the treasure of all (gifts), God, by whose worship honour is gained, whose service never goes in vain: sing the virtues of (that) Lord for ever and ever. Show grace, O God, knower of hearts, O Lord, treasure of peace, unseen Master: all beings and creatures are in your shelter; may Nanak receive the Naam: (that is his) glory. ॥4॥
184.2: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). He in whose hands is the way of life of (all) beings: remember him, the Lord of those who have no lord. When God comes into the mind, all sorrow goes; through the Lord's Name all fears perish. Of whom, apart from the Lord, are you afraid? Forgetting the Lord, what peace do you think you know? He who holds up many earths and skies, whose light shines in all beings, whose gift no one can undo: remembering that God again and again, one becomes fearless. Remember God's Name at all hours; (it is) the dip and the bath at countless places of pilgrimage. If you take the shelter of the Supreme Lord, millions of stains are wiped away in an instant. (God) is the perfect King, dependent on no one; the servant of God holds a true trust (in him). The Perfect Guru has given his hand and saved (God's servants); O Nanak, the Supreme Lord holds all power. ॥4॥
184.3: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (The one whose) mind, by the Guru's grace, has become attached to the Naam, though asleep for birth after birth, has awoken. (He) utters God's virtues that are Amrit, and (his) Bani: the mortal (blessed with) the good counsel of the Perfect Guru. Remembering God, all joys have been found; at home and outside, all is peace and Sahaj. (He) has recognised the very One who created (him); in his grace God himself has united (him with himself). Holding (him) by the arm, (God) has taken (him) as his own; (now his task is) ever to tell the Lord's story, Har Har, and to repeat (his Name). Mantra, tantra (charm), medicine and the rite of atonement for sin: all is the Name of the Lord, Har Har, on which soul and life-breath rest. In the Lord's love the true wealth has been found; in the company of the Saadh (the Guru) the hard-to-cross (world-ocean) has been crossed. Sit at ease, O Sants and friends, as one family; the Lord's wealth has been earned, beyond all reckoning. The Guru gives (it) to the one in whose destiny it is (written); O Nanak, no one goes empty (from the Guru's door). ॥4॥
185.1: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The hands become pure at once, and the snares of Maya are destroyed. With your tongue utter the virtues of Ram every day; (so) you will find peace, my brother, my friend. Write on paper, with pen and ink, the Name of Ram, the Lord's Bani that is Amrit. By this deed your vices will depart; remembering Ram, one suffers no blows from Jam; the messengers of Dharam Raj do not (even) look towards (you); you will not be sunk in Maya, and nothing whatever will lure you. You yourself will be saved, and (through you) the world will cross over; repeat the Name of Ram, (repeat) the One Creator, Ekankar. Practise it yourself, and teach it to others; let the Name of Ram enter your heart. The one on whose forehead this treasure is (written), that person alone repeats (the Name of) God. Sing the Lord's praises, Har Har, at all hours; says Nanak, I am a sacrifice to that one. ॥4॥
185.2: Raag Gauri Guareri, Chaupade and Dupade, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. What belongs to another, that we take as our own; with what we must give up and leave behind, the mind is engrossed. Tell (me), how can we meet the Lord of the world, when our love is for what is forbidden? The thing that is false we have taken to be true; what is certain to come (death) does not touch the mind in the least. We walk the crooked path, on the left (the wrong) side; leaving the straight (way), we weave backwards. God himself is the Master of both sides; the one he unites (with himself), O Nanak, is liberated. ॥4॥
185.3: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). In Kalyug (husband and wife) come together through the bonds (of past deeds); for as long as (God's) command lasts, they share the joys (of the world). By burning (on the husband's pyre), the beloved Lord is not found; (yet), driven by the bond of her past deeds, (the widow) rises and becomes a sati. Copying others, out of the mind's stubbornness, (she) burns herself; (but) she does not win the beloved's company, and is made to wander through many births. She who, in gentle conduct and self-restraint, obeys her beloved's command: that woman suffers no pain from Jam. Says Nanak, she who has known her beloved as the Supreme Lord is a blessed sati, accepted in the Lord's court. ॥4॥
Sati: a widow who burned herself on her husband's funeral pyre, a custom of the time; the word also means a woman true in conduct, the sense of the last line.
185.4: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Through the True Name we are wealthy and fortunate; we sing the praises of the Lord in Sahaj and in love. When I opened and looked into the treasure of my father and grandfather, then my mind was filled with treasure. (In it are) jewels and rubies beyond any price; the storehouses are full, never to be exhausted, beyond weighing. O brother, (those who) eat and spend (from it) together find it never runs short; it goes on increasing. Says Nanak, the one on whose forehead such destiny is written is taken in as a sharer in this treasure. ॥4॥
The treasure of father and grandfather: the commentators take it to be the Bani of the Gurus before Guru Arjan Dev Ji, which came down to him as his inheritance.
186.1: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). While (God) is thought to be far away, we die of fear again and again; when (we) saw (him) pervading everywhere, the fear ended. I am a sacrifice to my True Guru, who never leaves (me), and surely carries (me) across. When the Naam is forgotten, (then come) pain, disease and grief; when the Lord's praises are sung, there is bliss for ever. No one should be called bad or good; giving up pride, one should grasp the Lord's feet. Says Nanak, keep the Guru's mantra in mind, and you will find peace in the True Court. ॥4॥
186.2: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). One whose friend and companion (God) is present everywhere alike: tell (me), what can that person lack? One whose love is fixed on Gobind: his pain, suffering and doubt run away. One who has come to taste the relish, the relish of the Lord, does not cling to other pleasures. One whose word holds good in the Lord's court: whom (else) does he take any notice of? One who belongs to him to whom everything belongs has peace for ever, O Nanak. ॥4॥
186.3: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). One to whom pain and pleasure seem alike: how can worry take hold of him? In the Lord's holy one dwell Sahaj and bliss; he lives obedient to the Lord King, Har Har. One in whose mind the carefree (Lord) comes to dwell has no anxiety anywhere at all. One from whose mind the wandering (of doubt) has perished has no fear of Jam at all. One into whose heart the Guru has given the Naam: says Nanak, within him are all treasures. ॥4॥
186.4: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The (Lord) of inaccessible form has his dwelling in the mind; by the Guru's grace, some rare one has come to know (this). There are springs of Amrit, of the story of Sahaj; the one to whom they are granted takes and enjoys them. (Where) the unstruck Bani (sounds), that place is unlike any other; Gopal is enchanted by its melody. There, countless and endless gatherings of Sahaj (are held); (there) the Sants are companions of the Supreme Lord. (There) is endless joy, and no grief, nor any other (care). That home the Guru has given to Nanak. ॥4॥
186.5: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (O Lord), which form of yours shall I worship? Taking up which yoga shall I discipline the body? Which virtue (of yours) shall I take up, to sing of you? With what words shall I please you, O Supreme Lord? What is that worship of you that I should perform? What is that way by which I may cross the world-ocean? What is the austerity by which one becomes a (true) ascetic? What is that Name which washes away the filth of Haumai? Praise, worship, wisdom, meditation, all such labour, O Nanak, (bears fruit for the one) whom the merciful True Guru, in his grace, meets. His alone is the merit, he alone has known God, whose (prayer) the Giver of peace accepts. ॥36॥
187.1: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The body, of which (you are) proud, is not your own; kingdom, land and wealth are not your own. (None of these) is your own; to what are you clinging? Your own is the Naam, which is found from the True Guru. Sons, wife and brothers are not your own; nor are dear friends, father and mother. Gold, silver and money too are not (your own); the choicest horses and elephants serve you nothing. Says Nanak, the one whom the Guru, in his grace, has united (with the Lord), everything is his, to whom the Lord King belongs. ॥4॥
187.2: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The Guru's feet are upon my forehead; by them all my sorrows have been taken away. I am a sacrifice to my True Guru; recognising my self, I enjoy the supreme joy. The one whose face the dust of the Guru's feet has touched has given up all the intellect of ego. The Guru's Shabad has come to taste sweet to my mind; through it I have beheld the Supreme Lord. The Guru is the bestower of peace, the Guru is the Creator; O Nanak, soul and breath of life rest on the Guru as their support. ॥4॥
187.3: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). O my mind, long for him in whose (home) nothing is lacking. O mind, my friend, take such a one as the Lord for your beloved; keep him, the support of the breath of life, ever in your mind. O my mind, serve him, the Primal Being, beyond the farthest beyond, the radiant Divine One. O mind, place your hope in him, on whom (all) have relied from the beginning, from the start of the ages. Through whose love there is lasting peace, Nanak, meeting the Guru, sings of him. ॥4॥
187.4: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Whatever the Friend does, that I accept; the Friend's doings are (to me) as joy itself. In my mind and heart there is one support alone: that he who does all things is my Friend. My Friend is free of all care; by the Guru's grace I have come to love (him). My Friend is the Knower of hearts; the almighty Being, the Supreme Lord, the Master. (O God), I am (your) servant, you are my Master; says Nanak, O God, my honour and greatness are yours. ॥4॥
188.1: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). O all-powerful Lord, the one whose side you take is touched by no stain at all. O Madho, the one whose hope is in you has no need of anything from the world. The one in whose heart the Master dwells is left with no anxiety at all. O God, the one to whom you have given fortitude: no pain comes near him. Says Nanak, I have found such a Guru as has shown (me) the Supreme Lord, pervading all. ॥4॥
188.2: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The rare (human) body is received by great good fortune; those who (even so) do not repeat the Naam are slayers of their own soul. Why do they not simply die, those who forget the Lord? Of what use is a life without the Name? Eating, drinking, playing, laughing, and all the display: what good is the adorning of a corpse? Those who do not listen to the praise of (God, who is) supreme bliss are worse than beasts, birds and the creatures that creep. Says Nanak, (the one in whom) the Guru has made the mantra (of the Name) firm: in his heart the Naam alone stays absorbed. ॥4॥
188.3: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Whose mother? Whose father? All these relations are in name only, and false. Why, you fool, do you babble (like one talking in his sleep)? Joined (with them) by the union (of past deeds), you have come (into the world) by (God's) Hukam. The clay (of all) is one, the light is one, the breath of life is one: why, then, should anyone weep? (People) wail, crying mine, mine; (but) this soul is not one that dies. Says Nanak, (those for whom) the Guru has opened the doors have been set free, and the structures of (their) delusion have been destroyed. ॥4॥
This shabad is spoken to one who is wailing over the death of a relative.
188.4: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The people who look great and mighty are gripped by the disease of anxiety. Who becomes great by Maya's greatness? Great is the one who has fixed his loving attention on the Lord. The landowner fights over land day after day; (in the end) he leaves (it) and goes, yet (his) thirst is not quenched. Says Nanak, (I) have reflected on this essence: without the worship of the Lord there is no release. ॥3॥
188.5: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Perfect is (his) path, perfect (his) bathing, perfect is all (he does), (the one) with the Naam in his heart. (Their honour) stayed whole when the Perfect One kept (it): (those) servants had looked to the shelter of the Supreme Lord. Perfect is (his) peace, perfect (his) contentment, perfect (his) austerity, and perfect both (his) rule and (his) union (with God). On the Lord's path even sinners become pure; (their) glory is complete, and complete (their) dealings with the world. The Creator ever dwells close beside (them); says Nanak, my True Guru is perfect. ॥4॥
188.6: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). By the dust (of the feet) of the Sant, millions of sins are erased; by the Sant's grace comes release from birth and death. The sight of the Sant is the perfect (pilgrim's) bath; by the Sant's grace the Naam is repeated. In the Sant's company pride is erased, (and) everywhere the One Creator, Ekankar, is seen. When the Sant is well pleased, the five (passions) come under control, (and one) takes the Amrit Naam and stores it up in the heart. Says Nanak, the one whose destiny is full comes to touch the feet of the Saadh (the Guru). ॥4॥
189.1: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Repeating the Lord's virtues, the lotus (of the heart) blossoms; remembering the Lord, all fear is destroyed. That understanding is perfect by which (one) sings the Lord's virtues; (it comes to the one who) by great good fortune finds the company of the Saadh. The Naam's treasure is found in the Saadh Sangat; in the Saadh Sangat all tasks are fulfilled. Devotion to the Lord makes one's birth approved; by the Guru's grace (one) utters the Naam. Says Nanak, that person is approved in whose heart God dwells. ॥4॥
189.2: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The one whose mind is dyed with the One (God) forgets (his) burning envy of others. (He) sees no one but Gobind; that Creator alone does and causes all to be done. (The one who) practises (the Name) with his mind and says Har Har with his mouth: that person never wavers anywhere, here or hereafter. Whoever has the wealth of the Lord is a true banker; the Perfect Guru has made (his) credit good. (He) has met the Lord King, the Being who is the life (of all); says Nanak, (he) has attained the supreme state. ॥4॥
189.3: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The Naam is the support of the devotee's life-breath; the Naam alone is (his) wealth, the Naam alone (his) trade. Through the greatness of the Naam the servant wins honour: (the one) to whom (God), in his grace, himself causes (it) to be given. For the devotee, the Naam is the abode of peace; dyed in the Naam, such a devotee is approved. The Lord's Name upholds his servant; with every breath the servant cherishes the Naam. Says Nanak, the one whose fortune is full: his mind clings to the Naam. ॥4॥
189.4: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). By the Sant's grace (I) have meditated on the Lord's Name; from then on (my) restless mind has been content. Singing (his) virtues, (I) have found the resting place of peace; (my) weariness is gone, and my demon has been slain. Worshipping the lotus feet of God, through the Lord's Simran my anxiety has been erased. Forsaking all, (I,) the helpless one, came to the shelter of the One; then in Sahaj (I) attained the high abode. Sorrow, pain, doubt and fear have fled; O Nanak, the Creator has come to dwell in (my) mind. ॥4॥
189.5: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). With (my) hands I do service, with (my) tongue I sing (God's) virtues; with (my) feet I hasten on the Master's path. Good is (this) time (of human birth): it is the turn for Simran; remembering the Naam, (one) crosses beyond (all) fears. Let (your) eyes behold the sight of the Sants; write the imperishable God into (your) mind. Go to the Saadh and listen to the Kirtan, (and) be rid of the fear of birth and death. Enshrine the Master's lotus feet in (your) heart; O Nanak, carry (this) rare body across (the world-ocean). ॥4॥
190.1: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The one on whom (God) bestows his grace: that person utters the Naam with his tongue. Forgetting the Lord, anxiety and sorrow take hold; remembering the Naam, doubt and fear run away. The one who listens to the Lord's Kirtan and sings the Lord's Kirtan: sorrow does not come near that person. Serving the Lord, his servant is made beautiful; Maya's fire cannot touch him. (The one with) the Name of the merciful Lord in mind, body and mouth: O Nanak, (he) has cast off all other entanglements. ॥4॥
190.2: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Give up (your) cleverness and all (your) cunning, (and) take the support of the Perfect Guru. Singing the Lord's virtues, sorrows perish and peace (comes), (when) the Perfect Guru is met (and one) fixes (one's) loving attention (on God). The Guru has given (me) the Lord's Name as the mantra; grieving is over and anxiety has lifted. Meeting the merciful Guru, there is joy; in (his) grace (he) has cut the nets of Jam. Says Nanak, (the one who) has found the Perfect Guru: because of (that Guru), Maya does not grip (him) again. ॥4॥
190.3: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The Perfect Guru himself has saved (us); it is the manmukh who has been struck by torment. Repeat Guru, Guru, O my friend: (your) face will shine bright in (the Lord's) court. Enshrine the Guru's feet in (your) heart; (he) will slay (your) sorrows, (your) enemies and your demon. The Guru's Shabad is with you as (your) helper; all beings have become kind (to you), O brother. When the Perfect Guru showed grace, says Nanak, my (striving) bore its full fruit. ॥4॥
190.4: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (One without the Saadh Sangat) eats many tasty things, as a beast does, and is tied up with the rope of attachment, like a thief. A body that is without the Saadh Sangat is a corpse; (such a one) keeps coming and going through the life-forms and wastes away in pain. He is dressed in many fine clothes, (yet is) like a scarecrow put up in a field to scare (creatures) off. Every body (even a beast's) comes of some use; (but) fruitless is the human who does not repeat the Naam. Says Nanak, those to whom (the Lord) becomes merciful gather in the Saadh Sangat and dwell on Gopal in devotion. ॥4॥
190.5: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The Guru's Shabad has driven off the strife and anguish (of the mind); coming and going has ended, and every comfort (is found). Fears have perished (for those) who have meditated on the fearless Lord and sung the Lord's virtues in the Saadh Sangat. (Those who) have set (the Lord's) lotus feet within their hearts, the Guru has carried (them) across the ocean of fire. (They) were going under, and the perfect Guru has pulled (them) out; those broken off (from the Lord) for birth after birth he has joined (to him) again. Says Nanak, I am a sacrifice to that Guru, on meeting whom our liberation has come about. ॥4॥
191.1: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (O brothers,) in the Saadh Sangat seek the sanctuary of him (God); lay your mind and body before him. Drink the Naam that is Amrit, my brothers; remembering it again and again, all the burning (within) has been quenched. Give up pride, and put an end to birth and death; bow your head at the feet of the Lord's servant. With every breath hold God dear in (your) mind; gather that wealth which goes along with (you). (This wealth) comes only to one on whose forehead good fortune is (written); says Nanak, fall at that one's feet. ॥4॥
191.2: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (The Guru) has made the withered green in an instant; watering (them) with his glance of Amrit, he has brought (them) to life. The perfect Gurdev (the divine Guru) has cut away the troubles; he has given his servant his own service. Worry is wiped out, the mind's hope is fulfilled, (once) the True Guru, the treasure of virtues, showed mercy. Sorrows have fled, and comforts have come to settle (within); there was no delay once the Guru gave the word. Those who met the perfect Guru have had their wish fulfilled; O Nanak, those people have borne good fruit. ॥4॥
191.3: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The fevers are gone; God has brought calm (within); (we) have been cooled; God has given (this) gift. By God's grace (we) are at ease; (he) has united (with himself) those separated for birth after birth. Remembering, remembering God's Name, the very seat of every disease has been destroyed. In Sahaj and with love, (such a one) utters the Lord's Bani; O mortal, remember God at all hours. Neither sorrow nor pain nor Jam comes near (the one), says Nanak, who sings the Lord's virtues. ॥4॥
191.4: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Blessed are the days, blessed the occasions, in which the Supreme Lord, the unattached, is met. I am a sacrifice to that hour in which my mind repeats the Lord's Name. Fruitful is that moment, fruitful that hour, in which the tongue utters the Lord's Name, Har Hari. Fruitful is the forehead that bows before the Sant; holy are the feet that walk on the Lord's path. Says Nanak, blessed is my fortune, through which I have met the feet of the Saadh (the Guru). ॥4॥
192.1: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Keep the Guru's Shabad in your mind; remember the Naam, and every worry goes. Apart from the Lord God there is no other; he alone kills, and he alone preserves. Enshrine the Guru's feet in your heart, within your breast; repeating (the Name), you will cross the ocean of fire. Fix your attention on the Guru's form (the Shabad); you will be honoured here and hereafter. Leaving all (else), (Nanak) has come to the Guru's sanctuary; (his) anxieties are gone, and Nanak has found peace. ॥4॥
Gur murat: the Guru's form; in Gurbani this is the Guru's Shabad (Bhai Gurdas: the Guru's form is the Guru's Word), not a picture or an idol.
192.2: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (God is the one) remembering whom all sorrow departs and the jewel of the Naam comes to dwell in the mind. O my mind, repeat the Bani of Govind (his praise), the Bani in which holy people have told of Ram with their tongues. Besides the One there is no other, by whose glance (of grace) there is lasting peace. Take the One alone as your beloved, friend and companion; write the letters of Har Har (the Lord's Name) in your mind. The Master is pervading everywhere; Nanak sings the virtues of (him,) the knower of hearts. ॥4॥
192.3: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The whole world is steeped in fear; the one whose support is the Naam has no fear. (O God,) in your sanctuary fear takes no hold; what pleases you, that alone is done. Caught in grief and joy, (beings) keep coming and going; peace is found by the one who is pleasing to God. (The world) is an ocean of fire, and Maya grips (all) hard; those who have found the True Guru stay cool. God the Protector (himself) saves; says Nanak, what can the poor creature (do)? ॥4॥
192.4: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (O God,) by your grace (your) Name is repeated; by your grace a place is found in your court. Apart from you, O Supreme Lord, there is no one; by your grace there is lasting peace. When you dwell in the mind, sorrow does not touch (one); by your grace doubt and fear take flight. O Supreme Lord, infinite Master, you know the inner being of every heart. I make my prayer before my True Guru, that Nanak may receive the Naam, the true capital. ॥4॥
192.5: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). As husks without grain are hollow, so empty are those mouths that lack the Naam. O mortal, repeat the Name of the Lord, Har Har, every day; without the Naam, cursed is the body, which is not (truly) your own. Without the Naam no good fortune (shines) on the brow; without the husband, where is a wife's married joy? One who forgets the Naam and is drawn to other tastes has not one of his hopes fulfilled. O God, in your grace (grant) your gift, so that Nanak may repeat the Naam day and night. ॥4॥
193.1: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). You are all-powerful; you alone are my Master; all things come from you; you are the knower of hearts. O perfect Supreme Lord, (you are) the shelter of your servants; in your sanctuary millions of people are saved. As many beings as there are, all are yours; by your grace (they have) comforts in plenty. Whatever takes place is all your will; one who understands the Hukam merges in the True One. Show grace, O God, and give (this) gift, that Nanak may remember the Naam, the treasure. ॥4॥
193.2: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). By great good fortune one gains the sight of the one whose loving attention is held on the Lord's Name. One in whose mind the Lord has come to dwell knows no sorrow, even in a dream. (God) has placed all treasures within his servant; in his company sins and sorrows depart. The glory of (such) a servant cannot be told; the servant stays merged in the Supreme Lord. Show grace, O God, and hear (my) plea: give Nanak the dust (of the feet) of your servant. ॥4॥
193.3: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Remembering the Lord, the evil that haunts you departs, and every kind of well-being comes to dwell in the mind. O my mind, dwell in devotion on the Name of the One alone; (it is this) that serves your soul. Night and day sing the virtues of the Infinite; (this is) the perfect Guru's spotless mantra. Give up (other) devices and lean on the One alone; taste the essence of Amrit, the supreme treasure. They alone have crossed the treacherous ocean on whom, O Nanak, (God) casts his glance of grace. ॥4॥
193.4: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Those who have set God's lotus feet in their hearts have met the Perfect True Guru and been carried across (the world-ocean). Sing the praises of Govind, O my brother; meeting the Saadh (the Guru), meditate on the Lord's Name. (Their) human body, so hard to come by, has been accepted (at the Lord's door), (for they) have received from the True Guru the Naam, the seal (of passage). Remembering the Lord, (they) have attained the perfect state; in the Saadh Sangat (they) have rid themselves of fears and doubts. Wherever I look, there (God) pervades; servant Nanak is in the Lord's refuge. ॥4॥
193.5: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). I am a sacrifice to the sight of the revered Guru; I live by repeating the True Guru's name again and again. O perfect Supreme Lord, O divine Guru, be gracious, that I may keep to your service. I hold (the Guru's) lotus feet within my heart, in my breast; (the feet of) the Guru are the support of (my) mind, body, wealth and life-breath. (Thus) life bears fruit and is accepted (at the Lord's door): know the Guru, the Supreme Lord, to be near (you). The dust (of the feet) of the Sant (the Guru) is found by great good fortune; O Nanak, on meeting the Guru, loving attention is fixed on the Lord. ॥4॥
194.1: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (One who in secret) does evil deeds and shows (the world) something else is bound as a thief in the court of the Lord. He alone belongs to the Lord who remembers the Lord, the One who pervades water, land and sky. (One who has) poison within, yet recites Amrit (words) with his mouth, is bound in the city of Jam and suffers blows. Behind many veils he commits vices, (but) in an instant they come to light before the world. The one who within is steeped in the True Name and its delight: O Nanak, the Creator is gracious to him. ॥4॥
194.2: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The dye of the Lord's love never comes off (for the one) to whom the Perfect Guru gives understanding. The mind dyed in the Lord's love is true (fast in its colour); (it bears) the deep crimson (of the love) of the Perfect Being, the Creator. (One who) sits in the company of the Sants and sings (God's) praises: his dye (of love) never comes off. Without remembering the Lord, (no one) has found peace; all other dyes, those of Maya, are pale and tasteless. Those whom the Guru has dyed (in love) are made joyful; says Nanak, the Guru has shown mercy (to them). ॥4॥
194.3: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Remembering the Master, sins are destroyed, and peace, Sahaj and bliss come to dwell (within). The Lord's servants rely on the Lord; repeating the Naam, all (their) anxiety has been wiped away. In the Saadh Sangat there is no fear at all and no wandering (of mind); (there) the praises of Gopal are sung day and night. In his grace God has granted release from bonds, and has given the shelter of (his) lotus feet. Says Nanak, faith (in God) has arisen in (their) minds; the servants ever drink in (God's) pure praise. ॥4॥
194.4: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). One whose mind is attached to the Lord's feet: his pain, suffering and doubt have fled. The trader in the Lord's wealth is whole and perfect; the one whom (God) honours is the hero. Those to whom the Lord of the world has been gracious, those servants have fallen at the Guru's feet. (Theirs are) peace, Sahaj, calm and bliss; they live by repeating (the Name of) the Lord of supreme bliss again and again. (Those who) have earned the capital of the Naam in the Saadh Sangat: says Nanak, God has cut away (their) affliction. ॥4॥
194.5: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Remembering the Lord, all troubles are wiped away, and (God's) lotus feet enter and dwell in the mind. Utter the Lord's Name a hundred thousand times, and drink God's Amrit essence, O dear (tongue). Peace, Sahaj, delight and great bliss are theirs who live by repeating (the Name of) the Lord of supreme bliss again and again. (They) have cast off lust, anger, greed and pride; in the Saadh's company all (their) sins have been washed away. Show grace, O God, merciful to the meek, and grant Nanak the dust (of the feet) of the Saadh. ॥4॥
195.1: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The One whose gifts (a person) wears and eats: how can it be right, O mother, to be slack towards him? (Those who) forget the Master and busy themselves with other things give up a jewel in exchange for a cowrie. Forsaking God, they cling to greed for other things; where is the honour in saluting the handmaid (Maya)? They eat and drink fare as sweet as Amrit, (yet) the dogs do not know the One who gave (it). Says Nanak, we are untrue to (your) salt (ungrateful); forgive (us), O God, knower of hearts. ॥4॥
195.2: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). To keep the mind in meditation on God's feet is the dip and the bath at all places of pilgrimage. Remember the Lord every day, O my brother; (so) the filth of millions of births is washed off. (One who) has enshrined the Lord's story in the heart has obtained every fruit the mind longs for. Accepted (at the Lord's door) are the life, the death and the birth of the one in whose heart God dwells. Says Nanak, they alone are perfect who have received the dust (of the feet) of the Saadh. ॥4॥
195.3: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (One who) eats and wears (what God gives) and yet denies (him): the messengers of Dharam Raj keep their eye on him. (You) have turned your face from him who gave (you) soul and body; (so) you will wander through many species for millions of births. Such is the way of the Saakat: whatever he does is all perverse. The One who upholds soul and breath, mind and body: that very Master (he) has put out of his mind. (His) vices have grown; many sheets have been written (with them). Save Nanak, O ocean of mercy and of peace. O Supreme Lord, (whoever comes) to your refuge cuts (his) bonds and crosses over (the world-ocean) through the Lord's Name. ॥78॥
195.4: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (Whoever) made (God) a friend, even for his own gain, was given all he longed for, and the state of liberation (too). Let everyone make such a friend, from whom no one goes away empty. (Whoever) took (him) into the heart, even for his own ends, had all (his) pain, suffering and disease destroyed (by God). (One whose) tongue has grown used to uttering the Lord's Name: all (his) tasks have been fulfilled. Nanak is a sacrifice many times over; fruitful is the sight of our Gobind. ॥4॥
195.5: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). In an instant millions of obstacles are taken away (for those) who hear the story of the Lord, Har Har, in the Saadh Sangat. One who drinks the Lord's essence, the Amrit of (his) virtues: meditating on the Lord's feet, his hunger is gone. All blessings, the treasures of peace and Sahaj, are his in whose heart you dwell, O God. Medicines, mantras and tantras are all mere ash; enshrine the Creator in your heart. (One who) has cast off all doubts and worshipped the Supreme Lord: says Nanak, this dharma (of his) never wavers. ॥4॥
196.1: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). By (God's) grace I have met that Guru, by whose strength no disease takes hold (of me). To remember the Lord is to cross the ocean of fear; in the refuge of the valiant (Guru), the papers (of account) of Jam are torn up. The True Guru has imparted the mantra of the Lord's Name; with this support (all) tasks have been fulfilled. The full glory of japa, austerity and self-restraint (has been gained), (since) the Guru was gracious and the Lord became (my) helper. The Guru has done away with pride, attachment and doubt; behold, O Nanak, the Supreme Lord spread out (everywhere). ॥4॥
196.2: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Better the blind man than one who lords it in sensual pleasures, (for) when pain strikes, he remembers the Lord's Name. (O Lord,) for your servant you alone are glory; (but) Maya takes the one engrossed in her into hell. One gripped by disease (too) remembers the Name, (but) one drunk on the poison (of vice) has no shelter (here) and no place (hereafter). (One whose) love is fixed on the lotus feet (of the Lord) does not call other pleasures to mind. May I remember (you) for ever and ever, O God, my Master; meet Nanak, O Lord, knower of hearts. ॥4॥
196.3: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). At all hours the highwaymen (lust and the other vices) keep (one) company; God in his grace has driven (them) off. Let everyone savour the sweet essence of such a Lord; that God is full of every power. The world-ocean burns with fierce heat (of the vices); God can carry (one) across (it) in an instant. The bonds are many, and (by one's own effort) they cannot be broken; remembering the Name, (people) gain the fruit of liberation. No argument or cleverness of this (mortal) can do anything; O Nanak, (when God) shows grace, (mortals) sing (his) praises. ॥4॥
196.4: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (If you) have gained the purse (of wealth) of the Lord's Name, move about the world (free of care): all (your) tasks will be fulfilled. It is by great good fortune that the Lord's Kirtan is sung; O Supreme Lord, only if you give is (this gift) received. Keep the Lord's feet enshrined in your heart, deep within; climbing aboard (them, as on a ship), you will cross over the world-ocean. Let everyone keep the company of the Saadh (the Guru); (there) is lasting well-being, and sorrow comes no more. With loving devotion, worship the treasure of virtues (the Lord); O Nanak, (so) honour is gained in the Lord's court. ॥4॥
196.5: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The Lord, our friend, fills the water, the land and the sky; as (his) praises are sung day by day, doubts have perished. Waking and sleeping, the Lord stays at (one's) side as a watchman, he by whose remembrance the fear of Jam is gone. God's lotus feet have come to dwell in the heart, (and) every sorrow has been destroyed. The One (Lord) alone is hope, honour, strength and wealth; in the mind is the support of the True King (God). Those who were very poor and without support, (once they became) servants of the Saadh (the Guru), O Nanak, God gave (them his) hand and saved (them). ॥4॥
197.1: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Bathing in the Name of the Lord, Har Har, (mortals) become pure; (its) rewards are greater than the merit (earned) at millions of eclipses. (The one in whose) heart the Lord's feet have come to dwell: (his) sins of birth after birth have fled. (The one who) has gained the fruit of Kirtan in the Saadh Sangat has not even caught sight of the road of Jam. (The one whose) support in thought, word and deed is Govind, from him (the hold of) the poisonous world has fallen away. (The one whom) God in his grace has made his own, O Nanak, (he) repeats the Lord's chant, and repeats the Lord alone. ॥4॥
Bathing at a place of pilgrimage and giving alms at an eclipse of the sun or moon was held to earn very great merit.
197.2: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Take refuge with the one who has come to know the Lord; dyed in the love of the Lord's feet, mind and body grow cool and calm. (Those who) do not enshrine in the mind God, the destroyer of fear, pass through many births, ever trembling with fear. The one in whose heart the Lord's Name has come to dwell: all his wishes and tasks are fulfilled. He in whose power are birth, old age and death: remember that all-powerful (Lord) with every breath and every morsel. The One God alone is friend, companion and comrade; the Master's Name is Nanak's support. ॥4॥
197.3: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Out (in the world, the Sants) keep (the Lord) cherished in the heart; coming back home, (they) bring Govind along. The Name of the Lord, Har Har, is (ever) at the side of the Sants; (their) mind and body stay dyed in the colour of Ram's love. By the Guru's grace (they) have crossed the (world-)ocean, (and) all the sins of birth after birth are taken away. Fortunate (is he): glory (is his), and (his) awareness (rests) in the Name, (in whose heart dwells) the pure mantra of the Perfect Guru. Meditate on (God's) lotus feet in the heart; Nanak lives by beholding (his) glory. ॥4॥
197.4: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Blessed is this place (where) Govind's praises are sung; God himself has made peace and well-being dwell (there). Misfortune is there where the Lord is not remembered; where the Lord's praises are sung, (there) are joys by the million. When the Lord is forgotten, a host of sorrows and diseases (close in); when God is served, Jam comes nowhere near. Fortunate and unshakeable is that place where God's Name alone is repeated. Wherever one goes, my Master is there alongside; Nanak has met the Knower of hearts. ॥4॥
197.5: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The mortal who meditates on Govind, lettered or unlettered, attains the highest spiritual state. In the company of the Saadh (the Guru), remember Gopal; without the Name, wealth and possessions are (all) false. He alone is handsome, clever and wise, the person who has accepted God's will. His coming into the world is approved (who) knows his Master (to dwell) in every heart. Says Nanak, the one whose fortune is perfect: his mind is fixed on the Lord's feet. ॥4॥
198.1: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The Saakat has no fellowship with the Lord's servant; the one (the Saakat) is given over to vice, while the other (the servant) is dyed in Ram's love. (Their fellowship is) like riding an adorned mare in the mind alone, (or) like an impotent man fondling a woman. (Or as if one) were to rope an ox's legs and milk it, (or) mount a cow and drive (it) after a lion; (or) take a sheep and worship (it) as Kamdhenu, (or) rush off to trade without capital. O Nanak, repeat Ram's Name in your mind; remember the Master, the Lord: (there is no) friend like (him). ॥4॥
198.2: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). That understanding is called pure and steadfast, O brother, (through which) Ram('s Name), the home of all delights, is drunk. Make the Lord's feet (your) shelter in the heart; (so) release from birth and death is won. Pure is the body in which no sin springs up; in Ram's love (shines) a spotless radiance. In the Saadh Sangat the vices are erased; this is the highest blessing of all. (Those) dyed in loving devotion to Gopal: Nanak begs for the dust of the feet of (such) holy ones. ॥4॥
198.3: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (Those whose) love for Govind has grown like this: (God) has united (with himself) those of perfect good fortune. As a wife blossoms at the sight of her husband, so the Lord's servant lives by calling the Name to mind. As a mother lives by the sight of her son, (so) the servant is steeped in the Lord, through and through, like warp and weft. As the greedy man delights at the sight of wealth, (so) the servant's mind clings to (God's) lotus feet. O Giver, do not slip from (my) mind even for a moment; O God of Nanak, (you are) the support of (his) life-breath. ॥4॥
198.4: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Those who are absorbed in Ram, the home of all delights, stay pierced through with loving devotion to (God's) lotus feet. All other pleasures look (to them) like ashes; without the Name, the world (seems to them) fruitless. (God) himself has drawn (them) out of the blind well (of Maya); wondrous is the glory of Govind's virtues. Gopal fills the forests, every blade of grass and the three worlds; (all) is God's own expanse; the merciful (Lord) is with every being. Says Nanak, that is the best of speech which the Creator accepts. ॥4॥
198.5: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Day after day, let one bathe in the pool of Ram('s Name); stirring it well, let one drink the Lord's Amrit, the supreme delight, (with relish). The Name of Govind is pure water; as one bathes (in it), all one's tasks are fulfilled. There, in the company of the Sants, (God's) discourse goes on, (which) wipes out the sins of millions of births. The holy remember (God) and rejoice; supreme bliss (God, its source) pervades (their) mind and body. The one who has received the treasure of the Lord's feet: servant Nanak is a sacrifice to him. ॥4॥
199.1: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Do that by which no filth (of vice) clings (to the mind), (and) this mind stays awake in the Lord's Kirtan. Remember the One (Lord) alone, with no love for another; in the company of the Sants, repeat the Name alone. Rituals, religious duties, observances, fasts and worship: count none (of these) a second (support) beside the Supreme Lord. His toil has borne its full fruit whose love is with his own God. Supreme beyond all, boundless, is that Vaishnav (the true devotee), says Nanak, who has given up the vices. ॥4॥
Baisno (Vaishnav): a worshipper of Vishnu, who keeps rules of purity, fasts and worship; here the name is given to the one whose love is with God and who has given up the vices.
199.2: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (Maya's goods) leave (a person) while he is still alive, O madman; once he is dead, who gains anything from them? Remember Govind in mind and body: this is the lot written (for you) from the start; Maya's poison serves no purpose at all. Whoever has eaten the swindler's drug of the senses' pleasures, his craving never departs. The world (-ocean) is full of terrible pain and hard to cross; without the Name of Ram, how will you get across? Join the Saadh Sangat and set right both worlds (this one and the next); O Nanak, worship the Name of Ram. ॥4॥
199.3: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The beard that bristles (in arrogance) against the poor the Supreme Lord has burnt in the fire. The Creator dispenses perfect justice; he is the protector of his own servant. From the beginning, from the start of the ages, (God's) glory has been made manifest: the slanderer has died, a great torment rising up (within him). He has been struck down by the One whose stroke no one can ward off; hereafter and here (his) name is evil. (God) keeps his servants clasped to his bosom; O Nanak, take (his) refuge and meditate on the Lord's Name. ॥4॥
199.4: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The mahzar (a complaint signed by many, drawn up against his servant) God himself has proved false; anguish has seized the sinner. To the one whose helper is my Gobind Jam does not come near. (He who) tells lies in the True Court, that blind fool beats (his) head with his hands. Those who commit sins are gripped by diseases; God himself sits as the judge. By their own doings (people) are bound by their own hand; all their wealth went along with their life. Nanak has taken refuge at (the Lord's) court; my Creator has kept (my) honour. ॥5॥
199.5: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The dust (of the feet) of (the Lord's) servant tastes sweet to the mind of that mortal for whom (it) is written from the start, by (his) deeds of the past. Through the intellect of ego, the mind was coated with grease; with the dust of the Saadh, (that intellect) has been scoured clean. If (one) washes the body in many waters, (the mind's) filth does not come off; no one is made pure that way. (The one who) has met the True Guru, ever merciful, has cut away the fear of death by remembering the Lord again and again. The Lord's Name is liberation, it is enjoyment, it is the way (of life); O Nanak, sing (his) virtues with loving devotion. ॥4॥
200.1: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The servants of the Lord hold the rank of true life; meeting them, the soul is filled with light. O mind, listen with (your) ears to the Simran of the Lord; O mortal, (so) you will find peace at the Lord's door. Let us meditate on Gopal at all hours; O Nanak, beholding (his) sight, (the mind) is filled with delight. ॥2॥
200.2: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Calm has come: the Guru, who is Gobind (in form), has bestowed it; afflictions and sins have perished, O my brother. Utter the Name of Ram with the tongue every day; (by it) diseases have perished and joy has come. Reflect on the virtues of the inaccessible Supreme Lord; in the company of the Saadh (the Guru) lies deliverance. Sing the pure virtues (of God) day after day; O friend, the servants (who sing them) are rid of disease and are saved. (Be gracious, O Lord,) that I may meditate on my God in thought, word and deed; servant Nanak has come to your refuge. ॥4॥
200.3: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The divine Guru has given light to the eyes; doubts are gone, and (the) service (done) has borne its fruit. Bihari (the Lord who sports in his creation) has given protection from smallpox (Sitala); the Supreme Lord God has shown grace. O Nanak, the one who repeats the Naam truly lives; in the Saadh Sangat he drinks the Lord's Amrit. ॥2॥
Sitala is smallpox, which people took to be the wrath of the goddess Sitala.
200.4: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (O Lord,) blessed is that forehead (which bows to you), blessed are the eyes (that behold) your (sight); blessed are those devotees who love you. Without the Naam, how can peace be found? (So) let the tongue speak the praise of the Name of Ram. Let us be a sacrifice to those, O Nanak, each one who has meditated on the (Lord) beyond all desire. ॥2॥
200.5: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (O Lord,) you alone are (my) counsel, you alone are with (me); you yourself protect (me), watching over and caring for (me). Such is Ram, the helper in this world and the next: he keeps the honour of (his) servant, O my brother. He in whose control is this world is himself (the helper) in the world hereafter; (my) mind repeats (the Name of that) Lord at all hours. Honour is his, he is accepted (in the Lord's court), and the True Name is his pass, for whom you yourself issue the command. (God) himself is the giver, himself the one who sustains; O Nanak, cherish the Name of Ram (in your heart) every day. ॥4॥
200.6: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). When the Perfect True Guru became merciful, Gopal came to dwell in the heart for ever. Remembering Ram, lasting peace has been found; the perfect Lord, the King, has shown mercy. Says Nanak, the one whose destiny is perfect has the Name of the Lord, Har Har, as (his) lasting wedded bliss. ॥2॥
201.1: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (The priest, at his patron's house,) loosens his dhoti and spreads it beneath him, and like a donkey he stuffs (everything) into his belly. Without (the) deeds (of remembrance), liberation is not attained; let us meditate on the Naam, the treasure (that brings) liberation. (He) takes his ritual baths, marks his brow with the tilak and performs worship, (yet) with a knife drawn (pitilessly) he takes the offerings into his hand. He reads the Veda in a sweet voice from his mouth, (yet that) mortal does not shrink from butchering living beings. Says Nanak, the one on whom (God) shows grace is pure in heart and reflects on Brahm (God). ॥4॥
201.2: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Sit steady in the home (of your heart), O beloved servants of the Lord: the True Guru has set your affairs right. The Supreme God has struck down the wicked foes; the Creator has kept the honour of (his) servant. (God) has brought emperors and kings, all of them, under the sway (of his servants); (they) have drunk the supreme essence of the Amrit Naam. Become fearless, and worship Bhagwan; on (your) joining the Saadh Sangat, (God) has granted (this) gift. O God, knower of hearts, (I) have come to (your) refuge; Nanak has grasped (your) support, O God, my Master. ॥4॥
201.3: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Dyed in the love of the Lord, one does not burn in the fire (of craving); Dyed in the love of the Lord, one is not deceived by Maya; Dyed in the love of the Lord, one does not drown in the water (of the world-ocean); Dyed in the love of the Lord, (one's life) bears good fruit. (O Lord,) through your Name all fears are wiped away; on meeting (the holy) company, one sings the virtues of the Lord, Har Har. Dyed in the love of the Lord, one is rid of all anxiety; (but) only that one is absorbed in the Lord who has the teaching of the Saadh (the Guru). Dyed in the love of the Lord, one has no dread of Jam; Dyed in the love of the Lord, one's hopes are fulfilled. Dyed in the love of the Lord, one is touched by no sorrow; One dyed in the love of the Lord stays awake night and day; One dyed in the love of the Lord dwells in the home of Sahaj; Dyed in the love of the Lord, one's doubt and fear take flight. Dyed in the love of the Lord, one's understanding becomes noble; Dyed in the love of the Lord, one's renown is spotless. Says Nanak, I am a sacrifice to those who never forget my God. ॥4॥
201.4: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Those who make the effort (on the Lord's path) have become calm in mind; walking on (that) way, all their sorrows have gone. Repeating the Naam, bliss has filled their minds, as they have sung with love the virtues of the (Lord of) supreme bliss. There is well-being; they have come into the home of joy; on meeting the Saadh Sangat, the curse (of Maya) has gone. The eyes become pure the moment they behold (the Lord's) sight; blessed are the foreheads that touch (his) lotus feet. In the service of Gobind this body bears its fruit; by the grace of the Sant (the Guru) the supreme state has been attained. The servant whom (God) himself has helped has found peace by falling at the feet of (the Lord's) servants. When selfhood was gone, they became (one with the Lord) himself, (when) they came into the refuge of the treasure of mercy. When (one) has found the very One he longed for, where else would he go then to search (for him)? (Such ones) have become steady; they dwell on the seat of peace; O Nanak, by the Guru's grace (they) have come to live in peace. ॥4॥
a01.title: Raag Gauri: Sukhmani, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
a01.salok: Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Salutation to the Primal Guru, who was before all. Salutation to the Guru who has been since the ages began. Salutation to the True Guru. Salutation to the revered, divine Guru. ॥1॥
a01.p1: Let me practise Simran (meditative remembrance of God) and, remembering him again and again, find peace, and rid my body of strife and anguish. Let me remember the One, the Sustainer of the universe, whose Naam (the Name, God's presence remembered) is repeated by multitudes beyond counting. The Vedas, the Puranas and the Simritis have held the one word of the Lord's Name to be the purest of words. The one in whose heart God places even a particle of it has glory beyond counting. Some long for one thing only, the sight of you. Says Nanak, save me along with them. ॥1॥
a01.rahao: Sukhmani, the jewel of peace, is God's Name, the nectar of peace. It dwells in the minds of the devotees.
a01.p2: Through Simran of God, one does not come to lodge in the womb again. Through Simran of God, sorrow and the messenger of Death flee. Through Simran of God, death keeps away. Through Simran of God, the enemy turns back. While remembering God, no obstacle at all can touch one. Through Simran of God, one stays awake night and day. Through Simran of God, fear takes no hold. Through Simran of God, pain does not torment. Simran of God is found in the Saadh's company (the company of the holy one). All treasures, O Nanak, are found in the Lord's love. ॥2॥
a01.p3: Through Simran of God come riches, spiritual powers and the nine treasures. Through Simran of God come knowledge, meditation and insight into the essence. Through Simran of God, one has performed chanting, austerity and worship. Through Simran of God, duality is destroyed. Through Simran of God, one has bathed at the places of pilgrimage. Through Simran of God, one is honoured in the Lord's court. Through Simran of God, whatever happens is good. Through Simran of God, life bears its fruit in full. They alone practise Simran whom God himself moves to it. Says Nanak, I fall at their feet. ॥3॥
a01.p4: Simran of God is the highest of all. Through Simran of God, multitudes have been saved. Through Simran of God, craving is quenched. Through Simran of God, everything becomes clear. Through Simran of God, there is no terror of the messenger of Death. Through Simran of God, hopes are fulfilled. Through Simran of God, the mind's filth is washed away. The ambrosial Naam settles in the heart. God dwells on the tongue of the Saadh. Nanak is the slave of the slaves of God's servants. ॥4॥
a01.p5: All who remember God are rich. All who remember God are honoured. All who remember God are accepted by him. All who remember God are the foremost of people. All who remember God depend on no one. All who remember God are kings over all. All who remember God dwell in peace. All who remember God become forever imperishable. They alone take to Simran to whom God himself is merciful. Nanak begs for the dust of the feet of such a servant. ॥5॥
