a20.p5: Friends, Sants (saints), do this work: give up all else and repeat the Lord's Name. Remember, remember, remember him, and find peace. Repeat the Naam yourselves and have others repeat it. Through loving devotion the world-ocean is crossed; without devotion the body will turn to ashes. The Naam is the treasure of every blessing and comfort; even one who is drowning finds rest in it. Every sorrow is destroyed. Says Nanak, repeat the Naam, the treasure of virtues. ॥5॥
a20.p6: Love has welled up in me, the sweetness of love, and longing; within mind and body this alone is my aim: to behold the sight of him with my eyes and be at peace. The mind blossoms as it washes the feet of the Saadhs. The devotees are dyed in his love, mind and body; only a rare one gains their company. Be merciful and give me one thing: that by the Guru's grace I may repeat the Naam. His praise cannot be told. O Nanak, he is present in all. ॥6॥
a20.p7: God is forgiving, merciful to the meek. He loves his devotees and is ever kind. He is Master of the masterless, Gobind (the Lord of the universe), Gopal (the sustainer of the world); he cherishes every heart. He is the Primal Being, the cause of all, the Creator, he is the mainstay of his devotees' lives. Whoever repeats his Name becomes pure, fixing the mind's love on him in loving devotion. We are without virtue, lowly and ignorant. Nanak is in your refuge, Lord, Supreme Being. ॥7॥
a20.p8: All the heavens, freedom and liberation are gained by singing the Lord's praises for a single moment. Many kingdoms, pleasures and honours belong to one whose mind delights in the telling of the Lord's Name. Many foods, garments and music are his whose tongue repeats Har Har every day. Good are his deeds, glorious and rich is he in whose heart dwells the perfect Guru's teaching. God, let me dwell in the Saadh Sangat (the company of the holy). O Nanak, there every comfort shines forth. ॥8॥
a21.salok: He himself has qualities and is beyond qualities; he is the Formless One, absorbed in the trance of the void (sunn samadhi). O Nanak, he himself made all this, and he himself, in turn, meditates on himself. ॥1॥
a21.p1: When none of this visible world could be seen, where then could sin and merit come from? When he himself had entered his own trance of the void, then with whom could anyone practise hatred and strife? When the world had no colour or mark to be seen, then tell me, whom could joy and grief take hold of? When the Supreme Lord was all alone, by himself, then where was attachment, and who could have doubt? He himself has set his own play in motion. O Nanak, there is no other doer. ॥1॥
a21.p2: When God the Master alone existed, then tell me, who could be counted bound or free? When there was only the Lord, unreachable and infinite, then tell me, who could be born into hell or heaven? When God was beyond qualities, in his own natural poise, then tell me, where were Shiva and Shakti (spirit and matter)? When he kept his own light within himself, then who was without fear, and who feared what? He himself performs his own wondrous plays. O Nanak, the Master is unreachable and infinite. ॥2॥
a21.p3: When the Imperishable was seated at ease in his own place, then tell me, where were birth, death and destruction? When there was only that perfect Creator God, then tell me, who could feel the terror of the messenger of Death? When God, unmanifest and beyond the senses, was the One alone, then of whom could Chitra and Gupta (the recorders of deeds) ask an account? When there was only the Master, stainless, beyond the senses and unfathomable, then who was set free, and who was tied in bonds? He himself, by himself, is the wonder. O Nanak, he himself gave rise to his own form. ॥3॥
a21.p4: Where the pure Being, Master of all beings, was alone, there was no dirt; tell me, what could be washed? Where there was only the stainless, formless One, free of all desire, there who had honour, and who had pride? Where the Lord of the world was present in his own form alone, there, tell me, whom could deceit and fault cling to? Where the One whose being is light was merged in his own light, there who was hungry, and who could be satisfied? He is the Creator, who does and causes all to be done. O Nanak, the Creator is beyond all reckoning. ॥4॥
a21.p5: When he had made his glory with himself alone, then who was mother, father, friend, son or brother? Where he himself was master of every power, there where were the Vedas and the Katebs (the Semitic scriptures), and who was there to recognise them? When he held himself within himself, then who could weigh good omens and bad? Where he himself was the high and himself the near, there who could be called master, and who servant? We are lost in wonder upon wonder, amazed. Says Nanak, you alone know your own state. ॥5॥
a21.p6: Where the One who cannot be deceived, pierced or divided was absorbed in himself, there whom could Maya (the world's illusion and lure) take hold of? He bowed in homage to himself alone; the three qualities of Maya had no entry there. Where there was only the One, the one Lord alone, there who was free of care, and who could be touched by care? Where he himself was content within himself, there who was to speak, and who to listen? He is vast and endless, higher than the highest. O Nanak, he alone can reach himself. ॥6॥
a21.p7: When he himself fashioned the visible expanse of the world, he spread it out within the three qualities. Then came talk of sin and merit; one is bound for hell, another longs for heaven. The snares of household life and the entanglements of Maya, the burdens of Haumai (ego), attachment, doubt and fear, pain and pleasure, honour and dishonour: all these came to be told of in many ways. He himself stages his own play and watches it. When he winds up the play, O Nanak, then he alone remains. ॥7॥
a21.p8: Where the Unmanifest is, there is his devotee; where the devotee is, there he himself is. Where he spreads out the expanse of creation, it is for the glory of his Sants (saints). He is himself the Master of both sides; his glory befits him alone. He himself performs his plays, his joyful wonders; he himself enjoys every pleasure and yet remains untouched. Whom he pleases, he attaches to his Name; whom he pleases, he makes play the game of the world. He is beyond count, fathomless, numberless and beyond weighing. As you make him speak, so your servant Nanak speaks. ॥8॥
a22.salok: Master of every being and creature, you yourself are present and at work in all. O Nanak, the One alone is spread out everywhere; what other can be seen? ॥1॥
a22.p1: He himself speaks, and he himself listens. He himself is One, and he himself has spread out as all. When it pleases him, he brings forth the creation; by his own will he draws it back into himself. Nothing is apart from you; you have strung the whole world on your own thread. The one to whom God himself gives understanding, that servant receives the true Naam (the Name, God's presence remembered). He looks on all alike and knows the essence of reality. O Nanak, he is the conqueror of the whole world. ॥1॥
a22.p2: He holds all beings and creatures in his hands; merciful to the meek, he is the Master of the masterless. One whom he protects, no one can kill; that one is dead whom he puts out of his mind. Forsaking him, where else can one go? Above every head is the one stainless King. He in whose hand lie all the ways of every being, know him to be with you, within and without. He is the treasure of virtues, endless and infinite. His servant Nanak is ever a sacrifice to him. ॥2॥
a22.p3: The merciful one fills every place to the full, and he shows kindness to all. He alone knows what he does; the knower of hearts is present throughout. He cherishes his beings in many ways; whatever he has created meditates on him. Whom he pleases, he unites with himself; they worship him, singing the Lord's praises. With faith in their hearts they have believed in him. O Nanak, they have known the one Creator. ॥3॥
a22.p4: The Lord's servant is attached to the Name of the one Lord, and his hope does not go in vain. To the servant, service comes naturally; understanding the Hukam (God's will and command), he attains the supreme state. There is no thought higher than this for one in whose mind the Formless Lord dwells. Breaking their bonds, they have become free of enmity; night and day they worship the Guru's feet. They are happy in this world and at ease in the world hereafter. O Nanak, the Lord God himself has united them with himself. ॥4॥
a22.p5: Join the Saadh Sangat (the company of the holy) and rejoice; sing the praises of God, the supreme bliss. Reflect on the Lord's Name, the essence of all, and redeem this body so hard to obtain. Sing the Lord's praises, words of nectar; this is the way for the soul to cross over. At all hours see God near you; ignorance will end and darkness be destroyed. Hear the teaching and enshrine it in your heart. Says Nanak, you will receive the fruit your heart desires. ॥5॥
a22.p6: Set right both this life and the life hereafter: keep the Lord's Name enshrined deep in your heart. The teaching of the perfect Guru is perfect; one in whose mind it dwells has recognised the Truth. With mind and body repeat the Naam, attuned to him in love; pain, suffering and fear will leave the mind. Trader, deal in the true trade, and your cargo will come safely through to the Lord's court. Within your mind keep the One alone as your support. Says Nanak, you will not come and go again. ॥6॥
a22.p7: Where can anyone go far from him? One is saved by meditating on the Protector. When one repeats the Name of the Fearless One, all fear is erased; by God's grace a mortal is set free. One whom God protects has no pain; repeating the Naam, the mind finds peace. Anxiety goes and pride is erased; no one can equal that servant. The valiant Guru stands over his head. O Nanak, his tasks are all fulfilled. ॥7॥
a22.p8: Perfect is the wisdom of him whose glance is nectar; at the sight of him the world is saved. Matchless are his lotus feet; fruitful is the sight of the Lord, and beautiful his form. Blessed is his service, and his servant is accepted; he is the knower of hearts, the Supreme Being. One in whose mind he dwells is filled with joy; death does not come near him. They have become immortal and attained the immortal state, O Nanak, who meditated on the Lord in the Saadh Sangat. ॥8॥
a23.salok: The Guru has given the salve of divine knowledge for the eyes, and ignorance and its darkness are gone. When by the Lord's grace one meets the Sant (saint), O Nanak, the mind is lit up. ॥1॥
a23.p1: In the company of the Sants I have seen God within; God's Name tastes sweet to me. All things are within the heart of the One, though they appear in many colours and kinds. God's Name is the nectar, the nine treasures; its resting place is within the body. There is the trance of the void, and there the unstruck melody sounds, the divine music that no instrument makes; its wonder and amazement cannot be told. He alone has seen it to whom God himself has shown it. O Nanak, that servant gains understanding. ॥1॥
a23.p2: The Infinite One is within, and he is without; the Lord pervades every heart. In the earth, the sky and the regions below, in all the worlds, he is the perfect sustainer. In forest, grass and mountain is the Supreme Lord; as his command is, so is every deed. He is in air, water and fire; he fills the four corners and the ten directions. There is no place apart from him. By the Guru's grace, says Nanak, find peace. ॥2॥
a23.p3: See him in Vedas, Puranas and Simritis; the One is in moon, sun and stars. Everyone speaks the speech of God; he himself is steady and never wavers. With all his powers he plays his play; he cannot be bought at any price, and his virtues are priceless. He whose light is in every light, that Master upholds all, woven through like warp and weft. By the Guru's grace doubt comes to an end. O Nanak, in them this faith becomes firm. ॥3॥
a23.p4: To the Sants all they behold is God; in the hearts of the Sants is all righteousness. The Sants hear words of good; they are merged in the Lord who pervades all. Such is the conduct of one who has known him: all that the Saadh (holy one) says is true. Whatever happens, he accepts it gladly; he knows God as the one who does and causes all to be done. For him God dwells within, and outside too it is he alone. O Nanak, at the sight of him all are enchanted. ॥4॥
a23.p5: He is true himself, and true is everything he has made; from that God came the whole creation. When it pleases him, he spreads out the creation; when it pleases him, he is Ekankar (the One Creator) alone again. His many powers cannot be grasped; whom he pleases, he unites with himself. Who can be called near, and who far? He himself is all, filling everything. One whom he himself makes aware of his presence within, O Nanak, to that servant he himself gives understanding. ॥5॥
a23.p6: He himself is at work in all beings; through all eyes he himself is the one who sees. All creation is his body; he himself hears his own praise. The One has made coming and going a play; he has made Maya (the world's illusion and lure) obey his command. Amid all he remains untouched; whatever there is to say, he says it himself. By his command one comes, by his command one goes. O Nanak, when it pleases him, he takes them back into himself. ॥6॥
a23.p7: Whatever comes from him is not bad; tell me, apart from him, has anyone done anything? He himself is good, and his works are excellent beyond measure; he alone knows his own heart. He himself is the Truth, and all he upholds is true; woven through and through, he is absorbed in his own creation. No one can tell his state or his extent; only if there were another like him could that one understand. All that he does is to be accepted. By the Guru's grace, says Nanak, know this. ॥7॥
a23.p8: One who knows this has peace for ever; that God himself unites him with himself. He is wealthy, of noble family and honoured; liberated while living is the one in whose heart the Lord dwells. Blessed, blessed, blessed is that servant's coming, by whose grace the whole world is carried across. This is the purpose of such a servant's coming: that in his company the Name comes to mind. He himself is free, and he sets the world free. O Nanak, salutations for ever to that servant. ॥8॥
a24.salok: I have worshipped the perfect God, whose Name too is perfect. Says Nanak, I have found the Perfect One; sing the praises of the Perfect One. ॥1॥
a24.p1: Listen to the perfect Guru's teaching, and behold the Supreme Lord near you. Remember Gobind (the Lord of the universe) with every breath; the worry in your mind will lift. Let go of the waves of fleeting hope; ask, my mind, for the dust of the feet of the Sants (saints). Set aside self-conceit and make your prayer; cross the ocean of fire in the Saadh Sangat (the company of the holy). Fill your storehouses with the Lord's wealth. O Nanak, salutations to the perfect Guru. ॥1॥
a24.p2: For well-being, happiness, poise and bliss, worship the Lord of supreme bliss in the Saadh Sangat. Ward off hell and save your soul; drink the nectar of Gobind's praises. In your heart dwell on the one all-pervading Lord, whose form is one and whose colours are many. He is Gopal (the sustainer of the world), Damodar (a name of the Lord), merciful to the meek, destroyer of pain, wholly kind. Remember, remember the Naam (the Name, God's presence remembered), again and again. O Nanak, this alone sustains the soul. ॥2॥
a24.p3: The words of the Saadh (holy one) are verses of the highest praise; they are priceless rubies and gems. Hearing them and living by them, one is saved; such a one crosses over and carries others across. Fruitful is the life, and fruitful the company, of one whose mind is dyed in the Lord's love. For him the unstruck Word of victory resounds; hearing it again and again he rejoices, and God thunders forth within him. Gopal shines forth on the foreheads of the great souls. O Nanak, in their company people are saved. ॥3॥
a24.p4: Hearing that he is able to give refuge, we have come to his refuge; in his grace God has united us with himself. Enmity has vanished, and we have become the dust of all; in the Saadh Sangat we receive the Naam, which is nectar. The divine Guru is well pleased, and his servant's service is fulfilled. We are kept free of household entanglements and vice, hearing the Lord's Name and repeating it with the tongue. In his kindness God has shown mercy. Says Nanak, our cargo has come safely through. ॥4॥
a24.p5: Sants, friends, sing God's praise, with a mind alert and fixed on him alone. The Sukhmani, the jewel of peace, is poise, Gobind's praises and the Naam; one in whose mind it dwells becomes a treasure-house. All his desires are fulfilled; he becomes the foremost of men, renowned in all the world. He reaches the highest place of all, and he comes and goes no more. that servant alone departs having earned the wealth of the Lord: O Nanak, the one to whom it is granted. ॥5॥
a24.p6: Well-being, peace, prosperity and the nine treasures; wisdom, knowledge and every spiritual power; learning, austerity, yoga and meditation on God; the highest knowledge and the most purifying bath; the four great blessings and the blossoming of the heart-lotus; living amid all and yet detached from all; beauty, insight and knowledge of the essence of reality; looking on all alike and seeing the One alone: these fruits come to that servant who utters with his mouth and hears with his mind, O Nanak, the Guru's word and the Naam. ॥6॥
a24.p7: Whoever repeats this treasure in the mind, he is liberated, in every age. This Bani, the Guru's word, holds the praises of Gobind and the melody of the Naam, of which the Simritis, Shastras and Vedas speak. The Lord's Name alone is the essence of all creeds; it rests in the minds of Gobind's devotees. In the Saadh Sangat millions of sins are erased; the Sant's grace frees one from the messenger of Death. Those on whose foreheads God has written his grace, O Nanak, they come to the refuge of the Saadh. ॥7॥
a24.p8: One in whose mind it dwells, who hears it lovingly: into that servant's mind the Lord God comes. His pain of birth and death is taken away; this body, so hard to obtain, is redeemed at once. Spotless is his glory, and his speech is nectar; the one Name fills his mind. Pain, sickness, fear and doubt are gone; he is called a Saadh, and his deeds are spotless. His glory rises above all. It is for these virtues, O Nanak, that its name is Sukhmani, the jewel of peace. ॥8॥

151.1: Raag Gauri Guareri, Chaupade and Dupade, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).

There is one God, Ik Oankar, the One who pervades all and is ever the same; his Name is Sat (the One who truly is); he is the Creator, the Being who dwells in all, without fear, without enmity, his form beyond time, unborn, self-existent, realised by the Guru's grace.
The fear of God is very heavy; its weight is great.
The mind's own counsel is light, and (one who follows it) speaks light words.
If one walks with (this fear) set upon the head and bears its weight,
then, by (God's) glance of grace and his favour, the Guru's wisdom is gained.
No one crosses (the world-ocean) without the fear (of God).
(Only they cross who,) living in that fear and adorning (their lives) with love, have kept the fear (in the heart).
In the fear (of God) the fire within the body blazes, and with that fear it keeps ablaze;
in the fear, and adorned through the Shabad, a life of reverent fear is fashioned.
Without the fear, what is fashioned is raw, utterly raw:
the mould is blind, and blind is the hammer's stroke.
In (the self-willed one's) intellect arises a craving for the play (of the world);
for all its thousand clevernesses, the heat (of the fear) does not reach it.
O Nanak, the speech of the manmukh is (empty as) the wind;
his word is blind, idle wind and worthless. ॥3॥
151.2: Raag Gauri, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Through the fear (of God) one finds the home (within), and in that home dwells the fear; through that fear, (every other) fear departs.
What sort of fear is that, if in it some (other) fear still takes hold?
(O Lord,) apart from you there is no other place (of refuge);
whatever happens is all your will.
One would be afraid if there were some other to fear;
to live in fear upon fear is only the turmoil of the mind.
The soul does not die, nor does it drown or swim across.
He who made (all) this does everything.
By his Hukam one comes, and by his Hukam one goes;
in this world and the next, one abides within his Hukam.
Where there is cruelty, attachment, desire and pride,
there hunger (craving) runs high, like a river (in flood).
The fear (of God) is (the soul's) food and drink, its support;
without eating it, the foolish waste away and die.
Rare, very rare, is the one who has someone (to call his own);
everyone is yours, and you are the one who cares for all.
He to whom belong all beings and creatures, all wealth and property:
O Nanak, to describe him and to reflect on him is hard. ॥4॥
151.3: Raag Gauri, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Make wisdom your mother and contentment your father,
and make truthful living your special brother.
There is something to say, but it cannot be said:
(O Lord,) the worth of your creation cannot be reckoned.
Effort and awareness, these two, have become the parents-in-law,
and, O mind, good conduct has been taken as the wife.
Union (with the holy) is the wedding day, and parting (from the world) the marriage;
truth is the offspring: says Nanak, this is the union (with God). ॥3॥
152.1: Raag Gauri, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
(The body) is a union of air, water and fire,
the play of a restless, fickle intellect.
(It has) nine doors, and the Tenth Gate:
O wise one, understand this thought.
He (the Lord) alone is the one who speaks, utters and hears.
The one who reflects on his own self becomes truly wise.
The body is clay; it is the air (the breath) that speaks.
O wise one, understand: who is it that has died?
What has died is the awareness (that ran after Maya), strife and pride;
the One who beholds (all) has not died.
That for which (people) go to the banks of tiraths,
that jewel, that treasure, is within the heart itself.
Reading and reading, the pandit voices his arguments,
but does not know the thing that is within (him).
I have not died; what has died is my demon (of mine-ness).
The One who pervades all has not died.
Says Nanak, the Guru has shown me Brahm (God),
and (now) I see no one dying or being born. ॥4॥
152.2: Raag Gauri Dakhani, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
The one who, hearing again and again, understands and accepts the Name,
to him I am ever a sacrifice.
Those whom (the Lord) himself leads astray find no place, no refuge;
(O Lord,) you give understanding, and join (us) in union (with you).
May I receive the Naam, that it may go with me;
without the Name, all are bound by death.
The support of the Name is (my) farming and (my) trade;
sin and merit are a bundle of seed (that will sprout).
Those within whose hearts lust and anger strike their blows
forget the Name and depart with falseness in their minds.
True is the teaching of the True Guru:
(by it) body and mind are cooled, and the True One is recognised.
The mark (of those who receive it) is that they live untouched, like the water-lily and the lotus in water;
steeped in the Shabad, they are sweet as the juice of the sugarcane.
By (his) Hukam, through the joining (of destiny), the fortress (of the body) with ten gates (is made);
in it the five (elements) dwell, joined with the infinite Light.
He is himself the goods that are weighed, and himself the trader;
O Nanak, through the Name he is the one who adorns (all). ॥4॥
152.3: Raag Gauri, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
How can it be known where (the soul) comes from,
where it springs from, and where it goes and merges?
How is it bound, and how does it win liberation?
How does it merge in the imperishable (state of) Sahaj?
One who has the Naam in the heart and the ambrosial Name on the lips
through the Name of the Lord (Narhar) becomes, like the Lord, free of desire.
(The soul) comes of itself, by the natural order, and of itself it goes;
it springs from the mind and merges into the mind.
The Gurmukh is free; no bond holds him.
Reflecting on the Shabad, he is released through the Lord's Name.
On a tree many birds make their home for the night;
some happy, some sad, they are ruined by attachment in the mind.
As evening passes into dawn, they look to the sky,
and fly off in the ten directions; (so beings) run about as their deeds have written.
Those joined to the Name (take this world as) a brief halt in a goil (a pasture);
(in them) the poisoned pot of lust and anger bursts.
Without the goods (of the Name), house and shop (of the heart) lie empty;
meeting the Guru, the hard shutters are opened.
The Saadh (the holy Guru) is met through destiny from the past;
the perfect people of the Lord rejoice in the True One.
Giving their minds and bodies, they receive (the Name) in Sahaj and with love;
Nanak touches their feet. ॥5॥
153.1: Raag Gauri, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
(In me are) lust and anger, and my mind is in Maya;
my mind's love wakes to falsehood and vice;
I have gathered a capital of sin and greed.
(O Lord, your) purifying Name in the mind is the raft and the boat (to cross over).
Wonderful, wonderful are you, O True One; I lean on you (alone).
I am a sinner; you alone are pure.
Like water set on the fire, (the mortal) seethes and bubbles in his speech;
the tongue and each sense has its own craving;
the gaze is on vice; there is neither fear nor love (of God).
Only by killing self-conceit does one obtain the Name.
One who dies through the Shabad does not die again;
without dying (so), how can one become perfect?
The mind stays caught in the world's show and in duality;
Narayan is eternal: whatever he does, that comes to pass.
I can board the ship (of the Name) only when my turn comes;
those held back from the ship are beaten in the Lord's court.
I praise the True One; blessed is the Guru's door.
O Nanak, at (the Guru's) door and in the home (of the heart) is the One Creator, Ekankar. ॥4॥
153.2: Raag Gauri, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Reflecting on God (Brahm), the (inverted) lotus (of the heart) has turned upright;
in the sky of the Tenth Gate the stream of Amrit flows;
the Lord (Murari) himself pervades the three worlds.
O my mind, do not wander in doubt;
when the mind is won over, the essence of Amrit is drunk.
Having won (the game of) life, the mind has accepted death (to self);
self-conceit has died, and the mind has come to know (this) from within itself;
(the Lord's) glance of grace has fallen, and within one's own home the home (of the Lord) is known.
Continence, truthful living, pilgrimage and holy bathing lie in the Name;
why should I make a great show (of anything else)?
The Lord, Nar Narayan, knows every heart from within.
Were I to believe in any other, only then would I go to another's house;
of whom should I ask? There is no other place.
Through the Guru's teaching, Nanak is absorbed in Sahaj. ॥4॥
153.3: Raag Gauri, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
If the True Guru is met, he shows (one) that death (to self)
whose joy, the joy of dying (so) and (truly) living, becomes dear within;
casting off pride, one reaches the city in the sky (the highest state of the spirit).
(All) have come with death written (for them); no one is to stay (here).
By repeating and meditating on the Lord, one finds a lasting abode in the Lord's refuge.
If the True Guru is met, duality runs away;
the lotus (of the heart) blossoms, and the mind clings to the Lord God;
one who dies while living has the supreme joy before him.
When the True Guru is met, one becomes pure through the discipline of truth;
(climbing) the Guru's ladder, one rises higher and higher;
by (God's) grace (this) is found, and the fear of Jam comes to an end.
When the Guru is met, one meets (the Lord) and merges in his embrace;
in his grace (the Guru) has shown (him) the home, the mansion (of the Lord);
O Nanak, (the Guru) has killed his Haumai and united him (with the Lord). ॥4॥
154.1: Raag Gauri, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
What has fallen (to one's lot) from past deeds, no one can erase;
what can I know of what lies ahead?
Whatever pleased him is what has come to pass;
there is no second, no other, who does anything.
(O Lord,) I do not know how great your grace is, how great your gift;
your Name is my deeds, my dharma and my caste.
You are so great a Giver, the One who gives to all;
your storehouses of devotion never run short.
The pride one takes is of no avail;
soul and body, all is in your keeping.
You slay and bring to life again; forgiving, you unite (with yourself);
as it pleases you, so you have (beings) repeat your Name.
You are the Knower, the Seer, the True One over my head;
(you) give the Guru's teaching; I rest my trust in you.
No filth remains in the body of one whose mind is dyed (in your love);
through the Guru's words, through the Shabad, he has recognised the True One.
Your strength is (his support), and the glory of your Name (his honour);
O Nanak, (he) dwells in devotion, in (the Lord's) refuge. ॥4॥
154.2: Raag Gauri, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
One who speaks of the Unspeakable and has others speak of him, who drinks the nectar (of the Name) and gives it to others to drink,
forgets every other fear and is absorbed in the Name.
Why should such a one fear? (All his) fear has merged in the fear (of God),
(for he) has come to know (the Lord) through the Shabad of the Perfect Guru.
The one in whose heart the Lord dwells, whose capital is the Lord (Hari),
abiding in Sahaj and in love, receives (the Lord's) approval.
Those whom (the Lord) keeps asleep (in Maya) evening and morning,
those manmukhs are bound by death, here and hereafter.
Those with the Lord in their hearts day and night are perfect;
O Nanak, meeting the Lord, they are rid of their doubts. ॥4॥
154.3: Raag Gauri, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
One who loves (Maya of) the three qualities is born and dies (again and again);
the four Vedas tell (only) of the visible form;
they expound the three states;
(but) the fourth state is (union with) the Lord: know him through the True Guru.
Through devotion to the Lord and service of the Guru one swims across (the world-ocean);
(then) there is no birth again, and no death.
Everyone talks of the four great gifts;
the Simritis, the Shastras and the pandits have the same on their lips;
(but) without the Guru, (their true) meaning and understanding are not found;
the gift of liberation is found through devotion to the Lord.
The one in whose heart that Lord has come to dwell
has received devotion through the Guru.
In devotion to the Lord is the bliss of liberation;
through the Guru's teaching one finds supreme bliss.
Whoever has found (this bliss), the Guru, having seen (the Lord himself), has shown (him) to that one,
and has taught him to stay free of hopes while living amid hopes.
(That Lord) is the Master of the lowly, the Giver of every comfort;
O Nanak, (that one's) mind stays dyed in (love of) the Lord's feet. ॥4॥
154.4: Raag Gauri Cheti, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
The body, (thinking itself) immortal, lives at its ease; (but) this world is (only) a play.
(O body,) you practise greed, avarice and much falsehood, and carry a great load (of sin).
O body, I have seen you scattered like ashes over the ground.
(O soul,) listen, listen to my counsel:
only the good you have done will stay (with you), my soul; this turn will not come again.
I tell you, O my body, listen to my counsel:
you brood on slander of others and carry false tales;
you cast your eyes on another's wife, O soul, and you steal and do evil.
When the swan (the soul) departs, you (O body) will be left behind, like a deserted wife.
O body, you have lived as if in a dream; what deeds have you done?
When I stole and brought something home, it seemed good to (your) mind;
(so) there is no honour here and no shelter hereafter; the precious (human) life is wasted.
(The body says:) I have become most wretched, O brother; O Nanak, no one asks after me now.
Horses of Arab and Turki breed, gold and silver, loads of fine clothes:
(none of them) has gone along with anyone, O Nanak; they have dropped away (and stayed here), you fool.
Rock sugar and dried fruits, I have tasted everything; your Name alone is Amrit.
Laying foundation upon foundation, the walls are raised, (but those) mansions (become) a heap of ashes;
(one) piles up hoards and gives nothing to anyone; the blind one thinks it is all his own.
Lanka of gold, palaces of gold (did not last): wealth stays with no one.
Listen, foolish and ignorant mind:
his will alone shall prevail.
Our Master is the great Banker, and we are his traders;
soul and body, all of it, is his capital; he himself slays and he himself brings to life. ॥6॥
155.1: Raag Gauri Cheti, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
The others (the foes: lust, anger, greed, attachment and pride) are five, and I am one alone; how can I guard my house and home, O mind?
Day after day they beat and rob (me); before whom can I cry out, O brother?
O mind, utter the Name of Sri Ram (the Lord);
ahead of you stands the army of Jam, vast and terrible.
(God) built the hut (of the body) and set doors in it, and within it sits the soul-bride;
(thinking herself) immortal, the bride revels every day in her pleasures, while those other five go on robbing (her).
(Jam's army) pulled down the hut and plundered the temple, and the bride was seized, all alone;
Jam's club (struck), the chain fell about her neck, and those five ran away.
A wife craves gold and silver; friends crave things to eat;
O Nanak, for their sake (a man) commits sins, and will go bound to the city of Jam. ॥4॥
155.2: Raag Gauri Cheti, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
(O yogi,) the (true) earrings are those within the heart; make the body itself your patched coat;
bring the five disciples (the senses) under control, O Raval, and make this mind your staff.
In this way you will find the way of Yoga:
there is one Shabad, and no other; set your mind on that (as your food of) roots and tubers.
If by shaving the head the Guru is found, we have made the Guru our Ganga;
you do not remember the one Lord, the Saviour of the three worlds, O blind one.
Making a show, you win (people's) minds with (mere) talk; your (own) doubt does not leave you at all.
If you fix your consciousness on the feet of the One, why would you chase after greed and avarice?
With your mind absorbed (in him), repeat (the Name of) the Niranjan;
why, O yogi, do you speak so much deceit?
The body is crazed and the swan (the soul) a child; life goes by in crying, mine, mine.
Nanak humbly prays: when the naked (body) burns, then, afterwards, (the soul) repents. ॥4॥
156.1: Raag Gauri Cheti, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
O mind, the One alone is the root of all medicine and every mantra, if you make your consciousness firm (in him);
take (the Name of) the One who cuts away the sinful deeds of birth after birth.
O brother, the Master of the mind is the One alone;
(while) your three qualities stay engrossed in the world, the Unseen cannot be perceived.
Maya tastes sweet to the body, like sugar; we have taken up (its) bundle;
the night is dark and nothing can be seen, and the mouse (of time) gnaws away at the rope (of life), O brother.
As much as the manmukhs act (by their own will), so much pain befalls them; the Gurmukh receives honour.
What he has done, that alone has come to be; the record of past deeds cannot be erased.
Those who are dyed (in the Lord), having given (him) their love, are full to the brim and never run dry;
if Nanak becomes the dust of their feet, then (this) fool too may gain something. ॥4॥
156.2: Raag Gauri Cheti, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Since when has (anyone) been our mother, since when our father? From what place have we come?
We took shape in the fire (of the womb), from the water (of the seed): for what purpose were we made?
O my Master, who knows your virtues?
How many lives as trees and plants we have seen; how many times we were made beasts;
how many times we came among the families of snakes; how many times we were made to fly as birds.
(Man) breaks into the town's shops and its solid houses, and having stolen, comes home;
he looks ahead and looks behind, (but) where can he hide from you, (O Lord)?
We have seen river banks and tiraths, the nine regions (of the earth), shops, towns and bazaars;
(at last) the trader took up the scales and began to weigh within his own heart.
As full as the ocean is of water, so many are our faults.
Show mercy, show some kindness: you have carried sinking stones across.
The soul burns like fire; a knife (of craving) cuts within;
Nanak humbly prays: (one who) recognises the Hukam has peace day and night. ॥6॥
156.3: Raag Gauri Bairagan, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
You have wasted the night in sleep and the day in eating;
this life is (precious) as a diamond, yet it goes in exchange for a cowrie shell.
You have not known the Name of the Lord;
(Man) buries endless wealth in the earth, (but) the Endless One is not longed for;
those who went off longing for endless (wealth) came back having lost the Endless One.
If it came to whoever reached out and took it, everyone would be rich;
it is settled by deeds, however much everyone may long (for it).
O Nanak, the One who made the creation takes care of it;
no one can tell the Master's Hukam, to whom he will give glory. ॥4॥
157.1: Raag Gauri Bairagan, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Were I a doe, I would live in the forest, picking roots and tubers to eat,
and if by the Guru's grace my Husband (the Lord) met me, I would give myself up to him again and again.
(O Lord,) your Name is my merchandise and my trade.
Were I a koel (the Indian cuckoo), I would dwell in the mango tree and reflect on the Shabad in Sahaj;
in Sahaj and in love my Husband would meet me, whose sight and form are beyond all measure.
Were I a fish, I would live in the water (of the Lord), who takes care of all beings and creatures;
my Husband dwells on this shore and on the far shore; I will meet him with my arms spread wide.
Were I a she-snake, I would dwell in the earth; (if) the Shabad dwelt (within me), fear would go.
O Nanak, they are ever happy soul-brides, whose light merges in the Light. ॥4॥
157.2: Raag Gauri Poorbi Deepaki, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
In the house where (God's) praise is spoken and the Creator is reflected upon,
in that house sing the Sohila and remember the Creator.
Sing the Sohila of my Fearless Lord.
I am a sacrifice to the Sohila by which there is peace for ever.
Day after day all beings are cared for; the Giver will watch over (each one).
(O soul,) you cannot set a value on his giving; what measure can be taken of that Giver?
The year and the day (of my wedding) have been written; gather, (friends,) and pour the oil (of the wedding rite).
Give me your blessings, friends, so that I may be united with my Master.
To every house this same summons comes; these calls go out every day.
Let us remember the One who sends the call; O Nanak, those days are coming (for us too). ॥4॥
157.3: Raag Gauri Guareri, Chaupade, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
When the Guru is met, union with the Lord comes about;
that (Lord) himself brings (one) into his union.
My God himself knows every way;
by his Hukam he unites (one), who then recognises (him) through the Shabad.
In the fear of the True Guru, doubt and dread depart;
one steeped in that fear merges in the love of the True One.
When the Guru is met, the Lord comes to dwell in the mind, of his own loving nature.
My God is great; his worth cannot be found.
Whoever praises him through the Shabad, him who has no end and no near or far shore,
my God, the Forgiver, forgives (that one).
When the Guru is met, all wisdom and understanding come;
that True One dwells in the mind made pure.
When the True One dwells (within), all one's work is true;
reflection on the Shabad is the noblest conduct.
True service comes from the Guru;
through the Guru, some rare one recognises the Naam.
The Giver, who bestows all gifts, lives for ever;
O Nanak, (by his gift) love for the Lord's Name takes hold. ॥4॥
158.1: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Some rare one receives spiritual wisdom from the Guru;
the one who comes to understand from the Guru succeeds.
From the Guru come Sahaj and reflection on the True One;
from the Guru one finds the door of liberation.
By perfect fortune the Guru comes and meets one,
and one merges in true Sahaj, in the True One.
When the Guru is met, one quenches the fire of craving;
from the Guru, peace comes to dwell in the mind.
From the Guru come purity, holiness and cleanness;
from the Guru, union (with God) comes about through the Shabad.
Without the Guru, all (the world) is led astray in doubt;
without the Name, it suffers great pain.
One who becomes Gurmukh meditates on the Naam;
through the sight of the True One, true honour is gained.
To whom else should one speak? That One alone is the Giver;
when he shows grace, union comes about through the Shabad.
Having met the Beloved (Guru), may I sing the True One's praises;
may Nanak, becoming true, merge in the True One. ॥4॥
158.2: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
True is that place (the Sat Sangat), where the mind becomes pure;
one makes one's dwelling in the True One, and becomes true.
The true Bani is manifest through all four ages;
the True One is himself everything, of his own self.
When (God's) grace comes, he brings one into the Sat Sangat,
and, seated in that place, one sings the Lord's praises.
Let this tongue burn that is in the love of another,
that does not taste the Lord's sweet essence and utters insipid words.
Without understanding (that taste), body and mind become insipid;
without the Name, the wretched one departs weeping.
One whose tongue has tasted the Lord's sweet essence abides in Sahaj and in love;
by the Guru's grace, that one merges in the True One.
Dyed in the True One, (the tongue) makes the Guru's Shabad its reflection,
and (that one) drinks the pure stream of Amrit.
That which is a (fit) vessel merges in the Name;
in a vessel turned upside down (the heart turned away from God) nothing stays.
Through the Guru's Shabad the Name comes to dwell in the mind;
O Nanak, that vessel is true which thirsts for the Shabad. ॥4॥
158.3: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Some keep on singing, but their mind finds no relish;
they sing in Haumai, and it goes to waste.
They truly sing the songs (of praise) who love the Name;
(theirs is) the true Bani and reflection on the Shabad.
One keeps on singing (his praise) if it pleases the True Guru;
mind and body dyed in the Name, (one's life) becomes beautiful.
Some sing, and some perform worship (with dance and show),
but without love they do not obtain the Naam.
True devotion lies in love for the Guru's Shabad;
(such devotees) have kept their own Beloved ever enshrined in the heart.
Fools perform worship and make a show of themselves;
they dance and dance and leap about, and suffer much pain.
By dancing and leaping, devotion is not done;
the one who dies (to self) through the Shabad, that one obtains devotion.
He, the Lover of devotion, himself causes devotion to be done;
true devotion is to lose self-conceit from within.
My true God knows every way (of all);
O Nanak, the one he forgives recognises the Naam. ॥4॥
159.1: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
When one subdues the mind, its wandering dies away;
without dying (to self), how can one find the Lord?
Rare is the one who knows the medicine by which the mind dies;
the mind dies through the Shabad: that one alone understands this.
The one whom he forgives, he grants the glory
that, by the Guru's grace, the Lord comes to dwell in the mind.
When, through the Guru, one practises the conduct worth practising,
then one comes to understand this mind.
The mind is drunk, like an elephant maddened by wine;
the Guru, striking it with the goad, brings it to life.
The mind is hard to tame; some rare one tames it.
When one consumes what will not yield (the mind's stubbornness), then (the mind) becomes pure.
Through the Guru, one has set this mind in order,
and casts Haumai and the vices out from within.
Those whom he has, from the very beginning, kept joined in his union
are never parted (from him); they stay merged in the Shabad.
He himself alone knows his own power;
O Nanak, through the Guru one recognises the Naam. ॥4॥
159.2: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
In Haumai the whole world has gone mad;
in the love of another, it has strayed, lost in doubt.
It frets with many anxious thoughts, but has not known its own self;
busy with worldly affairs, its every day has slipped away.
Remember the Lord (Ram) in your heart, O my brother;
through the Guru, let your tongue savour the Lord's sweet essence.
One who, through the Guru, has recognised the Lord in the heart,
serving the Life of the world, is known through the four ages.
Killing Haumai, one recognises (him) through the Guru's Shabad,
when God, the Ordainer of destinies, shows his grace.
True are those people whom he joins to the Guru's Shabad;
he checks their running (mind) and holds it still.
They obtain from the Guru the Naam, the nine treasures;
through the Lord's grace, the Lord comes to abide in their minds.
Repeating Ram, Ram, the body finds peace and calm;
when he dwells within, the pain of Jam does not touch one.
He himself is the Master, and he himself the minister;
O Nanak, serve for ever the Lord, the deep ocean of virtues. ॥4॥
159.3: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Why should he be forgotten, to whom belong our soul and breath?
Why should he be forgotten who pervades all,
by serving whom one is honoured and accepted in the Lord's court?
I give myself in sacrifice to the Lord's Name;
if I forget you, that very moment I die.
They forget you whom you yourself have led astray;
they forget you who are in the love of another.
The ignorant manmukhs are cast into births.
Those with whom (the Lord) is wholly pleased, he sets to the True Guru's service;
those with whom he is wholly pleased, in their minds the Lord makes (himself) dwell.
Following the Guru's teaching, they merge in the Lord's Name.
Those who have merit in their store reflect on divine wisdom;
those who have merit in their store have killed Haumai.
Nanak is a sacrifice to those who are dyed in the Name. ॥4॥
160.1: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
You are beyond telling; how can you be told?
With the Guru's Shabad as the means that kills (the mind's ego), you come to dwell in the mind.
Your virtues are countless; their worth cannot be found.
The Bani (of praise) merges in the One to whom it belongs;
your untold story the Guru's Shabad has proclaimed.
Where the True Guru is, there the Sat Sangat is formed;
where the True Guru is, the Lord's praises are sung in Sahaj;
where the True Guru is, there the Shabad burns Haumai away.
Through the Guru, by service one finds a place in (the Lord's) mansion;
through the Guru, one enshrines the Lord's Name within;
through the Guru, by devotion one merges in the Lord's Name.
The Giver himself bestows the gift,
(and that one's) love for the perfect True Guru takes hold.
O Nanak, those dyed in the Name are hailed in glory. ॥4॥
160.2: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
From the One come all forms and colours;
air, water and fire: all of them are joined together (in every being).
The Lord God watches over (his creation of) many different colours.
This is a wonder: he alone is the One (in all);
rare is the one who, through the Guru, reflects on this.
In Sahaj, God pervades every place;
somewhere hidden, somewhere manifest: God has fashioned this design.
He himself awakens those who sleep.
His worth has never been found by anyone;
everyone speaks and speaks, describing him.
One who merges in the Guru's Shabad comes to understand that Lord.
Hearing (all) again and again, he watches over them and joins (them) to the Shabad;
great glory is gained through service of the Guru.
O Nanak, those dyed in the Name merge in the Lord's Name. ॥4॥
160.3: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The manmukh lies asleep in attachment to Maya, in love with her.
The Gurmukh stays awake, dwelling on the knowledge of (God's) virtues.
They alone are awake who are in love with the Naam.
In Sahaj such a one stays awake and never falls asleep (in attachment),
whoever comes to understand through the perfect Guru.
The unsaintly one, set in his stubborn ways, never understands.
He talks (of wisdom), yet stays entangled, struggling with Maya.
The blind, ignorant one never succeeds.
In this age, deliverance comes through the Name of Ram.
Some rare one gains this understanding through the Guru's Shabad.
He crosses over himself, and saves all his family lines as well.
In this Kalyug no ritual or religious observance (avails).
Kalyug is born in the house of the chandal.
O Nanak, without the Name no one is liberated. ॥4॥
161.1: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
True is (his) command; true is the King.
Those whose minds are dyed in the True One, the Lord who needs no one,
dwell in the True One's mansion and merge in the True Name.
Listen, my mind: reflect on the Shabad.
Repeat (the Name of) Ram, and cross over the ocean of the world.
In doubt one comes, and in doubt one goes;
this world is born in the love of another (than God).
The manmukh does not remember (the Lord), and keeps coming and going.
Has (this being) strayed of itself, or has God himself led it astray?
This soul has been set to serve what is not its own;
it earns great pain, and wastes its life in vain.
When (God), in his grace, brings (one) to the True Guru,
that one remembers the one Name, and does away with doubt from within.
O Nanak, such a one repeats the Naam, and obtains the Name, which is (to him) the nine treasures. ॥4॥
161.2: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
I go and ask those who have meditated (on the Lord) through the Guru;
by serving the Guru the mind is won over.
They are the wealthy who earn the Lord's Name;
this understanding is gained from the perfect Guru.
O my brothers, repeat the Name of the Lord, Har Har.
The labour of service done through the Guru, the Lord accepts.
One who recognises his own self, his mind becomes pure;
he is liberated while yet alive, and finds the Lord.
One who sings the Lord's praises, his understanding becomes sublime,
and with ease he merges in Sahaj.
In the love of another, (the Lord) cannot be served;
(such a one) eats the deadly poison of Haumai and Maya.
Through son, family and home, Maya has bewitched (him);
the blind manmukh keeps coming and going.
The one to whom (the Lord) gives the Name of the Lord, Har Har, is (his) servant;
through the Guru's Shabad his devotion goes on night and day.
Through the Guru's teaching some rare one understands (this);
O Nanak, that one merges in the Naam. ॥4॥
161.3: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Service of the Guru has held good in all four ages;
some perfect person carries out this task.
Inexhaustible is the wealth of the Lord's Name; there is never any shortage in it.
(With it) there is lasting peace here, and glory at (the Lord's) door.
O my mind, have no doubt (of this);
by service through the Guru, drink the essence of Amrit.
Those who serve the True Guru are the great beings of the world;
they are saved themselves, and carry all their family lines across.
They keep the Lord's Name enshrined in the heart;
dyed in the Naam, they cross the terrifying world-ocean.
Those who serve the True Guru are ever servants at heart;
killing Haumai, (their heart-) lotus blossoms.
The Anhad (Shabad) plays (within them), and they dwell in their own home;
dyed in the Naam, they stay detached while living in the home.
Those who serve the True Guru, their word is true (and lasting);
in every age the devotees have uttered it and made it known.
Night and day they repeat (the Name of) the Lord, Saringpani.
O Nanak, dyed in the Naam, they become pure and free of desire. ॥4॥
162.1: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
(The one who) meets the True Guru by great fortune and by destiny's union
has the Naam in (his) heart, and ever enjoys the Lord's sweet essence.
The mortal who meditates on the Lord's Name through the Guru
wins this human life, and gains the profit of the Naam.
The Guru's Shabad is wisdom and meditation (to one who finds it) sweet;
(but) by the Guru's grace some rare one alone has tasted (it) and seen.
(People) carry out many rites and ceremonies and religious observances;
without the Name, cursed, cursed is (such) pride.
Tied in bonds, (the mortal is caught) in Maya's noose;
O servant Nanak, he is set free (only) by the light the Guru gives. ॥4॥
162.2: Raag Gauri Bairagan, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
As the cloud rains down upon the earth, is there not water within the earth (as well)?
Just as water comes forth within the earth, (so the same water) the footless (clouds) go about raining.
O brother, in this way dispel (your) doubt:
as (the Lord) makes anyone, so that one becomes, and that is the way beings go and are absorbed.
Born woman or man, what deeds can they do (of themselves)?
(O Lord,) the many forms are ever yours, and they merge in you alone.
Through so many births (beings) lay astray; when (you) were found, they strayed no more.
He whose work (the world) is, he alone knows it well; (this is seen) if (beings) merge in the Guru's Shabad.
(O Lord,) yours is the Shabad, your command; you alone are (all) yourself; where then is doubt?
O Nanak, (those whose) essence has merged with the Essence do not come into birth again and again. ॥4॥
162.3: Raag Gauri Bairagan, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The whole world is in the power of death, bound by the love of another.
Doing their deeds in Haumai, the manmukhs receive punishment.
O my mind, fix your attention on the Guru's feet.
Through the Guru take the treasure of the Naam; it will set (you) free in the Lord's court.
(Beings) wander through the eighty-four lakh (forms of life); by the mind's stubbornness one comes and goes.
(One who) has not recognised the Guru's Shabad falls into wombs again and again.
One who has recognised his own self through the Guru, the Lord's Name has come to dwell in his mind.
Dyed in devotion night and day, he stays merged in peace in the Lord's Name.
When the mind dies through the Shabad, faith takes root, and one gives up Haumai and the vices.
O servant Nanak, the treasures of the Lord's Name and of devotion are obtained only by (his) grace. ॥4॥
162.4: Raag Gauri Bairagan, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
In the parents' home (this world) the stay is four days; so the Lord, Har Har, has written it.
Honoured is the (soul-) bride who has sung (his) praises through the Guru.
(She who) gathers virtues in her parents' home finds a dwelling in her in-laws' home (the world hereafter).
Through the Guru she stays merged in Sahaj, and the Lord, Har Har, is dear to her mind.
The Husband dwells in the in-laws' home and in the parents' home; say, by what means is he found?
He himself is stainless and beyond knowing; he himself unites (one with himself).
You, God, yourself give the understanding, (and then) the Lord's Name is meditated on.
By great fortune the True Guru is met, and Amrit is put into the mouth.
Haumai and duality perish, and with ease one merges in peace.
He himself, himself alone, pervades all; he himself attaches (one) to the Name.
The manmukhs, in their pride, have not found (him); they are ignorant and childish.
They do not serve the True Guru, and they repent again and again.
They are given a dwelling in womb after womb, and in the womb itself they rot away.
So it pleases my Creator: the manmukhs go wandering astray.
The one on whose forehead my Lord God had the perfect writ written from the beginning
has meditated on the Name of the Lord, Har Har, on meeting the Guru, the hero.
The Lord's Name is my father and my mother; the Lord is my kinsman and brother.
O Lord, Har Har, O God, forgive (me) and unite (me with you); servant Nanak is (your lowly) worm. ॥4॥
163.1: Raag Gauri Bairagan, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
When wisdom was obtained from the True Guru and the Lord, the essence (of all), was reflected on,
the soiled understanding grew bright, repeating the Name of Murari.
Shiv (the Lord, the source of good) has wiped out Shakti (Maya), and the darkness has ended.
Those on whose foreheads (this) was written from the beginning hold the Lord's Name dear.
O Sants, by what means is the Lord found, seeing whom I live?
Without the Lord I cannot live for a moment; bring me to the Guru, so that I may drink the Lord's sweet essence.
I sing the Lord's praises and ever hear (of) the Lord; the Lord, Har Har, has raised me to the highest state.
From the Guru I have obtained the Lord's sweet essence; my mind and body are absorbed (in it).
Blessed, blessed is the Guru, the true Being; he has given (me) devotion to the Lord.
The Guru from whom I have found the Lord, that Guru I have made my own.
The Lord King is the giver of virtues; we are full of faults.
Sinners sinking like stones the Lord carries across through the Guru's teaching.
You are the pure giver of virtues; we are full of faults.
O Lord, (we have come) to your refuge: save (us); you have carried even fools and dullards across.
Through the Guru's teaching there is ever Sahaj and bliss, when the Lord, Har Har, is meditated on in the mind.
When the Lord God, the Friend, is found, songs of joy are sung in the home (of the heart).
O Lord, O God, show mercy; (this is my) prayer: make me remember (your Name), Har Har.
Those who have found the True Guru: servant Nanak begs for the dust (of their feet). ॥4॥
163.2: Raag Gauri Guareri, Chaupade, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
The pandit reads the Shastras and the Simritis;
the yogi calls out, Gorakh, Gorakh;
I, a fool, have learned only to repeat (the Name of) the Lord, Har Har.
O Ram, I do not know what my state will be.
O my mind, worship the Lord and cross the terrifying world-ocean; (the Lord's Name) is the boat.
The sannyasi smears ashes and so adorns his body;
he gives up other men's women and lives as a celibate;
O Lord, I, a fool, have hope in you alone.
The Khatri does deeds (of valour) and wins renown for bravery;
the Shudra labours in the service of others, and the Vaish at (his) trade;
me, a fool, the Lord's Name (alone) sets free.
(O Lord,) all creation is yours; you yourself pervade it.
O Nanak, (the Lord) bestows glory through the Guru.
I, the blind one, have made the Lord my support. ॥4॥
164.1: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
The Lord's story (the telling of his praise) is a story beyond the three qualities (of Maya).
Join the company of the holy, (the Lord's) servants, and worship him;
hear the story of the Lord, which no words can tell, and cross the fearful world-ocean.
O Gobind, unite (me) with the Sat Sangat,
so that (my) tongue may taste the Lord's sweet essence and sing the praises of Ram.
Those who meditate upon the Name of the Lord, Har Har:
make me, O Ram, a servant of their servants.
To serve (your) servant is the highest work.
The one who tells (me) the story of the Lord, Har:
that person is dear to my mind and my heart.
Only one of great good fortune obtains the dust of the feet of (the Lord's) servant.
Love for the Sants takes firm root in those
who have received the writ (of grace) written for them from the beginning;
such people, O Nanak, merge in the Naam. ॥4॥
164.2: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
The mother delights when her son eats;
the fish delights in bathing in the water;
(so) the True Guru delights in putting (food) into a Gursikh's mouth.
O Lord, unite me with those beloved servants of the Lord
by meeting whom my sorrows leave me.
As the cow, meeting her calf, brims over with love,
(as) the wife delights when her husband comes home,
(so) the Lord's servant delights when he sings the Lord's praise.
The chatrik delights when the rain pours down in streams;
the king delights in seeing the spread of his wealth;
(so) the Lord's servant delights in repeating (the Name of) the Formless One.
Mortal man delights in earning riches and wealth;
the Gursikh delights when the Guru meets him with an embrace;
servant Nanak's delight is to kiss the feet of the holy. ॥4॥
164.3: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
The beggar delights on receiving alms from a master (of plenty);
the hungry man delights in eating food;
(so) the Gursikh's delight is to meet the Guru and be filled.
O Lord, grant (me) the sight of you; O Lord, my hope is in you.
Show mercy and fulfil my longing.
The chakvi delights when the sun comes before her eyes;
(then) she meets her beloved and leaves all her pain behind;
(so) the Gursikh delights when the Guru comes before his eyes.
The calf delights in taking milk into its mouth;
seeing its mother, it blossoms in its heart;
(so) the Gursikh delights when the Guru draws him face to face (and favours him).
All other love is attachment to Maya, and it does not last;
it perishes; it is false, a show like the glitter of glass.
For servant Nanak, the True Guru is delight and contentment. ॥4॥
165.1: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Service of the True Guru has proved fruitful,
for through it, meeting (the Guru), one meditates on the Name of the Lord, the Master.
Following those who have repeated (the Name of) the Lord, a great many are set free.
O Gursikhs, my brothers, utter (the Name of) the Lord;
as (the Name of) the Lord is uttered, every sin is washed off.
When the Guru was met, the mind came under control;
the five (senses), running wild, came to rest, and the Lord was meditated on;
day after day, in the town (of the body), the Lord's praises were sung.
Those who have put the dust of the True Guru's feet on their foreheads
have given up falsehood and fixed their attention on the Lord.
In the Lord's court their faces are bright, O brother.
Service of the Guru pleases the Lord himself;
Krishna and Balbhadra (too) meditated (on him), falling at the Guru's feet.
O Nanak, through the Guru the Lord himself carries (them) across. ॥4॥
165.2: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
The Lord himself is the yogi who bears the staff;
the Lord himself sits in deep trance and practises austerity.
Such is my Ram: he fills (every place);
he dwells close by; the Lord is not far.
The Lord himself is the Shabad; he himself is the attention and its absorption;
the Lord himself watches, and himself rejoices;
the Lord himself has (others) repeat (his Name), and the Lord himself repeats it.
The Lord himself is the chatrik, and (himself) the stream of nectar;
the Lord is the nectar, and himself the one who gives it to drink;
the Lord himself creates, and himself brings (all) safely across.
The Lord himself is boat and raft, and he who ferries (us) over;
the Lord himself, through the Guru's teaching, brings (us) across;
O Nanak, the Lord himself takes (us) to the far shore. ॥4॥
165.3: Raag Gauri Bairagan, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
O Master, you are our Banker; such capital as you give, that we take.
With love we would trade in the Lord's Name, should you yourself, being merciful, give (that capital).
the Lord gives (us) capital and has (us) trade, O brother.
(The one who) has earned this profit, the wealth of the Lord's devotion, has pleased the mind of the Lord, the true Banker.
(The one who), repeating the Lord's Name, has loaded the Lord's merchandise: Jam, the toll-collector, has not come near him.
The traders who deal in other trade (suffer) pain in the endless waves of Maya;
to whatever trade the Lord has set them, such is the fruit they have received.
That person alone trades in (the Name of) the Lord, Har Har, to whom God, in his kindness, gives (it).
O servant Nanak, (the one who) has served the Lord, the Banker, is never again called (by him) to account. ॥4॥
165.4: Raag Gauri Bairagan, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
As a mother nurses (the child in) her womb, hoping for a son,
(thinking) he will grow up and earn money and give it, so that (we) may enjoy comfort and pleasure,
so the Lord keeps his servant's love alive, himself giving (him) the support of his hand.
O my Ram, O Lord, O my Master, protect me, a fool.
Your servant's praise is your own glory.
There is bliss in the temple, in the home (of the heart), when the praise of the Lord, Har Har, pleases the mind;
all sweet flavours fill (his) mouth when he sings the Lord's praises;
the Lord's servant is guardian and support to twenty-one generations; he sets the whole world free.
Whatever has been done, the Lord has done; (all) is the Lord's glory.
O Lord, the beings are yours, and you are at work (in them); the Lord (himself) has (his) worship done.
The Lord lets (us) find the treasures of devotion, and himself hands them out.
What cleverness can a slave bought in the market (show)?
If (the Lord) seats him on a throne, he is (still) the Lord's slave; even the grass-cutter the Lord makes to utter the Lord's Name.
Servant Nanak is the Lord's slave; (this is) the Lord's glory. ॥4॥
166.1: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
The farmer tills the land and longs (for the crop) with all his heart;
he yokes the plough and toils, (thinking,) my son and daughter will eat;
so the Lord's servant repeats (the Name of) the Lord, Har Har, and at the end the Lord sets him free.
Raise me, a fool, to the highest state, O my Ram;
O Lord, set me to the work of serving the Guru, the True Guru.
Taking horses, the merchant hurries off to trade;
he earns wealth, hopes (for more), and increases his attachment to Maya;
so the Lord's servant utters (the Name of) the Lord, Har Har, and uttering the Lord finds peace.
The shopkeeper sits in his shop and plies his trade, hoarding poison;
the attachment is false, the display is of falsehood, and he clings to the false;
so the Lord's servant has gathered the wealth of the Lord, and takes (the Name of) the Lord with him as provisions for the journey.
This family is attachment to Maya, a noose in the love of another;
through the Guru's teaching that person crosses over who is the servant of (the Lord's) servants.
Servant Nanak has meditated on the Naam; through the Guru, the light has dawned (within). ॥4॥
166.2: Raag Gauri Bairagan, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Always, day and night, (man) is greedy, and wanders, led astray (by Maya);
(like) the man pressed into forced labour, who goes about at his unpaid toil with a load lifted on his head.
The one who serves the Guru the Lord has set to the work of (his own true) home.
O my Ram, break the bonds of Maya and set (us) to the work of (our true) home,
that we may ever sing the Lord's praises, merged in the Lord's Name.
A man serves a king, the lord of men, all for the sake of wealth;
(the king) either puts him in chains, or exacts a fine, or the king (himself) dies.
Blessed, blessed is the True Guru's service, and fruitful, for through it, repeating the Name of the Lord, Har Har, one has found the Lord's peace.
Every day, in many ways, trade is done for profit, for the sake of Maya;
when it yields a profit, there is joy in the mind; at a loss one dies (of grief).
The one who goes into partnership with the Guru in virtues finds peace for ever and ever.
However great the hunger for other pleasures and tastes, just so great a hunger strikes again.
The one on whom the Lord himself shows grace sells his head to the Guru.
O servant Nanak, (the one who is) filled with the Lord's sweet essence feels no hunger again. ॥4॥
167.1: Raag Gauri Bairagan, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
In my mind and heart, O Lord, is ever this hope: how may I see the sight of you, O Lord?
He who kindled this love knows it: to my mind and heart the Lord is very dear.
I am a sacrifice to my Guru, who has united me, the one cut off, with my Creator.
O my Ram, I, a sinner, have sought (your) refuge, (fallen) at your door, O Lord,
in the hope that, bestowing your grace, you may some day unite me, without virtue, (with yourself).
My faults are many, very many; (committed) again and again, O Lord, they are beyond counting.
You, O Lord, Har Har, are full of virtue and merciful; you yourself forgive, O Lord, when it pleases you.
Me, a wrongdoer, (the Lord) has kept safe in the Guru's company; he has given the teaching, and the Lord's Name sets free.
What virtues of yours can I tell, O my True Guru? When I utter (the word) Guru, I am lost in wonder.
Would anyone else protect wrongdoers like me, as the True Guru has protected and freed me?
You, the Guru, are my father; you, the Guru, alone are my mother; you, the Guru, are my kinsman, my friend and helper.
The state I was in, O my True Guru, that state, O Lord, you yourself know.
I wandered about, cast aside, and no one asked after me; through the company of the Guru, the True Guru, this worm has been raised to honour.
Blessed, blessed is the Guru of servant Nanak, meeting whom all sorrows and torments have ended. ॥4॥
167.2: Raag Gauri Bairagan, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
My soul is lured by gold and woman; attachment to Maya is sweet (to me).
In houses, mansions and horses (I take) delight; my mind is fixed on other pleasures.
The Lord God does not come to (my) mind; how can I be set free, O my Lord King?
O my Ram, such are my lowly deeds, O my Lord.
O Lord, Har Har, full of virtue and merciful, show grace and forgive all my faults.
I have no beauty, no caste, no good ways.
With what face shall I speak? I am without virtue, and I have not repeated your Name.
I, a sinner, have been saved in the Guru's company; (this is) the True Guru's goodness.
(God) has given all: soul and body, mouth and nose, and water to use;
he has given grain for food and cloth for wear, and countless pleasures to enjoy;
the one who gave them does not come to mind; I, a beast, take it all to be my own doing.
All that happens is your doing; you know the inner heart (of all).
What can we poor creatures do? All is your play, O Master.
Servant Nanak, bought in the market, is a slave of the Lord's slaves. ॥4॥
168.1: Raag Gauri Bairagan, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
As a mother gives birth to a son, then rears him and keeps him within her sight;
indoors and out, she feeds him by the mouthful and fondles him every moment:
so the True Guru keeps the Guru's Sikh in the Lord's love, with affection.
O my Lord, we are children of the Lord God, and know nothing.
Blessed, blessed is the Guru, the True Guru, the teacher, who gave us the Lord's teaching and made us wise.
As the (crane) clad in white feathers wheels and flies about in the sky,
yet keeps her mind on the young she has left behind, and always holds them close in her heart:
so the True Guru gives his Sikh the love of the Lord, Har Har, and the Guru holds the Sikh as dear as his own life.
As there are the shears of the thirty-two teeth, and within them (the Lord) keeps the tongue of flesh and blood (safe):
one may think it lies in the hands of the flesh or of the shears, but all is in the Lord's power.
So, though people slander the Sants, the Lord keeps the honour of his servant.
O brother, let none of you think that anything lies in anyone's hands; all is what (the Lord) does and causes to be done.
Old age, death, fever, headache and curse: all are in the Lord's power; nothing can strike unless the Lord makes it strike.
Meditate always, in mind and in consciousness, on such a Name of the Lord, O servant Nanak, which sets one free at the very last moment. ॥4॥
168.2: Raag Gauri Bairagan, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
He whose meeting brings bliss to the mind is the one to be called the True Guru:
the mind's double-mindedness is destroyed, and the Lord, the supreme state, is attained.
How may I meet my beloved True Guru?
Every moment I bow (to him): how may I meet my Perfect Guru?
In his grace the Lord has united me with my Perfect True Guru.
The longings of (his) servant are fulfilled, taking the dust (of the feet) of the True Guru.
One should meet that True Guru who makes devotion to the Lord firm (within), and with whom one hears of devotion to the Lord.
(With him) no loss ever comes; the Lord's profit is made firm every day.
(The Guru) in whose heart there is blossoming, and no love of another:
O Nanak, meeting that Guru one is saved, and (such people) sing the Lord's praises. ॥4॥
168.3: Raag Gauri Poorbi, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
The merciful Lord God has shown mercy: the Lord's word (of praise) is in my mind, my body and my mouth.
Through the Guru, the colour has become very deep; the bodice (of my heart) is soaked in the Lord's colour.
I am the handmaid of my Lord God.
When my mind came to accept the Lord, he made the whole world my servant, unbought.
Reflect and discern, O Sants, O brothers: search your hearts, look, and seek.
All is the form of the Lord, Har Har; (his) light is in all creation; the Lord dwells near, the Lord is close by.
The Lord, Har Har, dwells near the whole world, the infinite, immeasurable Being.
The Perfect Guru has made the Lord, Har Har, manifest (within me); for a price, I have sold the Guru my head.
O dear Lord, you are within and without; I have come to your refuge; you are the great Being, the greatest of all.
Servant Nanak sings the Lord's praises night and day, having met the True Guru, the Guru, the go-between. ॥4॥
169.1: Raag Gauri Poorbi, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
O Life of the world, boundless Master, Lord of the universe, all-pervading Being, Creator:
on whatever path you prompt us, Master, on that path we go.
O Lord, my mind is steeped in the Lord.
Joining the Sat Sangat, we have found the Lord's sweet essence, and we stay merged in the Name of the Lord.
The Name of the Lord, Har Har, is the one medicine in the world; the Name of the Lord, Har Har, brings peace.
All the sins and faults of those are destroyed who, through the Guru's teaching, savour the Lord's sweet essence.
Those on whose foreheads the writ was written from the beginning bathe in the Guru, the pool of contentment.
All the filth of evil-mindedness is gone from those who are dyed in the colour of the Lord's Name.
O Lord, you yourself, you alone, are God and Master; no other giver is as great as you.
Servant Nanak lives when he takes the Naam; the Lord is meditated on by the Lord's grace. ॥4॥
169.2: Raag Gauri Poorbi, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Show grace, O Life of the world, O Giver, that my mind may stay absorbed in the Lord.
The True Guru has given me (his) most pure word; repeating Har Har Har, my mind rejoices.
O Lord, the True Lord has pierced my mind and body (with his love).
Death, in whose mouth the whole world is seized: through the word of the Guru, the True Guru, O Lord, we have been saved (from it).
Those who have no love for the Lord are Saakats, foolish and frail men.
For them birth and death are a very heavy load; dying again and again, they rot in filth.
You are merciful, the protector of those who come to your refuge: give me this gift, Lord; I beg it of you.
Make me a slave of the Lord's slaves, and let my mind dance and dance (in delight).
God, the Master, is himself the great banker; we are his traders.
My mind, body and soul, all this capital, are yours, O God, the true banker of servant Nanak. ॥4॥
169.3: Raag Gauri Poorbi, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
You are merciful, the destroyer of all pain: hear one prayer of mine, and give it your ear.
Unite me with that True Guru, my very life, through whom you, Lord and Master, are known.
O Lord, I have taken the True Guru to be the Supreme Lord.
I was foolish, ignorant, of impure mind; through the word of the Guru, the True Guru, I have come to know the Lord.
Of all the tastes and other delights I have tried, every one is insipid, utterly insipid.
Meeting the True Guru, I have tasted the Lord's Name, the nectar; it is sweet as sugarcane juice.
Those whom the Guru, the True Guru, has not met are Saakats, foolish and crazed.
A lot without grace was set for them from the beginning; like (moths) seeing the lamp, they burn in attachment.
Those whom you, in your mercy, unite (with the Guru) are set to the service of the Lord, Har Har.
O servant Nanak, repeating Har Har Har they shine forth; taking the Guru's teaching as their understanding, they merge in the Naam. ॥4॥
170.1: Raag Gauri Poorbi, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
O my mind, that God, the Master, is always with you; say, where can one run from the Lord?
The Lord, the True God, himself forgives; when the Lord himself sets free, one is set free.
O my mind, repeat Har Har Har; let him be repeated within the mind.
O my mind, hurry to the True Guru's refuge; one is set free by following the Guru, the True Guru.
O my mind, serve that God, the giver of all peace, by serving whom one dwells in one's own home (within).
Through the Guru, go and find your own home; let the Lord's praise be rubbed, as sandalwood is rubbed.
O my mind, the praise of the Lord, Har Har Har Har Har, is sublime; earning the Lord's profit, one rejoices in the mind.
When the Lord, Har Har, himself in mercy gives (it), then the nectar, the Lord's essence, is tasted.
O my mind, those who, without the Naam, are attached to another are Saakats, and are throttled by Jam.
Those Saakats who have forgotten the Naam are thieves; O mind, do not go near them or touch them.
O my mind, serve the unseen, stainless Lord, Narhari, by serving whom the account is cleared.
O servant Nanak, those whom the Lord God has made complete do not fall short by a masa's weight, not for an instant. ॥5॥
170.2: Raag Gauri Poorbi, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
God, my very breath is in your hands; my soul and body, all of it, is yours.
Be kind, Lord, and grant me the sight of you; my mind and body yearn for it deeply.
O Lord, my mind and body yearn to meet the Lord.
When the merciful Guru showed a little grace, my Lord God came and met me.
Master, whatever passes in my mind and heart, that state of mine, Lord, is known to you yourself.
May I repeat the Naam night and day and find peace; I live ever in hope of you, Lord.
The Guru, the True Guru, the Giver, pointed out the path; my Lord God came and met me.
Bliss abides night and day, by great good fortune; every hope of (his) servant has been fulfilled.
O Master of the world, Ruler of the universe, Creator: all is in the Lord's power.
Servant Nanak has come to your refuge: O Lord, guard your servant's honour. ॥4॥
170.3: Raag Gauri Poorbi, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
This mind, chasing many pleasures, does not stay still even for a moment; it runs and runs in all ten directions, wandering.
By great good fortune I have found the Perfect Guru; he gave me the Lord's mantra, and the mind has come to rest.
