O Lord, I am called the True Guru's slave.
On my forehead (his) mark has been branded; I have run up a great debt to the Guru.
He has done me great kindness and good; he has carried me across the world-ocean, so hard to cross.
Those in whose hearts there is no love for the Lord only tie knots that are false.
As paper falls apart in water, so the manmukhs waste away in the womb (of birth after birth).
We have known nothing, nor do we know what lies ahead; as the Lord keeps us, so we stand.
O Guru, we err and fall short: show us your grace; servant Nanak is called your dog. ॥4॥
171.1: Raag Gauri Poorbi, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
The city (of the body) is filled to the brim with lust and anger; meeting the Saadh (the Guru), these are smashed to pieces.
By the writ of the past the Guru has been found, and loving absorption (liv) in the Lord is set like a jewel in the mind.
Join your palms before the Saadh: this is a great merit.
Lie stretched out before him in prostration: this is a great merit.
The Saakats (those who have turned from God) have not known the taste of the Lord's sweet essence; within them is the thorn of Haumai (ego).
The further they walk, the more it pricks and they suffer pain, and they bear the rod of Jamkaal (death) upon their heads.
The Lord's servants remain merged in the Name of the Lord, Har Har; they have cut away the pain of birth and death in the world.
They have found the imperishable, all-pervading Supreme God, and great is their glory across the lands and universes.
We are poor and meek, God, and we are yours; save us, O Lord, save us: you are the greatest of the great.
Servant Nanak's support and prop is the Naam; in the Lord's Name alone has peace been found. ॥4॥
171.2: Raag Gauri Poorbi, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Within this fortress (of the body) is the Lord, the Sovereign Ram; but the stubborn one finds no taste (of him).
When the Lord, merciful to the meek, showed his favour, the Lord was tasted and seen through the Guru's Shabad.
O Lord, the Kirtan of the Lord, with attention fixed on the Guru, is sweet.
The Lord is beyond reach, beyond the senses, the Supreme Lord; (he is found) by meeting the True Guru and holding to (him), the intermediary.
Those to whose hearts the Guru's words are pleasing: before them (the Lord) is brought and served.
The manmukh's heart is very hard; within them is blackness, pitch black.
Give a snake ever so much milk to drink: search it and turn it over, and poison comes out.
O Lord God, bring and unite me with the Guru, the Saadh, that I may grind the Shabad as the Garur (antidote) and take it into my mouth.
Servant Nanak is the Guru's bondsman and servant; joined to the Sangat, what was bitter has turned sweet. ॥4॥
171.3: Raag Gauri Poorbi, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
I have sold my body before the Perfect Guru, for the sake of the Lord, Har Har.
The True Guru, the Giver, has made the Naam firm within me; on my face and forehead good fortune has dawned.
O Lord, through the Guru's teaching, attention is fixed on the Lord.
The beautiful Lord, the Sovereign Ram, pervades every heart; through the Guru's Shabad, through the Guru, attention is fixed (on him).
I would cut up my mind and body and give them to the Guru; by the Guru's words my doubt and fear are put to flight.
Into the darkness (the Guru) has brought and lit lamps; through the Guru's wisdom, through the Guru, attention is fixed (on him).
The darkness of ignorance is utterly destroyed; the treasure is found in the home (within), and the mind is awake.
The Saakats are hunters, clinging to Maya; Jam keeps them in his sight.
They have not sold their heads before the True Guru; those wretched ones come and go.
Hear my prayer, God, my Master: I beg for the refuge of God, the Lord.
The Guru is servant Nanak's honour and standing; he has sold his head before the True Guru. ॥5॥
172.1: Raag Gauri Poorbi, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
We were proud, our minds full of pride and ignorance; meeting the Guru, self-conceit has been lost.
The disease of Haumai is gone, and peace is found; blessed, blessed is the Guru, the Lord and King.
O Lord, through the Guru's word the Lord is found.
In my heart is love for the Sovereign Lord; the Guru has shown me the road, the path.
My soul and body, all, (I have placed) before the True Guru, who has brought me, separated as I was, into the Lord's embrace.
Within me arose the love to see (him); the Guru has shown (him) to me, right there with my heart.
The bliss of Sahaj has arisen in my mind; I have sold myself before the Guru.
I committed many offences and sins; doing wicked deeds, I stole like a thief.
Now Nanak has come to your refuge: O Lord, keep his honour, as it pleases you, Lord. ॥4॥
172.2: Raag Gauri Poorbi, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Through the Guru's teaching the unstruck Shabad resounds; through the Guru's teaching the mind sings (his praise).
By great good fortune I have had the sight of the Guru; blessed, blessed is the Guru, who fixes (our) attention (on the Lord).
Through the Guru, one fixes loving attention on the Lord.
My Master is the Perfect True Guru; my mind does the Guru's work.
I wash the feet of the Guru, rubbing them again and again, who tells (me) the story of the Lord, Har Har.
In the heart, through the Guru's teaching, is the Lord, the home of all delights; the tongue sings the Lord's praises.
Relishing and relishing, the mind is sated with the Lord's essence, and hunger never strikes again.
One may try countless ways, very many, but without (his) grace the Naam is not found.
On servant Nanak the Lord has shown grace; through the Guru's teaching he makes the Naam firm in (his) understanding. ॥4॥
172.3: Raag Gauri Majh, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
O dear soul, through the Guru meditate on the Name: this is the deed (for you to do).
Make the (Guru's) wisdom your mother, make that wisdom your life, and keep the Name of Ram on your lips.
Make contentment your father, and the Purakh who is never born your Guru.
I have met the Guru, the Yogi (joined to God), the Purakh, and I delight in his love.
The Guru is steeped in the Lord's love, ever free of all desire.
O fortunate one, meet him, (the Guru,) skilled and all-wise.
My mind and body are drenched in the Lord's love.
Come, O Sants, let us gather and meditate on the Name;
in the Sangat, ever reap the profit of the Name.
Serving the Sants, let us put the Amrit (of the Name) into our mouths.
Meet (the Lord), by the grace written for you from his court of old.
In Sawan the cloud has spread over the world with its Amrit (of rain);
the peacock of the mind calls out sweetly, having taken the (Guru's) Shabad into its mouth.
The Lord's Amrit has rained down within, the Lord, the King, has been met,
and (the mind of) servant Nanak is dyed in love. ॥4॥
173.1: Raag Gauri Majh, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Come, my companion, let us make virtues our charms (to win the Husband Lord),
and, joining the Sants, enjoy the love and delight (of his union).
(Those in whose) minds the lamp of the Guru's wisdom ever burns,
have met him, melting (with love), since the Lord was pleased.
Love for the Lord, my darling, has taken hold of my mind and body.
May the True Guru, the go-between, unite me with my Friend.
I would give my mind to the Sants, (that they) may unite me with my God.
To the Lord I am ever a sacrifice.
Dwell, my beloved; dwell, O my Govind; O Lord, show your grace and dwell in my mind.
I have received the fruit my mind longed for, O my Govind; seeing the perfect Guru, (my mind) has blossomed.
The happy wife has received the Lord's Name, O my Govind; in her mind are bliss and gladness day and night.
The fortunate ones have found the Lord, O my Govind; ever reaping the profit (of the Name), their minds laugh with joy.
The Lord himself creates (beings), the Lord himself watches over (them), the Lord himself has set (them) to their tasks.
Some eat of his gifts, which never run short; to some (he) has given but a pinch.
Some sit on thrones as kings, ever at ease; some (he) has made to beg for alms.
Everywhere (your) one Word, (your Hukam,) is at work, O my Govind; servant Nanak has meditated on the Name. ॥4॥
173.2: Raag Gauri Majh, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Within my mind, within my mind, O my Govind, within my mind I am dyed in the Lord's love.
The Lord's love is with (each one), yet it is not perceived, O my Govind; the perfect Guru makes the unseen (Lord) seen.
(In whom) the Name of the Lord, Har Har, has shone forth, O my Govind, all (their) poverty and pain are gone.
(Those who) have attained the supreme state of the Lord, O my Govind, the fortunate ones, remain absorbed in the Name.
With the eyes, my beloved, with the eyes, O my Govind, only some rare one has seen the Lord God with the eyes.
My mind and body are deeply sad (in longing), O my Govind; without the Lord, (I,) the bride, have withered.
Meeting the Sants, I have found (him), O my Govind, my Lord God, my friend and companion.
The Lord, the Life of the world, came and met (me), O my Govind; now (my) night (of life) goes by in peace.
O Sants, unite me with my Lord God, my friend; a hunger (for him) has seized my mind and body.
I cannot live without seeing (you), my Beloved; the Lord has set the pain of separation within me.
The Lord, the King, is my dear friend; (when) the Guru unites (me with him), my mind comes alive.
The hope of my mind and body is fulfilled, O my Govind; meeting the Lord, my mind is full of rejoicing.
A sacrifice, O my Govind, a sacrifice, my beloved: I am ever a sacrifice to you.
In my mind and body is love for the Beloved, O my Govind; O Lord, keep this capital of mine safe.
Unite me with the True Guru, the go-between, O my Govind, who will guide me and unite me with the Lord.
By (your) kindness I have received the Lord's Name, O my Govind; servant Nanak is in your refuge. ॥4॥
174.1: Raag Gauri Majh, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Maker of wondrous plays, O my Govind; maker of wondrous plays, my beloved: my Lord God works wondrous plays.
The Lord himself brings Kanh into being, O my Govind; the Lord himself is the gopi who searches (for him).
The Lord himself enjoys (the world through) every body, O my Govind; he himself is the one who relishes and the one who enjoys.
The all-wise Lord does not go astray, O my Govind; he himself is the True Guru, the Yogi (untouched by pleasures).
(The Lord) himself creates the world, O my Govind; the Lord himself plays in many colours.
Some (he) gives pleasures to enjoy, O my Govind; some go about naked, utterly bare.
(The Lord) himself creates the world, O my Govind; all beg of him, and the Lord gives his gifts.
The Name is the support of the devotees, O my Govind; they ask the Lord (only) for the Lord's sublime story.
The Lord himself (moves his devotees to) worship him, O my Govind; the Lord fulfils the longing in his devotees' minds.
(The Lord) himself is at work in the water and on the land, O my Govind; he pervades (all), and is not far.
Within and without is the Lord himself, O my Govind; the Lord himself fills (every place).
The Lord, the all-pervading Ram, has spread out (this world), O my Govind; the Lord himself watches over it, ever present.
Within (all), the Lord, as the breath, is the instrument, O my Govind; as the Lord himself plays it, so it sounds.
Within (all) is the treasure of the Lord's Name, O my Govind; through the Guru's Shabad the Lord God resounds (within).
(The Lord) himself brings (beings) to his refuge, O my Govind; the Lord is the guardian of his devotees' honour.
O fortunate one, join the Sangat, O my Govind; O servant Nanak, through the Name (life's) task is accomplished. ॥4॥
175.1: Raag Gauri Majh, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
The Lord has set in me the longing of separation for the Lord's Name.
(Only if) my friend, the Lord God, meets me do I find peace.
O my mother, it is by seeing the Lord God that I live.
The Lord's Name is my companion and my brother.
Dear Sants, sing the praises of my Lord God.
Through the Guru, meditate on the Name, dear ones: (this is) great good fortune.
The Name of the Lord, Har Har, is my very breath of life.
(With it) there are no more rounds in the ocean of the world.
How may I see the Lord God? (This) yearning fills my mind and body.
Dear Sants, unite (me) with the Lord; love (for him) has taken hold of my mind.
Through the Guru's Shabad the Lord, the beloved King, is found.
O fortunate one, meditate on (his) Name.
In my mind and body is a great hope for God, Govind.
Dear Sants, unite (me) with the Lord, with God, Govind, who is close at hand.
Through the True Guru's teaching the Name ever shines (within).
The hope in servant Nanak's mind has been fulfilled. ॥4॥
175.2: Raag Gauri Majh, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Only when I meet the Name, the beloved I am parted from, do I live.
Within the mind is the Amrit; through the Guru's teaching I take in the Lord's (Amrit).
(My) mind is dyed in the Lord's love; I ever drink the Lord's nectar.
Having found the Lord in my mind, I live.
My mind and body are struck by love, the Lord's arrow.
The Lord, the all-wise Purakh, is my beloved, my friend.
The Guru, the Sant, unites (me) with the Lord, skilled and all-wise.
I am a sacrifice to the Name.
I ask for word of the Lord, Har Har, my friend, the Lord my companion.
Tell me of the Lord, dear Sants; I am searching for the Lord.
(When) the True Guru, well pleased, shows the way, I find the Lord,
and merge in the Lord's Name, in the Name alone.
The ache of love, the pain of separation from the Lord, has struck me.
O Guru, fulfil my heart's wish, that I may put the Amrit (of the Name) into my mouth.
O Lord, be kind, that I may meditate on the Lord's Name,
and (I,) servant Nanak, may receive the Lord's nectar. ॥4॥
175.3: Raag Gauri Guareri, Chaupade, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
By what means does true well-being come, my brother?
How is the Lord, Ram, our helper, to be found?
There is no well-being in the household, nor in (holding that) all this wealth is mine,
nor in lofty mansions and lovely shade.
In false greed (for these, one) has wasted this life.
(One) is delighted at the sight of elephants and horses,
gathers armies, (keeps) deputies and royal attendants,
(yet) round (his) neck is the rope, the noose of Haumai.
(One) holds sway over all (the earth) in the ten directions,
enjoys revels and pleasures and many women;
(but it is) like a king who becomes a beggar in a dream.
The True Guru has shown me the one (true) well-being:
the Lord's devotees are glad of whatever the Lord does.
O servant Nanak, (the devotee) kills Haumai and merges (in the Lord).
In this way true well-being comes, my brother;
thus is the Lord, Ram, our helper, found.
176.1: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Why should one wander in doubt? What is there to doubt,
when he alone pervades the water, the land and the sky?
Delivered are the Gurmukhs; the manmukhs have lost their honour.
The one whom the merciful Lord, Ram, himself protects,
no other can come up to.
In all, the one Infinite (Lord) is at work;
so sleep in peace, free of care.
The manmukhs, who thirst for what is other (than God), are dead (within).
They wander through many births, as written from the Lord's court by (their) deeds.
everywhere I have seen God (Brahm) shining forth.
The Lord has fulfilled servant Nanak's hope. ॥4॥
176.2: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
In many births (you) were a worm and a moth,
in many births an elephant, a fish, a deer,
in many births (you) became a bird and a snake,
in many births (you) were a horse and an ox under the yoke.
Meet the Master of the world: (now) is your turn to meet him.
After a very long time this (human) body has been given (to you).
In many births (you) were made rocks and mountains,
in many births (you) were lost from the womb before birth,
in many births (you) were brought forth as plants;
(so you) were made to wander through the eighty-four lakh forms of life.
(Now) you have been granted (human) birth: in the Saadh Sangat
do seva, and by the Guru's teaching dwell on the Lord, Har Har.
Give up pride, falsehood and arrogance.
If (you) die while living, (you) will be accepted in the Lord's court.
Whatever has been (and is to be) comes from you, (O Lord);
there is no other able to do anything.
You are met only when you unite (one with yourself).
Says Nanak: sing the virtues of the Lord, Har Har. ॥4॥
176.3: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(O brother), in the field of deeds (this human life) sow the Naam,
and your task (in life) will be fulfilled.
You will gain the fruit that the fear of Jam is ended,
(if) you sing day after day the virtues and praise of the Lord, Har Har.
Enshrine the Name of the Lord, Har Har, within your heart,
and set your affairs right without delay.
Be ever alert, with your mind on your God;
then you will receive honour in the Lord's court.
Give up all clever arguments and cunning,
and fall at the feet of the Sants.
He in whose hands all beings are
is never parted (from anyone); he is with all.
Leave (other) devices and take hold of his shelter,
and in an instant you will be set free.
Know him to be ever near,
and accept God's command as true.
By the Guru's word, erase your self-conceit.
O Nanak, repeat the Name of the Lord, Har Har; repeat this chant. ॥4॥
177.1: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The Guru's word is ever imperishable.
By the Guru's word, the noose of Jam is cut.
The Guru's word stays with the soul;
by the Guru's word one remains steeped in the Lord's love.
(O brother), what the Guru has given is of use to the mind;
hold what the Sant (the Guru) has done to be true and lasting.
The Guru's word is unshakeable; nothing can pierce it.
By the Guru's word, doubt and the sense of separateness are cut away.
The Guru's word never goes anywhere (it never fails);
by the Guru's word one sings the virtues of the Lord.
The Guru's word goes along with the soul;
the Guru's word is a master to those who have none.
By the Guru's word one does not fall into hell;
by the Guru's word the tongue savours the Amrit (of the Name).
The Guru's word is manifest in the world;
by the Guru's word one does not come away defeated.
To the servant on whom (the Lord) himself is kind,
O Nanak, the True Guru is ever merciful. ॥4॥
177.2: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
He who made (me) a jewel out of dust,
who took care to keep (me) safe in the womb,
who gave (me) glory and greatness:
on that God I meditate at all hours.
O all-pervading Lord, (grant that) I may obtain the dust of the feet of the holy,
and, meeting the Guru, meditate on my Master.
He who made (me) a speaker out of a fool,
who gave (me) understanding where there was none,
by whose grace I obtain the nine treasures:
that God does not leave my mind.
He who gave a place to (me), the homeless,
who gave honour to (me), the dishonoured,
who fulfilled my every hope:
him I remember day and night, with every breath and every morsel.
He by whose grace (my) noose of Maya is cut,
(and) by the Guru's grace the bitter poison has become Amrit:
says Nanak, nothing can be done by this (mortal) of himself;
I praise (him), the Protector. ॥4॥
177.3: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
In his refuge there is neither fear nor sorrow;
nothing will happen outside his power.
I have given up cleverness, (pride in) strength and intellect, and vice;
(God) is the protector of his own servant.
Repeat, O my mind, the Lord's Name, Ram Ram, with love;
at home and abroad he is ever with you.
Keep his support in your mind;
taste the Guru's Shabad, the sweet essence of Amrit.
Tell me, of what use are other efforts?
God himself, in his grace, saves (one's) honour.
Tell me, what is a mortal? What is his power?
All the clamour of Maya is false.
The Master is the one who does and causes all to be done;
he knows the inner being of every heart.
Of all comforts, this is the true comfort:
take the Guru's teaching into your mind.
The one whose loving attention is held on the Lord's Name,
says Nanak, is blessed, and greatly fortunate. ॥4॥
178.1: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Hearing the Lord's story, (those who) have washed off (the mind's) filth
have become most pure, and (gained) a mountain of peace.
By great good fortune (those who) have found the Saadh Sangat
have been dyed with love for the Supreme Lord.
(The Guru) has saved the servant who repeats the Name of the Lord, Har Har;
the Guru has carried (him) across the ocean of fire.
Singing Kirtan, (their) minds have been cooled;
the sins of birth after birth are gone.
(They) have seen all the treasures within (their own) mind;
why would they now go searching (outside)?
When their own God became merciful,
the servant's toil bore its full fruit.
Cutting (their) bonds, (God) made (them) his own servants,
through remembering, remembering, ever remembering the treasure of virtues.
The One is in (their) mind; the One is in every place;
the Perfect One is filling all places.
The perfect Guru has dispelled all (their) doubt.
Remembering the Lord, O Nanak, (they) have found peace. ॥4॥
178.2: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Those who died before are left behind (forgotten);
those who survive stand with their loins girded (for the race after Maya).
The affairs in which those (dead) were entangled,
to the Maya of those same affairs these (living) cling twice as tightly as they did.
That hour (of death) never comes to (the mortal's) mind;
he clings to that very thing which is bound to perish.
The fool's body is bound by hopes;
he is wrapped up in lust, anger and attachment.
Dharam Raj stands over (his) head,
(yet) he eats the poison (of Maya), taking it to be sweet.
(He says:) I will bind (my enemy), I will settle my score;
who dares set foot on my land?
I am a pandit, I am shrewd and wise.
(But) the ignorant one does not know the Creator.
(God) alone knows his own state and his own extent;
what can anyone say? What can one describe in words?
(O Lord), to whatever you attach (beings), to that they must be attached;
everyone must ask for his own good.
(O Lord), everything is yours; you are the Creator;
you have no end, no near shore and no far one.
Grant your servant this gift:
that Nanak may never forget the Naam. ॥5॥
178.3: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
By countless efforts, release (from Maya's hold) does not come;
much cleverness only heaps on a heavier load.
(The one who) serves the Lord with pure love
(goes) with honour to God's court.
O my mind, take hold of the shelter of the Lord's Name,
and the hot wind (of suffering) will not touch you.
As a ship (carries one) in the fearful ocean,
as lamps give light in the dark,
as fire takes away the pain of cold,
so, repeating the Naam, peace comes to the mind.
The thirst of your mind will be quenched,
every hope will be fulfilled,
your mind will not waver;
repeat the Amrit Naam through the Guru, O friend.
Only that person obtains the medicine of the Naam
whom (the Lord) himself, in his grace, causes to receive it.
The one in whose heart the Name of the Lord, Har Har, dwells,
his pain and suffering, O Nanak, run away. ॥4॥
179.1: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Amassing great wealth, the mind is not sated;
beholding many beauties, it is not satisfied.
(The mortal) is entangled in sons and wife, thinking them his own;
(but) that (wealth and beauty) perishes, and they (sons and wife) become a heap of ashes.
Without worship of the Lord, I see (people) wailing.
Cursed is the body and cursed the wealth of those imbued with Maya.
As bags of money are set on the head of a man pressed into forced labour:
they go to the master's house, and he bears only the pain.
As in a dream one becomes a king and sits (on the throne),
(but) when he opens his eyes, his affairs come to nothing.
As a watchman (keeps guard) over another's field:
the field belongs to its owner, and the watchman gets up and goes.
For that field the watchman frets and worries,
(yet) nothing of it comes into his hands.
The kingdom is his (God's), and the dream too is his;
he who gave Maya has also attached the craving for it.
He himself destroys, and he himself sets right.
Nanak's prayer is before God. ॥4॥
179.2: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
I have seen Maya of many colours in many ways;
clever things have been written with pen and paper;
being a chief, a king and a khan has been tried and seen;
(yet) by these the mind is not satisfied.
O Sants, tell me of that peace
by which (my) thirst may be quenched; satisfy (my) mind.
Riding horses swift as the wind and elephants,
perfume and sandalwood, and the bed of a beautiful woman,
the plays of actors and the songs sung on the stage:
in these (too) the mind has found no contentment.
A throne, the adornments of a royal court, and carpets,
fruits of every kind and lovely gardens,
the taste for hunting and the pastimes of kings:
(with these too) the mind is not at ease; all this striving is a deception.
In their kindness the Sants have told (me) the truth:
all comforts and this bliss are found (thus),
by singing the Lord's Kirtan in the Saadh Sangat.
Says Nanak, (this) is found by great good fortune.
One who has the wealth of the Lord (in the heart), he alone is at ease;
by God's grace (one) comes to meet the Saadh Sangat. ॥12॥
179.3: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The mortal thinks this body is his own,
and clings to it again and again.
(While) the noose of children, wife and household (is around his neck),
one cannot become a servant of the Lord (Raam).
What is that way by which (one) may sing the Lord's virtues?
What is that understanding by which (one) may cross over this Maya?
What is for his good, he takes to be bad;
if (anyone) tells the truth, he takes it to be like poison.
He does not know victory from defeat:
such is the way of the world of the Saakats.
The madman drinks what is deadly poison,
and takes the Amrit of the Name to be bitter.
He does not come near the Saadh Sangat,
(and so) he wanders through the round of the eighty-four lakh (forms of life).
(The Lord) has snared the birds (the beings) in the one net (of Maya);
relishing and relishing, they indulge in pleasures of many kinds.
Says Nanak, the one to whom (the Lord) has become kind,
his snares the Perfect Guru has cut. ॥4॥
180.1: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(O God,) by your grace the path (of life) is found;
by God's grace the Naam is meditated on;
by God's grace (one's) bonds are loosed;
by your grace Haumai is broken.
When you yourself attach us, then we take to your service;
by ourselves nothing can be done, O Divine Lord.
If it pleases you, I sing the Bani (of your praise);
if it pleases you, I utter the True (Name);
if it pleases you, the True Guru's mercy (comes);
all comforts, O God, lie in your kindness.
What pleases you is the pure deed;
what pleases you is the true dharma.
All treasures and virtues are with you alone.
You are the Master; (your) servant prays to you (alone).
In the Lord's love mind and body become pure;
in the Sat Sangat I obtain every comfort.
(That) the mind stays dyed in your Name:
this Nanak has known to be (true) bliss. ॥4॥
180.2: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(O tongue,) all the other tastes you have tasted
have not taken away your thirst for even an instant.
If you taste the flavour of the Lord's sweet essence,
tasting it you will be lost in wonder.
O dear tongue, drink the Amrit;
steeped in this taste, you will be satisfied.
O tongue, sing the virtues of the Lord (Raam);
every moment meditate on the Lord, Har, Har, Har.
Let us listen to no other (talk), and go nowhere else;
the Saadh Sangat is found by great good fortune.
At all hours, O tongue, worship
the Supreme Lord, the unfathomable Master.
(So the tongue) is ever at ease, here and hereafter;
singing the Lord's virtues, the tongue becomes priceless.
(Though) the vegetation is in bloom, with fruit and flowers on the branches,
(the tongue) steeped in this taste never leaves it again.
No other tastes and flavours can equal it.
Says Nanak, the Guru has become (my) helper. ॥4॥
180.3: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The mind is a temple, and the body has been made (its) fence.
Within this very (temple) is the infinite treasure (of the Name);
within this very (temple) the Banker (the Lord) is heard to dwell.
Who is the trader who has credit there?
Whoever is a dealer in the jewel of the Naam
takes the Amrit for his food.
I offer (him my) mind and body, and serve (him);
(I ask:) what is that way by which (the Lord) is pleased?
Giving up mine and yours, I fall at (his) feet.
Who is that servant (of the Lord) who will strike (for me) the bargain (of the Name)?
By what means can (one) reach the Banker's mansion?
What is that way by which (the Banker) calls (one) within?
(O Lord,) you are the great Banker, with millions of traders.
Who is that giver who will take (me) and bring (me to you)?
Searching and searching, (I) have found (my) own home;
the priceless, lasting jewel has been shown (to me).
When in his grace the Banker united (me with himself),
says Nanak, (it was) on the Guru's credit. ॥4॥
181.1: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(The one in the Guru's refuge) stays in the love of the One night and day,
and knows God to be ever with (him).
He has made the Master's Name (the thing of) his daily use;
by the sight of the Lord he is fulfilled and content.
Those steeped in the Lord, their minds and bodies flourish;
they have fallen into the refuge of the Perfect Guru.
The lotus feet (of the Lord) are the support of (their) soul;
they behold the One alone, and obey (his) command.
the one (Name) alone is (their) trade; in the one (Name) alone they deal;
they know none other but the Formless One.
They are free of both joy and sorrow;
ever unattached (to Maya), they are joined (to the Lord) and live by the right way.
They are seen among all, (yet) they stay apart from all;
they keep their attention fixed on the Supreme Lord.
What glory of the Sants can I describe?
(Their glory) is unfathomable, beyond understanding; I know nothing of its measure.
O Supreme Lord, be gracious to me,
and grant Nanak the dust (of the feet) of the Sants. ॥4॥
181.2: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(O Lord,) you are my companion, you alone my friend;
you are my beloved; with you is my love.
You are my honour, you alone my ornament;
without you I cannot live even for an instant.
You are my darling, you are my very life;
you are my Master, you are my Khan (my lord).
As you keep (me), so I am to live;
what you say, that I am to do.
Wherever I look, there you dwell;
with my tongue I repeat your fearless Name.
You are my nine treasures, you (my) storehouse;
you are (my) joys and delights, you the support of (my) mind.
You are my glory; (my attention) is absorbed in you;
you are my shelter, you are my mainstay.
Within mind and body I have meditated on you alone;
your secret I have obtained from the Guru.
From the True Guru the One, the One alone, has been firmly implanted (in me);
servant Nanak (now) leans on the Lord, Har, Har, Har. ॥4॥
181.3: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(Maya) takes hold through the spread of joy and sorrow;
it takes hold through births in heaven and hell;
it takes hold of the rich, the poor, and (those who) look on (their own) glory;
as greed, the root of (all) ills, it takes hold.
Maya takes hold in many ways;
O God, the Sants live by your shelter.
(Maya) takes hold of one drunk with the ego-mind;
it takes hold of one dyed in (love of) children and wife;
it takes hold through elephants, horses and fine clothes;
it takes hold of one drunk with the wine of beauty and youth.
It takes hold of landowners, of paupers and of revellers;
it takes hold through songs and music heard in company;
it takes hold through beds, mansions and adornments;
as the five foes (lust and the rest) it takes hold in the darkness (of attachment).
It takes hold of one who does (his) deeds caught in Haumai;
it takes hold of the householder, it takes hold of the renunciate;
through ritual conduct, dealings and this (pride of) caste it takes hold;
it takes hold of everything, save (those) steeped in the Lord's love.
The Lord, the King, has cut the bonds of the Sants;
how can Maya take hold of them?
Says Nanak, the one who has obtained the dust (of the feet) of the Sants,
Maya does not come near him. ॥5॥
182.1: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Gazing at another's (beauty) with a corrupt eye is the sleep of the eyes;
the ears lie asleep, listening to talk of slander;
the tongue lies asleep in greed for sweet tastes;
and the mind lies asleep, spellbound by the marvel of Maya.
In this house (of the body) only a rare one stays awake;
he finds his own treasure (of life) whole and intact.
All the companions (the senses) are drunk on their own pleasures;
they have no awareness of their own house.
The five plundering highwaymen (lust, anger, greed, attachment and pride),
swindlers all, have fallen on the deserted town.
Neither father nor mother protects (one) from them;
neither friend nor brother protects (one) from them.
Neither wealth nor cleverness holds them back;
it is in the Saadh Sangat that those wicked ones are subdued.
Show me grace, O Saringpani:
the dust (of the feet) of the Sants is all treasures (to me).
In the True Guru's company the capital stays whole;
Nanak keeps awake in the love of the Supreme Lord.
Only that one stays awake on whom God is gracious;
this capital of his, his wealth and goods, stays whole. ॥20॥
182.2: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(God,) under whose sway are khans and sultans,
under whose sway is the whole world,
by whose doing all that happens comes about:
there is no one outside him.
(O brother,) make your plea before your own True Guru;
he will carry your tasks through to the end.
He whose court stands highest of all,
whose Name all his devotees lean on,
the perfect Master, present in all,
whose splendour graces every heart: (remember him).
The One, remembering whom the camp of sorrows is pulled down,
remembering whom Jam says nothing (to one),
remembering whom the withered turn green,
remembering whom sinking stones float across: (remember him).
Glory for ever to the assembly of the Sants;
the Name of the Lord, Har Har, sustains the life-breath of his servants.
Says Nanak, my prayer has been heard;
by the grace of the Sant (the Guru), I have been given a dwelling in the Naam. ॥4॥
183.1: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Through the sight of the True Guru the fire (of craving) is put out;
on meeting the True Guru, Haumai is slain;
in the True Guru's company the mind does not waver;
through the Guru, one speaks the Bani that is Amrit.
When (we) are dyed in the True One, the whole world (is seen as) the True One;
through the Guru God is known, and there is coolness and calm.
By the Sant's grace one repeats the Lord's Name;
by the Sant's grace one sings the Lord's Kirtan;
by the Sant's grace every sorrow has been wiped away;
by the Sant's grace one has been freed from the bonds (of Maya).
By the Sant's kindness attachment and doubt are gone;
bathing in the dust (of the feet) of the Saadh is every deed of dharma.
When the Saadh is kind, Govind is merciful;
this life of mine (dwells) among the Saadhs.
When I meditate on the merciful (Lord), the treasure of mercy,
then I find a place to sit in the Saadh Sangat.
On me, without virtue, God has shown mercy;
in the Saadh Sangat Nanak has taken up the Naam. ॥4॥
183.2: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
In the Saadh Sangat we have repeated (the Name of) the Lord God;
the Guru has given the Naam alone as the mantra.
Giving up pride, we have become free of enmity;
(O brothers,) worship the Guru's feet at all hours.
Now (our) evil intellect, which kept (us) strangers (to God), has perished,
ever since (we) heard the Lord's praise with (our) ears.
The treasure of Sahaj, peace and bliss,
the Protector, saves (us) at the last.
Pain and suffering, fears and doubts have perished;
in his grace he has stopped (our) coming and going.
(God) himself sees, speaks and hears in all;
O mind, repeat (the Name of) him who is ever with (you).
By the Sant's grace the light has dawned (within);
the One alone, the treasure of virtues, (is seen) filling all.
Pure become those who speak, holy those who listen,
who sing the virtues of Govind day after day.
Says Nanak, (O Lord,) the one to whom you are gracious,
that servant's every labour bears its fruit. ॥4॥
183.3: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(The Guru) breaks (one's) bonds and has (one) utter (the Name of) Ram;
(then) the mind settles in true, steady contemplation;
troubles are erased, and one lives at ease.
Such a giver is the True Guru said to be.
He (the Guru) is the giver of peace who has (us) repeat the Naam,
and in his grace unites (us) with him (God).
(God) himself unites (with the Guru) the one to whom he is merciful;
(such a one) obtains all treasures from the Guru.
Giving up self-conceit, (his) coming and going ends;
in the company of the Saadh (the Guru) he recognises the Supreme Lord.
God has become merciful to his servant;
the servant's mainstay is the One, Gopal.
(his) attention rests on the One alone, and in (his) mind is love for the One alone;
for the servant, the Lord's Name is all treasures.
(His) love is bound to the Supreme Lord;
(his) conduct is pure, (his) way of life true.
The Perfect Guru has wiped out the darkness;
Nanak's God is beyond all, and without limit. ॥4॥
184.1: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
That person crosses over (the world-ocean) in whose mind (God) dwells;
(God) is attained by his own grace.
No pain, disease or fear grips (that one) at all,
(who) repeats the Lord's Amrit Naam in his heart.
Let us meditate on the Supreme Lord, the Supreme God;
this understanding is received from the Perfect Guru.
The merciful (Lord) does and causes all to be done;
he sustains all beings and creatures;
he is inaccessible, beyond the reach of the senses, for ever without end:
O mind, remember (him) through the Perfect Guru's teaching.
He whose service is the treasure of all (gifts),
God, by whose worship honour is gained,
whose service never goes in vain:
sing the virtues of (that) Lord for ever and ever.
Show grace, O God, knower of hearts,
O Lord, treasure of peace, unseen Master:
all beings and creatures are in your shelter;
may Nanak receive the Naam: (that is his) glory. ॥4॥
184.2: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
He in whose hands is the way of life of (all) beings:
remember him, the Lord of those who have no lord.
When God comes into the mind, all sorrow goes;
through the Lord's Name all fears perish.
Of whom, apart from the Lord, are you afraid?
Forgetting the Lord, what peace do you think you know?
He who holds up many earths and skies,
whose light shines in all beings,
whose gift no one can undo:
remembering that God again and again, one becomes fearless.
Remember God's Name at all hours;
(it is) the dip and the bath at countless places of pilgrimage.
If you take the shelter of the Supreme Lord,
millions of stains are wiped away in an instant.
(God) is the perfect King, dependent on no one;
the servant of God holds a true trust (in him).
The Perfect Guru has given his hand and saved (God's servants);
O Nanak, the Supreme Lord holds all power. ॥4॥
184.3: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(The one whose) mind, by the Guru's grace, has become attached to the Naam,
though asleep for birth after birth, has awoken.
(He) utters God's virtues that are Amrit, and (his) Bani:
the mortal (blessed with) the good counsel of the Perfect Guru.
Remembering God, all joys have been found;
at home and outside, all is peace and Sahaj.
(He) has recognised the very One who created (him);
in his grace God himself has united (him with himself).
Holding (him) by the arm, (God) has taken (him) as his own;
(now his task is) ever to tell the Lord's story, Har Har, and to repeat (his Name).
Mantra, tantra (charm), medicine and the rite of atonement for sin:
all is the Name of the Lord, Har Har, on which soul and life-breath rest.
In the Lord's love the true wealth has been found;
in the company of the Saadh (the Guru) the hard-to-cross (world-ocean) has been crossed.
Sit at ease, O Sants and friends, as one family;
the Lord's wealth has been earned, beyond all reckoning.
The Guru gives (it) to the one in whose destiny it is (written);
O Nanak, no one goes empty (from the Guru's door). ॥4॥
185.1: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The hands become pure at once,
and the snares of Maya are destroyed.
With your tongue utter the virtues of Ram every day;
(so) you will find peace, my brother, my friend.
Write on paper, with pen and ink,
the Name of Ram, the Lord's Bani that is Amrit.
By this deed your vices will depart;
remembering Ram, one suffers no blows from Jam;
the messengers of Dharam Raj do not (even) look towards (you);
you will not be sunk in Maya, and nothing whatever will lure you.
You yourself will be saved, and (through you) the world will cross over;
repeat the Name of Ram, (repeat) the One Creator, Ekankar.
Practise it yourself, and teach it to others;
let the Name of Ram enter your heart.
The one on whose forehead this treasure is (written),
that person alone repeats (the Name of) God.
Sing the Lord's praises, Har Har, at all hours;
says Nanak, I am a sacrifice to that one. ॥4॥
185.2: Raag Gauri Guareri, Chaupade and Dupade, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
What belongs to another, that we take as our own;
with what we must give up and leave behind, the mind is engrossed.
Tell (me), how can we meet the Lord of the world,
when our love is for what is forbidden?
The thing that is false we have taken to be true;
what is certain to come (death) does not touch the mind in the least.
We walk the crooked path, on the left (the wrong) side;
leaving the straight (way), we weave backwards.
God himself is the Master of both sides;
the one he unites (with himself), O Nanak, is liberated. ॥4॥
185.3: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
In Kalyug (husband and wife) come together through the bonds (of past deeds);
for as long as (God's) command lasts, they share the joys (of the world).
By burning (on the husband's pyre), the beloved Lord is not found;
(yet), driven by the bond of her past deeds, (the widow) rises and becomes a sati.
Copying others, out of the mind's stubbornness, (she) burns herself;
(but) she does not win the beloved's company, and is made to wander through many births.
She who, in gentle conduct and self-restraint, obeys her beloved's command:
that woman suffers no pain from Jam.
Says Nanak, she who has known her beloved as the Supreme Lord
is a blessed sati, accepted in the Lord's court. ॥4॥
185.4: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Through the True Name we are wealthy and fortunate;
we sing the praises of the Lord in Sahaj and in love.
When I opened and looked into the treasure of my father and grandfather,
then my mind was filled with treasure.
(In it are) jewels and rubies beyond any price;
the storehouses are full, never to be exhausted, beyond weighing.
O brother, (those who) eat and spend (from it) together
find it never runs short; it goes on increasing.
Says Nanak, the one on whose forehead such destiny is written
is taken in as a sharer in this treasure. ॥4॥
186.1: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
While (God) is thought to be far away, we die of fear again and again;
when (we) saw (him) pervading everywhere, the fear ended.
I am a sacrifice to my True Guru,
who never leaves (me), and surely carries (me) across.
When the Naam is forgotten, (then come) pain, disease and grief;
when the Lord's praises are sung, there is bliss for ever.
No one should be called bad or good;
giving up pride, one should grasp the Lord's feet.
Says Nanak, keep the Guru's mantra in mind,
and you will find peace in the True Court. ॥4॥
186.2: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
One whose friend and companion (God) is present everywhere alike:
tell (me), what can that person lack?
One whose love is fixed on Gobind:
his pain, suffering and doubt run away.
One who has come to taste the relish, the relish of the Lord,
does not cling to other pleasures.
One whose word holds good in the Lord's court:
whom (else) does he take any notice of?
One who belongs to him to whom everything belongs
has peace for ever, O Nanak. ॥4॥
186.3: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
One to whom pain and pleasure seem alike:
how can worry take hold of him?
In the Lord's holy one dwell Sahaj and bliss;
he lives obedient to the Lord King, Har Har.
One in whose mind the carefree (Lord) comes to dwell
has no anxiety anywhere at all.
One from whose mind the wandering (of doubt) has perished
has no fear of Jam at all.
One into whose heart the Guru has given the Naam:
says Nanak, within him are all treasures. ॥4॥
186.4: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The (Lord) of inaccessible form has his dwelling in the mind;
by the Guru's grace, some rare one has come to know (this).
There are springs of Amrit, of the story of Sahaj;
the one to whom they are granted takes and enjoys them.
(Where) the unstruck Bani (sounds), that place is unlike any other;
Gopal is enchanted by its melody.
There, countless and endless gatherings of Sahaj (are held);
(there) the Sants are companions of the Supreme Lord.
(There) is endless joy, and no grief, nor any other (care).
That home the Guru has given to Nanak. ॥4॥
186.5: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(O Lord), which form of yours shall I worship?
Taking up which yoga shall I discipline the body?
Which virtue (of yours) shall I take up, to sing of you?
With what words shall I please you, O Supreme Lord?
What is that worship of you that I should perform?
What is that way by which I may cross the world-ocean?
What is the austerity by which one becomes a (true) ascetic?
What is that Name which washes away the filth of Haumai?
Praise, worship, wisdom, meditation, all such labour, O Nanak, (bears fruit for the one)
whom the merciful True Guru, in his grace, meets.
His alone is the merit, he alone has known God,
whose (prayer) the Giver of peace accepts. ॥36॥
187.1: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The body, of which (you are) proud, is not your own;
kingdom, land and wealth are not your own.
(None of these) is your own; to what are you clinging?
Your own is the Naam, which is found from the True Guru.
Sons, wife and brothers are not your own;
nor are dear friends, father and mother.
Gold, silver and money too are not (your own);
the choicest horses and elephants serve you nothing.
Says Nanak, the one whom the Guru, in his grace, has united (with the Lord),
everything is his, to whom the Lord King belongs. ॥4॥
187.2: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The Guru's feet are upon my forehead;
by them all my sorrows have been taken away.
I am a sacrifice to my True Guru;
recognising my self, I enjoy the supreme joy.
The one whose face the dust of the Guru's feet has touched
has given up all the intellect of ego.
The Guru's Shabad has come to taste sweet to my mind;
through it I have beheld the Supreme Lord.
The Guru is the bestower of peace, the Guru is the Creator;
O Nanak, soul and breath of life rest on the Guru as their support. ॥4॥
187.3: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O my mind, long for him
O mind, my friend, take such a one as the Lord for your beloved;
keep him, the support of the breath of life, ever in your mind.
the Primal Being, beyond the farthest beyond, the radiant Divine One.
O mind, place your hope in him,
on whom (all) have relied from the beginning, from the start of the ages.
Through whose love there is lasting peace,
Nanak, meeting the Guru, sings of him. ॥4॥
187.4: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Whatever the Friend does, that I accept;
the Friend's doings are (to me) as joy itself.
In my mind and heart there is one support alone:
that he who does all things is my Friend.
My Friend is free of all care;
by the Guru's grace I have come to love (him).
My Friend is the Knower of hearts;
the almighty Being, the Supreme Lord, the Master.
(O God), I am (your) servant, you are my Master;
says Nanak, O God, my honour and greatness are yours. ॥4॥
188.1: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O all-powerful Lord, the one whose side you take
is touched by no stain at all.
O Madho, the one whose hope is in you
has no need of anything from the world.
The one in whose heart the Master dwells
is left with no anxiety at all.
O God, the one to whom you have given fortitude:
Says Nanak, I have found such a Guru
as has shown (me) the Supreme Lord, pervading all. ॥4॥
188.2: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The rare (human) body is received by great good fortune;
those who (even so) do not repeat the Naam are slayers of their own soul.
Why do they not simply die, those who forget the Lord?
Of what use is a life without the Name?
Eating, drinking, playing, laughing, and all the display:
what good is the adorning of a corpse?
Those who do not listen to the praise of (God, who is) supreme bliss
are worse than beasts, birds and the creatures that creep.
Says Nanak, (the one in whom) the Guru has made the mantra (of the Name) firm:
in his heart the Naam alone stays absorbed. ॥4॥
188.3: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
All these relations are in name only, and false.
Why, you fool, do you babble (like one talking in his sleep)?
Joined (with them) by the union (of past deeds), you have come (into the world) by (God's) Hukam.
The clay (of all) is one, the light is one,
the breath of life is one: why, then, should anyone weep?
(but) this soul is not one that dies.
Says Nanak, (those for whom) the Guru has opened the doors
have been set free, and the structures of (their) delusion have been destroyed. ॥4॥
188.4: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The people who look great and mighty
are gripped by the disease of anxiety.
Who becomes great by Maya's greatness?
Great is the one who has fixed his loving attention on the Lord.
The landowner fights over land day after day;
(in the end) he leaves (it) and goes, yet (his) thirst is not quenched.
Says Nanak, (I) have reflected on this essence:
without the worship of the Lord there is no release. ॥3॥
188.5: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
perfect is all (he does), (the one) with the Naam in his heart.
(Their honour) stayed whole when the Perfect One kept (it):
(those) servants had looked to the shelter of the Supreme Lord.
perfect (his) austerity, and perfect both (his) rule and (his) union (with God).
On the Lord's path even sinners become pure;
(their) glory is complete, and complete (their) dealings with the world.
The Creator ever dwells close beside (them);
says Nanak, my True Guru is perfect. ॥4॥
188.6: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
By the dust (of the feet) of the Sant, millions of sins are erased;
by the Sant's grace comes release from birth and death.
The sight of the Sant is the perfect (pilgrim's) bath;
by the Sant's grace the Naam is repeated.
In the Sant's company pride is erased,
(and) everywhere the One Creator, Ekankar, is seen.
When the Sant is well pleased, the five (passions) come under control,
(and one) takes the Amrit Naam and stores it up in the heart.
Says Nanak, the one whose destiny is full
comes to touch the feet of the Saadh (the Guru). ॥4॥
189.1: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Repeating the Lord's virtues, the lotus (of the heart) blossoms;
remembering the Lord, all fear is destroyed.
That understanding is perfect by which (one) sings the Lord's virtues;
(it comes to the one who) by great good fortune finds the company of the Saadh.
The Naam's treasure is found in the Saadh Sangat;
in the Saadh Sangat all tasks are fulfilled.
Devotion to the Lord makes one's birth approved;
by the Guru's grace (one) utters the Naam.
Says Nanak, that person is approved
189.2: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The one whose mind is dyed with the One (God)
that Creator alone does and causes all to be done.
(The one who) practises (the Name) with his mind and says Har Har with his mouth:
that person never wavers anywhere, here or hereafter.
Whoever has the wealth of the Lord is a true banker;
the Perfect Guru has made (his) credit good.
(He) has met the Lord King, the Being who is the life (of all);
says Nanak, (he) has attained the supreme state. ॥4॥
189.3: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The Naam is the support of the devotee's life-breath;
the Naam alone is (his) wealth, the Naam alone (his) trade.
Through the greatness of the Naam the servant wins honour:
(the one) to whom (God), in his grace, himself causes (it) to be given.
For the devotee, the Naam is the abode of peace;
dyed in the Naam, such a devotee is approved.
The Lord's Name upholds his servant;
with every breath the servant cherishes the Naam.
Says Nanak, the one whose fortune is full:
his mind clings to the Naam. ॥4॥
189.4: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
By the Sant's grace (I) have meditated on the Lord's Name;
from then on (my) restless mind has been content.
Singing (his) virtues, (I) have found the resting place of peace;
(my) weariness is gone, and my demon has been slain.
Worshipping the lotus feet of God,
through the Lord's Simran my anxiety has been erased.
Forsaking all, (I,) the helpless one, came to the shelter of the One;
then in Sahaj (I) attained the high abode.
Sorrow, pain, doubt and fear have fled;
O Nanak, the Creator has come to dwell in (my) mind. ॥4॥
189.5: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
With (my) hands I do service, with (my) tongue I sing (God's) virtues;
with (my) feet I hasten on the Master's path.
Good is (this) time (of human birth): it is the turn for Simran;
remembering the Naam, (one) crosses beyond (all) fears.
Let (your) eyes behold the sight of the Sants;
write the imperishable God into (your) mind.
Go to the Saadh and listen to the Kirtan,
(and) be rid of the fear of birth and death.
Enshrine the Master's lotus feet in (your) heart;
O Nanak, carry (this) rare body across (the world-ocean). ॥4॥
190.1: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The one on whom (God) bestows his grace:
that person utters the Naam with his tongue.
Forgetting the Lord, anxiety and sorrow take hold;
remembering the Naam, doubt and fear run away.
The one who listens to the Lord's Kirtan and sings the Lord's Kirtan:
sorrow does not come near that person.
Serving the Lord, his servant is made beautiful;
(The one with) the Name of the merciful Lord in mind, body and mouth:
O Nanak, (he) has cast off all other entanglements. ॥4॥
190.2: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Give up (your) cleverness and all (your) cunning,
(and) take the support of the Perfect Guru.
Singing the Lord's virtues, sorrows perish and peace (comes),
(when) the Perfect Guru is met (and one) fixes (one's) loving attention (on God).
The Guru has given (me) the Lord's Name as the mantra;
grieving is over and anxiety has lifted.
Meeting the merciful Guru, there is joy;
in (his) grace (he) has cut the nets of Jam.
Says Nanak, (the one who) has found the Perfect Guru:
because of (that Guru), Maya does not grip (him) again. ॥4॥
190.3: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The Perfect Guru himself has saved (us);
it is the manmukh who has been struck by torment.
Repeat Guru, Guru, O my friend:
(your) face will shine bright in (the Lord's) court.
Enshrine the Guru's feet in (your) heart;
(he) will slay (your) sorrows, (your) enemies and your demon.
The Guru's Shabad is with you as (your) helper;
all beings have become kind (to you), O brother.
When the Perfect Guru showed grace,
says Nanak, my (striving) bore its full fruit. ॥4॥
190.4: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(One without the Saadh Sangat) eats many tasty things, as a beast does,
and is tied up with the rope of attachment, like a thief.
A body that is without the Saadh Sangat is a corpse;
(such a one) keeps coming and going through the life-forms and wastes away in pain.
He is dressed in many fine clothes,
(yet is) like a scarecrow put up in a field to scare (creatures) off.
Every body (even a beast's) comes of some use;
(but) fruitless is the human who does not repeat the Naam.
Says Nanak, those to whom (the Lord) becomes merciful
gather in the Saadh Sangat and dwell on Gopal in devotion. ॥4॥
190.5: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The Guru's Shabad has driven off the strife and anguish (of the mind);
coming and going has ended, and every comfort (is found).
Fears have perished (for those) who have meditated on the fearless Lord
and sung the Lord's virtues in the Saadh Sangat.
(Those who) have set (the Lord's) lotus feet within their hearts,
the Guru has carried (them) across the ocean of fire.
(They) were going under, and the perfect Guru has pulled (them) out;
those broken off (from the Lord) for birth after birth he has joined (to him) again.
Says Nanak, I am a sacrifice to that Guru,
on meeting whom our liberation has come about. ॥4॥
191.1: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(O brothers,) in the Saadh Sangat seek the sanctuary of him (God);
lay your mind and body before him.
Drink the Naam that is Amrit, my brothers;
remembering it again and again, all the burning (within) has been quenched.
Give up pride, and put an end to birth and death;
bow your head at the feet of the Lord's servant.
With every breath hold God dear in (your) mind;
gather that wealth which goes along with (you).
(This wealth) comes only to one on whose forehead good fortune is (written);
says Nanak, fall at that one's feet. ॥4॥
191.2: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(The Guru) has made the withered green in an instant;
watering (them) with his glance of Amrit, he has brought (them) to life.
The perfect Gurdev (the divine Guru) has cut away the troubles;
he has given his servant his own service.
Worry is wiped out, the mind's hope is fulfilled,
(once) the True Guru, the treasure of virtues, showed mercy.
Sorrows have fled, and comforts have come to settle (within);
there was no delay once the Guru gave the word.
Those who met the perfect Guru have had their wish fulfilled;
O Nanak, those people have borne good fruit. ॥4॥
191.3: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The fevers are gone; God has brought calm (within);
(we) have been cooled; God has given (this) gift.
By God's grace (we) are at ease;
(he) has united (with himself) those separated for birth after birth.
the very seat of every disease has been destroyed.
In Sahaj and with love, (such a one) utters the Lord's Bani;
O mortal, remember God at all hours.
Neither sorrow nor pain nor Jam comes near (the one),
says Nanak, who sings the Lord's virtues. ॥4॥
191.4: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Blessed are the days, blessed the occasions,
in which the Supreme Lord, the unattached, is met.
I am a sacrifice to that hour
in which my mind repeats the Lord's Name.
Fruitful is that moment, fruitful that hour,
in which the tongue utters the Lord's Name, Har Hari.
Fruitful is the forehead that bows before the Sant;
holy are the feet that walk on the Lord's path.
Says Nanak, blessed is my fortune,
through which I have met the feet of the Saadh (the Guru). ॥4॥
192.1: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Keep the Guru's Shabad in your mind;
remember the Naam, and every worry goes.
Apart from the Lord God there is no other;
he alone kills, and he alone preserves.
Enshrine the Guru's feet in your heart, within your breast;
repeating (the Name), you will cross the ocean of fire.
Fix your attention on the Guru's form (the Shabad);
you will be honoured here and hereafter.
Leaving all (else), (Nanak) has come to the Guru's sanctuary;
(his) anxieties are gone, and Nanak has found peace. ॥4॥
192.2: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(God is the one) remembering whom all sorrow departs
and the jewel of the Naam comes to dwell in the mind.
O my mind, repeat the Bani of Govind (his praise),
the Bani in which holy people have told of Ram with their tongues.
Besides the One there is no other,
by whose glance (of grace) there is lasting peace.
Take the One alone as your beloved, friend and companion;
write the letters of Har Har (the Lord's Name) in your mind.
Nanak sings the virtues of (him,) the knower of hearts. ॥4॥
192.3: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The whole world is steeped in fear;
the one whose support is the Naam has no fear.
(O God,) in your sanctuary fear takes no hold;
what pleases you, that alone is done.
Caught in grief and joy, (beings) keep coming and going;
peace is found by the one who is pleasing to God.
(The world) is an ocean of fire, and Maya grips (all) hard;
those who have found the True Guru stay cool.
says Nanak, what can the poor creature (do)? ॥4॥
192.4: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(O God,) by your grace (your) Name is repeated;
by your grace a place is found in your court.
Apart from you, O Supreme Lord, there is no one;
by your grace there is lasting peace.
When you dwell in the mind, sorrow does not touch (one);
by your grace doubt and fear take flight.
you know the inner being of every heart.
I make my prayer before my True Guru,
that Nanak may receive the Naam, the true capital. ॥4॥
192.5: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
As husks without grain are hollow,
so empty are those mouths that lack the Naam.
O mortal, repeat the Name of the Lord, Har Har, every day;
without the Naam, cursed is the body, which is not (truly) your own.
Without the Naam no good fortune (shines) on the brow;
without the husband, where is a wife's married joy?
One who forgets the Naam and is drawn to other tastes
has not one of his hopes fulfilled.
O God, in your grace (grant) your gift,
so that Nanak may repeat the Naam day and night. ॥4॥
193.1: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
You are all-powerful; you alone are my Master;
all things come from you; you are the knower of hearts.
O perfect Supreme Lord, (you are) the shelter of your servants;
in your sanctuary millions of people are saved.
As many beings as there are, all are yours;
by your grace (they have) comforts in plenty.
Whatever takes place is all your will;
one who understands the Hukam merges in the True One.
Show grace, O God, and give (this) gift,
that Nanak may remember the Naam, the treasure. ॥4॥
193.2: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
By great good fortune one gains the sight of the one
whose loving attention is held on the Lord's Name.
One in whose mind the Lord has come to dwell
knows no sorrow, even in a dream.
(God) has placed all treasures within his servant;
in his company sins and sorrows depart.
The glory of (such) a servant cannot be told;
the servant stays merged in the Supreme Lord.
Show grace, O God, and hear (my) plea:
give Nanak the dust (of the feet) of your servant. ॥4॥
193.3: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Remembering the Lord, the evil that haunts you departs,
and every kind of well-being comes to dwell in the mind.
O my mind, dwell in devotion on the Name of the One alone;
(it is this) that serves your soul.
Night and day sing the virtues of the Infinite;
(this is) the perfect Guru's spotless mantra.
Give up (other) devices and lean on the One alone;
taste the essence of Amrit, the supreme treasure.
They alone have crossed the treacherous ocean
on whom, O Nanak, (God) casts his glance of grace. ॥4॥
193.4: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Those who have set God's lotus feet in their hearts
have met the Perfect True Guru and been carried across (the world-ocean).
Sing the praises of Govind, O my brother;
meeting the Saadh (the Guru), meditate on the Lord's Name.
(Their) human body, so hard to come by, has been accepted (at the Lord's door),
(for they) have received from the True Guru the Naam, the seal (of passage).
Remembering the Lord, (they) have attained the perfect state;
in the Saadh Sangat (they) have rid themselves of fears and doubts.
servant Nanak is in the Lord's refuge. ॥4॥
193.5: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
I am a sacrifice to the sight of the revered Guru;
I live by repeating the True Guru's name again and again.
O perfect Supreme Lord, O divine Guru,
be gracious, that I may keep to your service.
I hold (the Guru's) lotus feet within my heart, in my breast;
(the feet of) the Guru are the support of (my) mind, body, wealth and life-breath.
(Thus) life bears fruit and is accepted (at the Lord's door):
know the Guru, the Supreme Lord, to be near (you).
The dust (of the feet) of the Sant (the Guru) is found by great good fortune;
O Nanak, on meeting the Guru, loving attention is fixed on the Lord. ॥4॥
194.1: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(One who in secret) does evil deeds and shows (the world) something else
is bound as a thief in the court of the Lord.
He alone belongs to the Lord who remembers the Lord,
the One who pervades water, land and sky.
(One who has) poison within, yet recites Amrit (words) with his mouth,
is bound in the city of Jam and suffers blows.
Behind many veils he commits vices,
(but) in an instant they come to light before the world.
The one who within is steeped in the True Name and its delight:
O Nanak, the Creator is gracious to him. ॥4॥
194.2: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The dye of the Lord's love never comes off
(for the one) to whom the Perfect Guru gives understanding.
The mind dyed in the Lord's love is true (fast in its colour);
(it bears) the deep crimson (of the love) of the Perfect Being, the Creator.
(One who) sits in the company of the Sants and sings (God's) praises:
his dye (of love) never comes off.
Without remembering the Lord, (no one) has found peace;
all other dyes, those of Maya, are pale and tasteless.
Those whom the Guru has dyed (in love) are made joyful;
says Nanak, the Guru has shown mercy (to them). ॥4॥
194.3: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Remembering the Master, sins are destroyed,
and peace, Sahaj and bliss come to dwell (within).
The Lord's servants rely on the Lord;
repeating the Naam, all (their) anxiety has been wiped away.
In the Saadh Sangat there is no fear at all and no wandering (of mind);
(there) the praises of Gopal are sung day and night.
In his grace God has granted release from bonds,
and has given the shelter of (his) lotus feet.
Says Nanak, faith (in God) has arisen in (their) minds;
the servants ever drink in (God's) pure praise. ॥4॥
194.4: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
One whose mind is attached to the Lord's feet:
his pain, suffering and doubt have fled.
The trader in the Lord's wealth is whole and perfect;
the one whom (God) honours is the hero.
Those to whom the Lord of the world has been gracious,
those servants have fallen at the Guru's feet.
(Theirs are) peace, Sahaj, calm and bliss;
they live by repeating (the Name of) the Lord of supreme bliss again and again.
(Those who) have earned the capital of the Naam in the Saadh Sangat:
says Nanak, God has cut away (their) affliction. ॥4॥
194.5: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Remembering the Lord, all troubles are wiped away,
and (God's) lotus feet enter and dwell in the mind.
Utter the Lord's Name a hundred thousand times,
and drink God's Amrit essence, O dear (tongue).
Peace, Sahaj, delight and great bliss are theirs
who live by repeating (the Name of) the Lord of supreme bliss again and again.
(They) have cast off lust, anger, greed and pride;
in the Saadh's company all (their) sins have been washed away.
Show grace, O God, merciful to the meek,
and grant Nanak the dust (of the feet) of the Saadh. ॥4॥
195.1: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The One whose gifts (a person) wears and eats:
how can it be right, O mother, to be slack towards him?
(Those who) forget the Master and busy themselves with other things
give up a jewel in exchange for a cowrie.
Forsaking God, they cling to greed for other things;
where is the honour in saluting the handmaid (Maya)?
They eat and drink fare as sweet as Amrit,
(yet) the dogs do not know the One who gave (it).
Says Nanak, we are untrue to (your) salt (ungrateful);
forgive (us), O God, knower of hearts. ॥4॥
195.2: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
To keep the mind in meditation on God's feet
is the dip and the bath at all places of pilgrimage.
Remember the Lord every day, O my brother;
(so) the filth of millions of births is washed off.
(One who) has enshrined the Lord's story in the heart
has obtained every fruit the mind longs for.
Accepted (at the Lord's door) are the life, the death and the birth
of the one in whose heart God dwells.
Says Nanak, they alone are perfect
who have received the dust (of the feet) of the Saadh. ॥4॥
195.3: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(One who) eats and wears (what God gives) and yet denies (him):
the messengers of Dharam Raj keep their eye on him.
(You) have turned your face from him who gave (you) soul and body;
(so) you will wander through many species for millions of births.
Such is the way of the Saakat:
whatever he does is all perverse.
The One who upholds soul and breath, mind and body:
that very Master (he) has put out of his mind.
(His) vices have grown; many sheets have been written (with them).
Save Nanak, O ocean of mercy and of peace.
O Supreme Lord, (whoever comes) to your refuge
cuts (his) bonds and crosses over (the world-ocean) through the Lord's Name. ॥78॥
195.4: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(Whoever) made (God) a friend, even for his own gain,
was given all he longed for, and the state of liberation (too).
Let everyone make such a friend,
from whom no one goes away empty.
(Whoever) took (him) into the heart, even for his own ends,
had all (his) pain, suffering and disease destroyed (by God).
(One whose) tongue has grown used to uttering the Lord's Name:
Nanak is a sacrifice many times over;
fruitful is the sight of our Gobind. ॥4॥
195.5: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
In an instant millions of obstacles are taken away
(for those) who hear the story of the Lord, Har Har, in the Saadh Sangat.
One who drinks the Lord's essence, the Amrit of (his) virtues:
meditating on the Lord's feet, his hunger is gone.
All blessings, the treasures of peace and Sahaj, are his
in whose heart you dwell, O God.
Medicines, mantras and tantras are all mere ash;
enshrine the Creator in your heart.
(One who) has cast off all doubts and worshipped the Supreme Lord:
says Nanak, this dharma (of his) never wavers. ॥4॥
196.1: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
By (God's) grace I have met that Guru,
by whose strength no disease takes hold (of me).
To remember the Lord is to cross the ocean of fear;
in the refuge of the valiant (Guru), the papers (of account) of Jam are torn up.
The True Guru has imparted the mantra of the Lord's Name;
with this support (all) tasks have been fulfilled.
The full glory of japa, austerity and self-restraint (has been gained),
(since) the Guru was gracious and the Lord became (my) helper.
The Guru has done away with pride, attachment and doubt;
behold, O Nanak, the Supreme Lord spread out (everywhere). ॥4॥
196.2: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Better the blind man than one who lords it in sensual pleasures,
(for) when pain strikes, he remembers the Lord's Name.
(O Lord,) for your servant you alone are glory;
(but) Maya takes the one engrossed in her into hell.
One gripped by disease (too) remembers the Name,
(but) one drunk on the poison (of vice) has no shelter (here) and no place (hereafter).
(One whose) love is fixed on the lotus feet (of the Lord)
does not call other pleasures to mind.
May I remember (you) for ever and ever, O God, my Master;
meet Nanak, O Lord, knower of hearts. ॥4॥
196.3: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
At all hours the highwaymen (lust and the other vices) keep (one) company;
God in his grace has driven (them) off.
Let everyone savour the sweet essence of such a Lord;
that God is full of every power.
The world-ocean burns with fierce heat (of the vices);
God can carry (one) across (it) in an instant.
The bonds are many, and (by one's own effort) they cannot be broken;
remembering the Name, (people) gain the fruit of liberation.
No argument or cleverness of this (mortal) can do anything;
O Nanak, (when God) shows grace, (mortals) sing (his) praises. ॥4॥
196.4: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(If you) have gained the purse (of wealth) of the Lord's Name,
move about the world (free of care): all (your) tasks will be fulfilled.
It is by great good fortune that the Lord's Kirtan is sung;
O Supreme Lord, only if you give is (this gift) received.
Keep the Lord's feet enshrined in your heart, deep within;
climbing aboard (them, as on a ship), you will cross over the world-ocean.
Let everyone keep the company of the Saadh (the Guru);
(there) is lasting well-being, and sorrow comes no more.
With loving devotion, worship the treasure of virtues (the Lord);
O Nanak, (so) honour is gained in the Lord's court. ॥4॥
196.5: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The Lord, our friend, fills the water, the land and the sky;
as (his) praises are sung day by day, doubts have perished.
Waking and sleeping, the Lord stays at (one's) side as a watchman,
he by whose remembrance the fear of Jam is gone.
God's lotus feet have come to dwell in the heart,
The One (Lord) alone is hope, honour, strength and wealth;
in the mind is the support of the True King (God).
Those who were very poor and without support, (once they became) servants of the Saadh (the Guru),
O Nanak, God gave (them his) hand and saved (them). ॥4॥
197.1: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Bathing in the Name of the Lord, Har Har, (mortals) become pure;
(its) rewards are greater than the merit (earned) at millions of eclipses.
(The one in whose) heart the Lord's feet have come to dwell:
(his) sins of birth after birth have fled.
(The one who) has gained the fruit of Kirtan in the Saadh Sangat
has not even caught sight of the road of Jam.
(The one whose) support in thought, word and deed is Govind,
from him (the hold of) the poisonous world has fallen away.
(The one whom) God in his grace has made his own,
O Nanak, (he) repeats the Lord's chant, and repeats the Lord alone. ॥4॥
197.2: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Take refuge with the one who has come to know the Lord;
dyed in the love of the Lord's feet, mind and body grow cool and calm.
(Those who) do not enshrine in the mind God, the destroyer of fear,
pass through many births, ever trembling with fear.
The one in whose heart the Lord's Name has come to dwell:
all his wishes and tasks are fulfilled.
He in whose power are birth, old age and death:
remember that all-powerful (Lord) with every breath and every morsel.
The One God alone is friend, companion and comrade;
the Master's Name is Nanak's support. ॥4॥
197.3: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Out (in the world, the Sants) keep (the Lord) cherished in the heart;
coming back home, (they) bring Govind along.
The Name of the Lord, Har Har, is (ever) at the side of the Sants;
(their) mind and body stay dyed in the colour of Ram's love.
By the Guru's grace (they) have crossed the (world-)ocean,
(and) all the sins of birth after birth are taken away.
Fortunate (is he): glory (is his), and (his) awareness (rests) in the Name,
(in whose heart dwells) the pure mantra of the Perfect Guru.
Meditate on (God's) lotus feet in the heart;
197.4: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Blessed is this place (where) Govind's praises are sung;
God himself has made peace and well-being dwell (there).
Misfortune is there where the Lord is not remembered;
where the Lord's praises are sung, (there) are joys by the million.
When the Lord is forgotten, a host of sorrows and diseases (close in);
when God is served, Jam comes nowhere near.
Fortunate and unshakeable is that place
where God's Name alone is repeated.
Wherever one goes, my Master is there alongside;
Nanak has met the Knower of hearts. ॥4॥
197.5: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The mortal who meditates on Govind,
lettered or unlettered, attains the highest spiritual state.
In the company of the Saadh (the Guru), remember Gopal;
without the Name, wealth and possessions are (all) false.
He alone is handsome, clever and wise,
the person who has accepted God's will.
His coming into the world is approved
(who) knows his Master (to dwell) in every heart.
Says Nanak, the one whose fortune is perfect:
his mind is fixed on the Lord's feet. ॥4॥
198.1: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The Saakat has no fellowship with the Lord's servant;
the one (the Saakat) is given over to vice, while the other (the servant) is dyed in Ram's love.
(Their fellowship is) like riding an adorned mare in the mind alone,
(or) like an impotent man fondling a woman.
(Or as if one) were to rope an ox's legs and milk it,
(or) mount a cow and drive (it) after a lion;
(or) take a sheep and worship (it) as Kamdhenu,
(or) rush off to trade without capital.
O Nanak, repeat Ram's Name in your mind;
remember the Master, the Lord: (there is no) friend like (him). ॥4॥
198.2: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
That understanding is called pure and steadfast, O brother,
(through which) Ram('s Name), the home of all delights, is drunk.
Make the Lord's feet (your) shelter in the heart;
(so) release from birth and death is won.
Pure is the body in which no sin springs up;
in Ram's love (shines) a spotless radiance.
In the Saadh Sangat the vices are erased;
this is the highest blessing of all.
(Those) dyed in loving devotion to Gopal:
Nanak begs for the dust of the feet of (such) holy ones. ॥4॥
198.3: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(Those whose) love for Govind has grown like this:
(God) has united (with himself) those of perfect good fortune.
As a wife blossoms at the sight of her husband,
so the Lord's servant lives by calling the Name to mind.
As a mother lives by the sight of her son,
(so) the servant is steeped in the Lord, through and through, like warp and weft.
As the greedy man delights at the sight of wealth,
(so) the servant's mind clings to (God's) lotus feet.
O Giver, do not slip from (my) mind even for a moment;
O God of Nanak, (you are) the support of (his) life-breath. ॥4॥
198.4: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Those who are absorbed in Ram, the home of all delights,
stay pierced through with loving devotion to (God's) lotus feet.
All other pleasures look (to them) like ashes;
