without the Name, the world (seems to them) fruitless.
(God) himself has drawn (them) out of the blind well (of Maya);
wondrous is the glory of Govind's virtues.
Gopal fills the forests, every blade of grass and the three worlds;
(all) is God's own expanse; the merciful (Lord) is with every being.
Says Nanak, that is the best of speech
198.5: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Day after day, let one bathe in the pool of Ram('s Name);
stirring it well, let one drink the Lord's Amrit, the supreme delight, (with relish).
The Name of Govind is pure water;
as one bathes (in it), all one's tasks are fulfilled.
There, in the company of the Sants, (God's) discourse goes on,
(which) wipes out the sins of millions of births.
supreme bliss (God, its source) pervades (their) mind and body.
The one who has received the treasure of the Lord's feet:
servant Nanak is a sacrifice to him. ॥4॥
199.1: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Do that by which no filth (of vice) clings (to the mind),
(and) this mind stays awake in the Lord's Kirtan.
Remember the One (Lord) alone, with no love for another;
in the company of the Sants, repeat the Name alone.
Rituals, religious duties, observances, fasts and worship:
count none (of these) a second (support) beside the Supreme Lord.
His toil has borne its full fruit
whose love is with his own God.
Supreme beyond all, boundless, is that Vaishnav (the true devotee),
says Nanak, who has given up the vices. ॥4॥
199.2: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(Maya's goods) leave (a person) while he is still alive, O madman;
once he is dead, who gains anything from them?
Remember Govind in mind and body: this is the lot written (for you) from the start;
Maya's poison serves no purpose at all.
Whoever has eaten the swindler's drug of the senses' pleasures,
The world (-ocean) is full of terrible pain and hard to cross;
without the Name of Ram, how will you get across?
Join the Saadh Sangat and set right both worlds (this one and the next);
O Nanak, worship the Name of Ram. ॥4॥
199.3: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The beard that bristles (in arrogance) against the poor
the Supreme Lord has burnt in the fire.
he is the protector of his own servant.
From the beginning, from the start of the ages, (God's) glory has been made manifest:
the slanderer has died, a great torment rising up (within him).
He has been struck down by the One whose stroke no one can ward off;
hereafter and here (his) name is evil.
(God) keeps his servants clasped to his bosom;
O Nanak, take (his) refuge and meditate on the Lord's Name. ॥4॥
199.4: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The mahzar (a complaint signed by many, drawn up against his servant) God himself has proved false;
To the one whose helper is my Gobind
(He who) tells lies in the True Court,
that blind fool beats (his) head with his hands.
Those who commit sins are gripped by diseases;
God himself sits as the judge.
By their own doings (people) are bound by their own hand;
all their wealth went along with their life.
Nanak has taken refuge at (the Lord's) court;
199.5: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The dust (of the feet) of (the Lord's) servant tastes sweet to the mind of that mortal
for whom (it) is written from the start, by (his) deeds of the past.
Through the intellect of ego, the mind was coated with grease;
with the dust of the Saadh, (that intellect) has been scoured clean.
If (one) washes the body in many waters,
(the mind's) filth does not come off; no one is made pure that way.
(The one who) has met the True Guru, ever merciful,
has cut away the fear of death by remembering the Lord again and again.
The Lord's Name is liberation, it is enjoyment, it is the way (of life);
O Nanak, sing (his) virtues with loving devotion. ॥4॥
200.1: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The servants of the Lord hold the rank of true life;
meeting them, the soul is filled with light.
O mind, listen with (your) ears to the Simran of the Lord;
O mortal, (so) you will find peace at the Lord's door.
Let us meditate on Gopal at all hours;
O Nanak, beholding (his) sight, (the mind) is filled with delight. ॥2॥
200.2: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Calm has come: the Guru, who is Gobind (in form), has bestowed it;
afflictions and sins have perished, O my brother.
Utter the Name of Ram with the tongue every day;
(by it) diseases have perished and joy has come.
Reflect on the virtues of the inaccessible Supreme Lord;
in the company of the Saadh (the Guru) lies deliverance.
Sing the pure virtues (of God) day after day;
O friend, the servants (who sing them) are rid of disease and are saved.
(Be gracious, O Lord,) that I may meditate on my God in thought, word and deed;
servant Nanak has come to your refuge. ॥4॥
200.3: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The divine Guru has given light to the eyes;
doubts are gone, and (the) service (done) has borne its fruit.
Bihari (the Lord who sports in his creation) has given protection from smallpox (Sitala);
the Supreme Lord God has shown grace.
O Nanak, the one who repeats the Naam truly lives;
in the Saadh Sangat he drinks the Lord's Amrit. ॥2॥
200.4: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(O Lord,) blessed is that forehead (which bows to you), blessed are the eyes (that behold) your (sight);
blessed are those devotees who love you.
Without the Naam, how can peace be found?
(So) let the tongue speak the praise of the Name of Ram.
Let us be a sacrifice to those,
O Nanak, each one who has meditated on the (Lord) beyond all desire. ॥2॥
200.5: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(O Lord,) you alone are (my) counsel, you alone are with (me);
you yourself protect (me), watching over and caring for (me).
Such is Ram, the helper in this world and the next:
he keeps the honour of (his) servant, O my brother.
He in whose control is this world is himself (the helper) in the world hereafter;
(my) mind repeats (the Name of that) Lord at all hours.
Honour is his, he is accepted (in the Lord's court), and the True Name is his pass,
for whom you yourself issue the command.
(God) himself is the giver, himself the one who sustains;
O Nanak, cherish the Name of Ram (in your heart) every day. ॥4॥
200.6: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
When the Perfect True Guru became merciful,
Gopal came to dwell in the heart for ever.
Remembering Ram, lasting peace has been found;
the perfect Lord, the King, has shown mercy.
Says Nanak, the one whose destiny is perfect
has the Name of the Lord, Har Har, as (his) lasting wedded bliss. ॥2॥
201.1: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(The priest, at his patron's house,) loosens his dhoti and spreads it beneath him,
and like a donkey he stuffs (everything) into his belly.
Without (the) deeds (of remembrance), liberation is not attained;
let us meditate on the Naam, the treasure (that brings) liberation.
(He) takes his ritual baths, marks his brow with the tilak and performs worship,
(yet) with a knife drawn (pitilessly) he takes the offerings into his hand.
He reads the Veda in a sweet voice from his mouth,
(yet that) mortal does not shrink from butchering living beings.
Says Nanak, the one on whom (God) shows grace
is pure in heart and reflects on Brahm (God). ॥4॥
201.2: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Sit steady in the home (of your heart), O beloved servants of the Lord:
the True Guru has set your affairs right.
The Supreme God has struck down the wicked foes;
the Creator has kept the honour of (his) servant.
(God) has brought emperors and kings, all of them, under the sway (of his servants);
(they) have drunk the supreme essence of the Amrit Naam.
on (your) joining the Saadh Sangat, (God) has granted (this) gift.
O God, knower of hearts, (I) have come to (your) refuge;
Nanak has grasped (your) support, O God, my Master. ॥4॥
201.3: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Dyed in the love of the Lord, one does not burn in the fire (of craving);
Dyed in the love of the Lord, one is not deceived by Maya;
Dyed in the love of the Lord, one does not drown in the water (of the world-ocean);
Dyed in the love of the Lord, (one's life) bears good fruit.
(O Lord,) through your Name all fears are wiped away;
on meeting (the holy) company, one sings the virtues of the Lord, Har Har.
Dyed in the love of the Lord, one is rid of all anxiety;
(but) only that one is absorbed in the Lord who has the teaching of the Saadh (the Guru).
Dyed in the love of the Lord, one has no dread of Jam;
Dyed in the love of the Lord, one's hopes are fulfilled.
Dyed in the love of the Lord, one is touched by no sorrow;
One dyed in the love of the Lord stays awake night and day;
One dyed in the love of the Lord dwells in the home of Sahaj;
Dyed in the love of the Lord, one's doubt and fear take flight.
Dyed in the love of the Lord, one's understanding becomes noble;
Dyed in the love of the Lord, one's renown is spotless.
Says Nanak, I am a sacrifice to those
who never forget my God. ॥4॥
201.4: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Those who make the effort (on the Lord's path) have become calm in mind;
walking on (that) way, all their sorrows have gone.
Repeating the Naam, bliss has filled their minds,
as they have sung with love the virtues of the (Lord of) supreme bliss.
There is well-being; they have come into the home of joy;
on meeting the Saadh Sangat, the curse (of Maya) has gone.
The eyes become pure the moment they behold (the Lord's) sight;
blessed are the foreheads that touch (his) lotus feet.
In the service of Gobind this body bears its fruit;
by the grace of the Sant (the Guru) the supreme state has been attained.
The servant whom (God) himself has helped
has found peace by falling at the feet of (the Lord's) servants.
When selfhood was gone, they became (one with the Lord) himself,
(when) they came into the refuge of the treasure of mercy.
When (one) has found the very One he longed for,
where else would he go then to search (for him)?
(Such ones) have become steady; they dwell on the seat of peace;
O Nanak, by the Guru's grace (they) have come to live in peace. ॥4॥
a01.title: Raag Gauri: Sukhmani, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
a01.salok: Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Salutation to the Primal Guru, who was before all.
Salutation to the Guru who has been since the ages began.
Salutation to the revered, divine Guru. ॥1॥
a01.p1: Let me practise Simran (meditative remembrance of God) and, remembering him again and again, find peace,
and rid my body of strife and anguish.
Let me remember the One, the Sustainer of the universe,
whose Naam (the Name, God's presence remembered) is repeated by multitudes beyond counting.
The Vedas, the Puranas and the Simritis
have held the one word of the Lord's Name to be the purest of words.
The one in whose heart God places even a particle of it
Some long for one thing only, the sight of you.
Says Nanak, save me along with them. ॥1॥
a01.rahao: Sukhmani, the jewel of peace, is God's Name, the nectar of peace.
It dwells in the minds of the devotees.
a01.p2: Through Simran of God, one does not come to lodge in the womb again.
Through Simran of God, sorrow and the messenger of Death flee.
Through Simran of God, death keeps away.
Through Simran of God, the enemy turns back.
While remembering God, no obstacle at all can touch one.
Through Simran of God, one stays awake night and day.
Through Simran of God, fear takes no hold.
Through Simran of God, pain does not torment.
Simran of God is found in the Saadh's company (the company of the holy one).
All treasures, O Nanak, are found in the Lord's love. ॥2॥
a01.p3: Through Simran of God come riches, spiritual powers and the nine treasures.
Through Simran of God come knowledge, meditation and insight into the essence.
Through Simran of God, one has performed chanting, austerity and worship.
Through Simran of God, duality is destroyed.
Through Simran of God, one has bathed at the places of pilgrimage.
Through Simran of God, one is honoured in the Lord's court.
Through Simran of God, whatever happens is good.
Through Simran of God, life bears its fruit in full.
They alone practise Simran whom God himself moves to it.
Says Nanak, I fall at their feet. ॥3॥
a01.p4: Simran of God is the highest of all.
Through Simran of God, multitudes have been saved.
Through Simran of God, craving is quenched.
Through Simran of God, everything becomes clear.
Through Simran of God, there is no terror of the messenger of Death.
Through Simran of God, hopes are fulfilled.
Through Simran of God, the mind's filth is washed away.
The ambrosial Naam settles in the heart.
God dwells on the tongue of the Saadh.
Nanak is the slave of the slaves of God's servants. ॥4॥
a01.p5: All who remember God are rich.
All who remember God are honoured.
All who remember God are accepted by him.
All who remember God are the foremost of people.
All who remember God depend on no one.
All who remember God are kings over all.
All who remember God dwell in peace.
All who remember God become forever imperishable.
They alone take to Simran to whom God himself is merciful.
Nanak begs for the dust of the feet of such a servant. ॥5॥
a01.p6: All who remember God do good to others.
To all who remember God I am a sacrifice, always.
All who remember God have radiant faces.
All who remember God pass their lives in peace.
All who remember God have conquered the self.
All who remember God live a spotless life.
All who remember God have joys in abundance.
All who remember God live close to the Lord.
By the grace of the Sant (saint), they stay awake night and day.
O Nanak, Simran comes through perfect good fortune. ॥6॥
a01.p7: Through Simran of God, one's tasks are accomplished.
Through Simran of God, one never grieves.
Through Simran of God, one utters the praises of the Lord.
Through Simran of God, one is absorbed in natural poise.
Through Simran of God, one gains a seat that never wavers.
Through Simran of God, the lotus of the heart blossoms.
Through Simran of God, the unstruck divine melody rings within.
The peace of Simran of God has no end and no limit.
They alone practise Simran on whom God has mercy.
Nanak has taken refuge with those servants. ॥7॥
a01.p8: By practising Simran of the Lord, the devotees became renowned.
Absorbed in Simran of the Lord, the sages brought forth the Vedas.
Through Simran of the Lord, people became Siddhas, celibates and givers.
Through Simran of the Lord, the lowly became known in all four directions.
Through Simran of the Lord, the whole earth is upheld.
Remember, remember the Lord, the Maker of all causes.
Through Simran of the Lord, all visible creation was made.
In Simran of the Lord, the Formless One himself is present.
When God, in his grace, has himself given someone understanding,
O Nanak, that Gurmukh (one who follows the Guru) has received Simran of the Lord. ॥8॥
a02.salok: O destroyer of the pain and sorrow of the poor, O Master present in every heart, Master of those who have none:
O God, in the company of Nanak (the Guru) I have come to your refuge. ॥1॥
a02.p1: Where there is no mother, father, son, friend or brother,
there, O mind, the Naam (the Name, God's presence remembered) is with you to help you.
Where the most dreadful messenger of Death would crush you,
there the Naam alone goes along with you.
Where the hardship is very heavy,
the Lord's Name rescues you in an instant.
Performing countless rites of atonement, one does not cross over.
The Lord's Name drives away millions of sins.
O my mind, repeat the Naam as a Gurmukh (one who follows the Guru).
Says Nanak, you will find joys in abundance. ॥1॥
a02.p2: Even a king of the whole world is unhappy.
Repeating the Lord's Name, he becomes happy.
Gathering hundreds of thousands and millions, one sets no bound to craving.
Repeating the Lord's Name, one is set free.
The countless pleasures of Maya (the world's illusion and lure) do not quench the thirst.
Repeating the Lord's Name, one is satisfied.
On the road where the soul travels alone,
there, with the Lord's Name beside it, it goes at ease.
O mind, meditate always on such a Naam.
O Nanak, as a Gurmukh one attains the supreme state. ॥2॥
a02.p3: Where one is not set free even by millions of helping arms,
there, repeating the Naam, people get across.
Where countless misfortunes come to destroy one,
the Lord's Name rescues at once.
Through countless species one is born, dies and is born again.
Repeating the Naam, one finds rest.
Soiled by Haumai (ego), one never washes the filth away.
The Lord's Name wipes out millions of sins.
O mind, repeat such a Naam with love.
O Nanak, it is found in the Saadh's company (the company of the holy one). ॥3॥
a02.p4: On the road whose miles cannot be counted,
the Lord's Name is your provision there.
On the journey that is pitch dark,
the Lord's Name goes with you as light.
On the path where no one knows you,
the Lord's Name is there with you as one who knows you.
Where there is fearful heat and a fierce sun,
there the Lord's Name gives you shade.
Where thirst, O mind, torments you,
there, O Nanak, the Lord's nectar, Har Har, rains down. ॥4॥
a02.p5: The Naam is what the devotees use every day.
It rests in the minds of the Sants (saints).
The Lord's Name is the shelter of his servant.
Through the Lord's Name millions of people have been saved.
The Sants sing the Lord's praise day and night.
The Saadhs make the Lord's Name, Har Har, their medicine.
The Lord's servant has the Lord's Name as his treasure.
The Supreme Lord has given it to his servant as a gift.
Their minds and bodies are dyed in the love of the One.
O Nanak, the servant's way is one of discernment. ॥5॥
a02.p6: To the servant, the Lord's Name is the way to liberation.
In the Lord's Name the servant finds contentment and his food.
The Lord's Name is the servant's beauty and delight.
Repeating the Lord's Name, he never meets an obstacle.
The Lord's Name is the servant's greatness.
Through the Lord's Name the servant has gained glory.
To the servant the Lord's Name is both enjoyment and Yoga.
Repeating the Lord's Name, he suffers no separation at all.
The servant is steeped in the service of the Lord's Name.
O Nanak, he worships the divine Lord, Har Har. ॥6॥
a02.p7: Har Har is the servant's wealth and treasure.
God himself has given the servant the wealth of the Lord.
Har Har is the servant's mighty shelter.
Through the Lord's glory, the servant knows no other.
Like warp and weft, through and through, his servants are steeped in the Lord's sweet essence.
In the deep stillness of Samadhi they are intoxicated with the taste of the Naam.
At all hours the servant repeats Har Har.
The Lord's devotee is known to all; he does not stay hidden.
Devotion to the Lord liberates many.
O Nanak, in the company of his servants so many have crossed over. ॥7॥
a02.p8: This Name of the Lord is the Parijat (the wish-fulfilling tree).
Singing the praises of Har Har is the Kamadhenu (the wish-fulfilling cow).
The discourse of the Lord is the most sublime of all.
When the Naam is heard, pain and sorrow fall away.
In the hearts of the Sants dwells the glory of the Naam.
Through the glory of the Sants all sin flees.
The company of the Sants is gained by great good fortune.
In the service of the Sants one meditates on the Naam.
Nothing else is equal to the Naam.
O Nanak, only a rare person, as a Gurmukh, obtains the Naam. ॥8॥
a03.salok: I have looked into many Shastras and many Simritis, searching through them all.
None of them equals Har, Haray: O Nanak, the Naam (the Name, God's presence remembered) is beyond price. ॥1॥
a03.p1: Chanting, austerities, all knowledge and meditation;
expounding the six Shastras and the Simritis;
the practice of Yoga, religious deeds and rites;
renouncing everything and wandering in the forest;
making many efforts of countless kinds;
good works, charity, and many jewels offered into the sacred fire;
having the body cut into tiny pieces and offering them into the fire;
keeping fasts and vows of many kinds:
none of these equals contemplation of the Lord's Name,
if, O Nanak, one repeats the Naam even once as a Gurmukh (one who follows the Guru). ॥1॥
a03.p2: One may roam the nine regions of the earth and live a long life;
become a great renunciant and a master of austerity;
offer one's life into the fire;
give gold, horses, the finest steeds and land in charity;
practise Neoli (the yogic cleansing of the bowels) and many postures;
follow the Jain way with its strict self-denial and disciplines;
have the body cut up bit by bit:
even then the filth of Haumai (ego) does not go.
O Nanak, repeating the Naam as Gurmukhs, people attain liberation. ॥2॥
a03.p3: One may give up the body at a place of pilgrimage with desire still in the mind,
yet pride and arrogance do not leave the mind.
One may perform cleansing rites day and night,
yet the mind's filth does not leave the body.
One may put this body through many disciplines,
yet the poison of Maya (the world's illusion and lure) never leaves the mind.
One may wash this perishable body with water again and again.
How can a wall of unbaked clay become clean?
O mind, the glory of the Lord's Name is high.
O Nanak, through the Naam a great multitude of the fallen have been saved. ॥3॥
a03.p4: For all one's cleverness, the fear of the messenger of Death still grips one.
For all one's countless efforts, craving is not satisfied.
For all the many religious garbs one wears, the fire within is not quenched.
For all one's millions of devices, one is not accepted in the Lord's court.
There is no escape, whether in the heavens above or in the underworld,
for those caught in attachment, in the net of Maya.
The messenger of Death punishes all other deeds.
Apart from devotion to Gobind (the Lord of the universe), he accepts not a particle.
Repeating the Lord's Name, pain departs.
Nanak utters it in natural poise and with love. ॥4॥
a03.p5: If anyone asks for the four great blessings of life,
let him take up the service of the Saadhs (holy ones).
If anyone would erase his own sorrow,
let him sing the Naam, Har Har, in his heart always.
If anyone longs for honour for himself,
in the Saadh Sangat (the company of the holy) let him give up this Haumai.
If anyone fears birth and death,
let him seek the refuge of the Saadhs.
To the one who thirsts for the sight of God,
says Nanak, I am a sacrifice, again and again. ॥5॥
a03.p6: Among all people, that person is foremost,
whose pride is erased in the Saadh Sangat.
he is reckoned the highest of all.
One whose mind becomes the dust of all,
he has recognised the Naam, Har Har, in every heart.
One who has erased evil from his own mind,
he looks on the whole creation as a friend.
The servant who sees joy and sorrow alike,
O Nanak, he is touched by neither sin nor virtue. ॥6॥
a03.p7: Your Name is wealth to those who have none.
Your Name is a place for those who have no place.
To those without honour, O God, you give honour.
You give your gifts to all beings.
O Master, you do and cause all to be done.
You know what is within every heart.
Your own state and extent only you know.
O God, you are steeped in yourself.
Your praise comes from you alone.
O Nanak, no one else knows it. ॥7॥
a03.p8: Of all religious duties, the highest duty is this:
repeat the Lord's Name and keep your conduct pure.
Of all rites, the most sublime rite is this:
to have the filth of an evil mind washed away in the Saadh Sangat.
Of all efforts, the good effort is this:
repeat the Lord's Name in your heart always.
Of all words, the words of nectar are these:
hearing the Lord's praise, speak it with your tongue.
Of all places, that place is most sublime,
O Nanak, the heart in which the Lord's Name dwells. ॥8॥
a04.salok: O worthless, ignorant one, keep that God always in your thoughts.
Hold in your mind the one who made you; says Nanak, he will stand by you. ॥1॥
a04.p1: O mortal, call to mind the virtues of the all-pervading Lord:
from what beginning he has brought you to how you now appear.
He fashioned you, shaped you and adorned you;
he kept you safe in the fire of the womb;
in childhood he fed you with milk;
in the fullness of youth, food, comfort and understanding;
when you grew old, kin and friends were there to tend you,
and put food into your mouth as you sat.
This worthless one does not appreciate any of these kindnesses.
Should you, Lord, forgive him, says Nanak, then he wins through. ॥1॥
a04.p2: By whose grace you live in comfort on the earth,
and laugh with your sons, brothers, friends and wife;
by whose grace you drink cool water,
and have the soothing air and priceless fire;
by whose grace you enjoy every pleasure,
and live with all things at hand;
who gave you hands and feet, ears, eyes and a tongue:
forsaking him, you are absorbed in others.
Such faults grip the blind fools.
Says Nanak, O God, pull them out yourself. ॥2॥
a04.p3: God is the protector from the beginning to the end,
yet the ignorant fool does not love him.
Serving him one obtains the nine treasures,
yet the fool does not set his mind on him.
The Master is ever and always present,
yet the blind man thinks him far away.
Serving him one is honoured in the Lord's court,
yet the ignorant simpleton forgets him.
Forever and ever this mortal goes astray.
O Nanak, the Protector is infinite. ॥3॥
a04.p4: Casting aside the jewel, he is engrossed in a cowrie shell.
Leaving the truth, he revels in falsehood.
What he must leave behind, he takes to be lasting.
What is sure to come, he believes to be far off.
He toils for what he will leave as he goes.
He forsakes the one who is his companion and helper.
He washes off the sandalwood paste.
Like the donkey's, his love is for ashes.
He has fallen into the dark and dreadful pit.
Says Nanak, O merciful God, pull him out. ॥4॥
a04.p5: His deeds are those of a beast, though he is born human.
Day and night he puts on a show for people.
Outside he wears a holy garb; inside is the filth of Maya (the world's illusion and lure).
However he tries to hide it, nothing stays hidden.
Outwardly there is knowledge, meditation and ritual bathing.
Within, the dog of greed has hold of him.
Within is fire; outside, the body is smeared with ashes.
With a stone around his neck, how can he cross the bottomless ocean?
Those within whom God himself dwells,
O Nanak, those people are absorbed in natural poise. ॥5॥
a04.p6: How can a blind man find the road by hearing alone?
Take him by the hand, and he is carried through to the end.
How can the deaf understand a riddle?
Say night, and he takes it for day.
How can the mute sing hymns to the Lord?
Even if he tries, his voice breaks.
How can the lame roam about on a mountain?
O Creator, full of compassion, this humble one makes his prayer:
Nanak crosses over by your grace alone. ॥6॥
a04.p7: The one who is his companion and helper does not come to his mind.
He loves the one who is his enemy.
He lives inside a house of sand.
He revels in games of pleasure and the delights of Maya.
He takes it all to be lasting; such is the belief in his mind.
Death does not come to the fool's mind.
lies, vice, great greed and deceit:
in these ways many lifetimes have passed.
Says Nanak, Lord, by your own grace, save him. ॥7॥
a04.p8: You are the Master; to you is my prayer.
Soul and body alike are your capital.
You are mother and father to us; we are your children.
Your grace holds joys in abundance.
O Lord God, you are higher than the highest.
All creation rests on your thread.
What comes from you obeys your command.
Your state and extent only you know.
Your servant Nanak is ever a sacrifice to you. ॥8॥
a05.salok: Those who leave God, the Giver, and attach themselves to other pursuits,
O Nanak, they never succeed anywhere; without the Naam (the Name, God's presence remembered), their honour is lost. ॥1॥
a05.p1: He takes ten things and puts them out of mind.
Over one thing he loses his good faith.
If God gave not even that one, and took away the ten as well,
then tell me, what could the fool do?
The Master against whom no one has any power,
to him one should always bow.
When God seems sweet to someone's mind,
all joys come to dwell in that mind.
The servant whom God brings to accept his Hukam (God's will and command),
O Nanak, he has obtained all things. ॥1॥
a05.p2: The Banker hands over his capital beyond counting.
The man eats, drinks and spends it with joy and delight.
If the Banker takes back some of what he had placed in trust,
the ignorant man feels resentment in his mind.
He destroys his own credit himself.
If one places the thing before the one it belongs to,
and accepts God's order with bowed head,
God makes him four times happier than before.
O Nanak, the Master is ever merciful. ॥2॥
a05.p3: Attachments to Maya (the world's illusion and lure) are of countless kinds.
Know that they are sure to pass away.
One falls in love with the shade of a tree.
The shade passes, and he regrets it in his mind.
Whatever is seen will pass away.
Yet one utterly blind clings to it.
One who gives his love to a passing traveller,
he is left with nothing in his hands.
O mind, love of the Lord's Name brings peace.
O Nanak, God in his grace himself attaches one to it. ॥3॥
a05.p4: Vain are the body, wealth and the whole family.
Vain are Haumai (ego), possessiveness and Maya.
Vain are power, youth, riches and property.
Vain are lust and dreadful anger.
Vain are chariots and elephants, horses and fine clothes.
Vain is the laughter of one who sees Maya and delights in its pleasures.
Vain are deceit, attachment and pride.
Vain is the conceit one has about oneself.
Lasting are devotion and refuge with the Saadh (holy one).
Nanak lives by dwelling, again and again, on the Lord's feet. ॥4॥
a05.p5: Vain are the ears that listen to slander of others.
Vain are the hands that steal what others own.
Vain are the eyes that gaze at the beauty of another man's wife.
Vain is the tongue that is given to food and other tastes.
Vain are the feet that run to do harm to others.
Vain is the mind that is lured by greed for what belongs to others.
Vain is the body that does no good to others.
Vain is the nose that takes in the scent of corruption.
Without understanding, all of these are in vain.
O Nanak, fruitful is the body that takes the Name of the Lord, Har Har. ॥5॥
a05.p6: Wasted is the life of the Saakat (one who has turned from God).
How can anyone become pure without the True One?
Wasted is the body of the blind without the Naam.
A foul smell comes from his mouth.
Without Simran (meditative remembrance of God), day and night pass in waste,
as a crop is lost without rain.
Without devotion to Gobind (the Lord of the universe), all deeds are wasted,
like the useless money of a miser.
Blessed, blessed are those people in whose hearts the Lord's Name dwells.
Says Nanak, I am a sacrifice to them, again and again. ॥6॥
a05.p7: His way of life is one thing, and what he practises is another.
In his mind there is no love, yet his mouth spins tall talk.
God, the Knower, is wise in all things.
He is not won over by anyone's outward garb.
One who preaches to others but does not practise it himself,
he keeps coming and going, being born and dying.
When the Formless Lord dwells within someone,
by his teaching the world crosses over.
Those who please you have known God.
Nanak falls at the feet of those people. ॥7॥
a05.p8: I offer my prayer to the Supreme Lord, who knows everything.
He himself honours what he has made.
He himself, all by himself, settles every matter.
To some he makes himself seem far away; to others he shows that he is near.
He is beyond all devices and cleverness.
He knows everything about the soul's way of living.
Whomever he pleases, he attaches to the hem of his robe.
He pervades every place and every space between.
That one alone is a servant on whom God has shown grace.
Says Nanak, repeat the Lord's Name at every instant. ॥8॥
a06.salok: May lust, anger, greed, attachment and egotism be destroyed.
Nanak seeks the refuge of God: O divine Guru, grant your grace. ॥1॥
a06.p1: By whose grace you eat the thirty-six delicacies,
keep that Master in your mind.
By whose grace you put perfumes on your body,
remembering him, you will attain the supreme state.
By whose grace you live in a palace of comfort,
meditate on him always within your mind.
By whose grace you live happily with your household,
remember him with your tongue at all hours.
By whose grace there are pleasures, tastes and enjoyments,
O Nanak, one should meditate always on him, the one worthy of meditation. ॥1॥
a06.p2: By whose grace you dress in silk and fine cloth,
why forsake him and be lured by others?
By whose grace one sleeps in comfort on a bed,
O mind, sing his praise at all hours.
By whose grace everyone honours you,
tell his praise with your mouth and tongue.
By whose grace your dharma, your righteous way, remains,
O mind, meditate always on the Supreme Lord alone.
Repeating the Name of God, you will be honoured in his court.
Says Nanak, you will go home with honour. ॥2॥
a06.p3: By whose grace your body is healthy and golden,
attune yourself in love to that Lord, your loving friend.
By whose grace your honour stays shielded,
O mind, you will find peace in telling the praise of Har Har.
By whose grace all your faults are covered,
O mind, seek the refuge of that God, the Master.
By whose grace no one can equal you,
O mind, remember the lofty God with every breath.
By whose grace you obtained this body, so hard to obtain,
says Nanak, worship him with devotion. ॥3॥
a06.p4: By whose grace one wears ornaments,
O mind, why be lazy in remembering him?
By whose grace you ride horses and elephants,
O mind, do not ever forget that God.
By whose grace you have gardens, lands and wealth,
keep God woven into your mind.
O mind, the one who gave you your shape:
rising or sitting, meditate on him always.
Meditate on him who is One and beyond sight.
Says Nanak, here and hereafter he will keep your honour. ॥4॥
a06.p5: By whose grace you do good works and give much in charity,
O mind, meditate on him at all hours.
By whose grace you keep up religious conduct and worldly dealings,
think of that God with every breath.
By whose grace your form is beautiful,
remember always that God, beyond compare.
By whose grace you are of good birth,
remember that God always, day and night.
By whose grace your honour is kept,
by the Guru's grace Nanak speaks his praise. ॥5॥
a06.p6: By whose grace your ears hear sound,
by whose grace you behold wonders,
by whose grace your tongue speaks words of nectar,
by whose grace you live in comfort and natural ease,
by whose grace your hands move and do their work,
by whose grace you prosper in every way,
by whose grace you attain the supreme state,
by whose grace you merge into peace and natural poise:
why leave such a God and cling to another?
By the Guru's grace, says Nanak, be awake within your mind. ॥6॥
a06.p7: By whose grace you are known in the world,
never put that God out of your mind at all.
By whose grace you have glory,
O foolish mind, repeat his Name.
By whose grace your tasks are accomplished,
O mind, know him to be ever present.
By whose grace you attain the Truth,
O my mind, be absorbed in him.
By whose grace all are liberated,
O Nanak, one repeats his Name, his alone. ॥7॥
a06.p8: He whom God himself moves to repeat it repeats the Name.
He whom God himself moves to sing sings the praises of the Lord.
Through God's grace, light dawns within.
Through God's mercy, the lotus of the heart blossoms.
When God is well pleased, he makes his home in the mind.
Through God's mercy, the intellect becomes sublime.
All treasures, O God, lie in your mercy.
By their own effort no one has gained anything.
To whatever you attach them, to that they are attached, O Lord and Master.
O Nanak, nothing is in their own hands. ॥8॥
a07.salok: That Supreme Lord is beyond reach and beyond measure.
Whoever speaks of him is set free.
wondrous is the account of the Saadhs (holy ones). ॥1॥
a07.p1: In the Saadh's company, faces become radiant.
In the Saadh Sangat (the company of the holy), all filth is washed away.
In the Saadh's company, pride is erased.
In the Saadh's company, true wisdom dawns.
In the Saadh's company, one realises that God is near.
In the Saadh Sangat, everything is settled.
In the Saadh's company, one gains the jewel of the Naam (the Name, God's presence remembered).
In the Saadh's company, one's effort is directed to the One.
What mortal can describe the greatness of the Saadh?
O Nanak, the glory of the Saadh is merged in God. ॥1॥
a07.p2: In the Saadh's company, one meets the Lord who is beyond the senses.
In the Saadh's company, one is ever in bloom.
In the Saadh's company, the five passions come under control.
In the Saadh Sangat, one savours the taste of nectar.
In the Saadh Sangat, one becomes the dust under everyone's feet.
In the Saadh's company, one's words become pleasing.
In the Saadh's company, the mind does not run off anywhere.
In the Saadh Sangat, the mind finds steadiness.
In the Saadh's company, one stays apart from Maya (the world's illusion and lure).
In the Saadh Sangat, O Nanak, God is well pleased. ॥2॥
a07.p3: In the Saadh Sangat, all enemies become friends.
In the Saadh's company, one becomes supremely pure.
In the Saadh Sangat, one bears enmity towards no one.
In the Saadh's company, the feet do not stray onto a crooked path.
In the Saadh's company, no one seems bad.
In the Saadh Sangat, one comes to know God, the supreme bliss.
In the Saadh's company, the fever of Haumai (ego) is gone.
In the Saadh's company, one gives up all sense of self.
Only God himself knows the Saadh's greatness.
O Nanak, a deep bond of love has formed between the Saadh and God. ॥3॥
a07.p4: In the Saadh's company, one never goes astray.
In the Saadh's company, one finds lasting peace.
In the Saadh Sangat, one attains that which is beyond the senses.
In the Saadh's company, one bears the unbearable.
In the Saadh's company, one dwells in the highest place.
In the Saadh's company, one reaches God's mansion.
In the Saadh's company, every righteous duty takes firm root.
In the Saadh's company, one's attention rests on the Supreme Lord alone.
In the Saadh's company, one gains the treasure of the Naam.
Nanak is a sacrifice to the Saadh. ॥4॥
a07.p5: In the Saadh's company, one redeems one's whole family line.
In the Saadh Sangat, one carries loved ones, friends and family across.
In the Saadh's company, one obtains that wealth,
In the Saadh Sangat, Dharam Rai (the judge of souls) serves one.
In the Saadh's company, the gods sing one's praise.
In the Saadh's company, sins take flight.
In the Saadh Sangat, the nectar-sweet praises of God are sung.
In the Saadh's company, every place is within reach.
O Nanak, in the Saadh's company, one's birth bears fruit. ॥5॥
a07.p6: In the Saadh's company, no toil at all is needed.
On gaining the sight of the Saadh, one is filled with bliss.
In the Saadh's company, all stains are taken away.
In the Saadh's company, hell is left far behind.
In the Saadh's company, one is at ease here and hereafter.
In the Saadh Sangat, those separated are united with the Lord.
Whatever one longs for, that very fruit one receives.
In the Saadh's company, no one goes away empty-handed.
The Supreme Lord dwells in the heart of the Saadh.
O Nanak, one is saved by hearing the Saadh's words and delighting in them. ॥6॥
a07.p7: In the Saadh's company, I hear the Lord's Name.
In the Saadh Sangat, I sing the Lord's praises.
In the Saadh's company, God does not slip from the mind.
In the Saadh Sangat, one is surely carried across.
In the Saadh's company, God feels sweet.
In the Saadh's company, he is seen in every heart.
In the Saadh Sangat, we have become obedient to God.
In the Saadh Sangat, we have been set free.
In the Saadh's company, all ailments have gone.
O Nanak, the Saadh is met by good fortune. ॥7॥
a07.p8: The Vedas do not know the greatness of the Saadh.
They describe only as much as they have heard.
The Saadh's likeness is beyond the three qualities of Maya (nothing made of them compares);
the Saadh can be likened only to the all-pervading Lord.
The glory of the Saadh has no end.
The glory of the Saadh is boundless for ever.
The glory of the Saadh is higher than the highest.
The glory of the Saadh is greater than the greatest.
The glory of the Saadh befits the Saadh alone.
O Nanak, between the Saadh and God there is no distinction, brother. ॥8॥
a08.salok: He has the True One in his mind and that same True One on his lips.
He sees no one but the One.
O Nanak, whoever bears these marks is a Brahm Giani (one who knows God). ॥1॥
a08.p1: The Brahm Giani is ever unattached,
as the lotus stays untouched in the water.
The Brahm Giani is ever without blemish,
as the sun dries up all things yet stays untainted.
The Brahm Giani looks on all alike,
as the wind touches king and pauper the same.
The Brahm Giani's patience never changes,
like the earth: one man digs it, another anoints it with sandal paste.
This is the Brahm Giani's quality,
O Nanak, like the innate nature of fire (to burn away all impurity). ॥1॥
a08.p2: The Brahm Giani is purer than the pure,
as dirt does not cling to water.
The Brahm Giani's mind is filled with light,
like the sky above the earth.
The Brahm Giani holds friend and foe alike.
The Brahm Giani has no pride.
The Brahm Giani is higher than the highest,
yet in his own mind he is the lowliest of all.
Those alone have become Brahm Gianis,
O Nanak, whom God himself has made so. ॥2॥
a08.p3: The Brahm Giani is the dust under everyone's feet.
The Brahm Giani has come to know the joy of the soul.
The Brahm Giani is kind to all.
The Brahm Giani never does anything bad.
The Brahm Giani ever sees all with an equal eye.
The Brahm Giani's glance rains nectar.
The Brahm Giani is free of all bonds.
The Brahm Giani's way of life is pure.
The Brahm Giani's food is divine wisdom.
O Nanak, the Brahm Giani's meditation is fixed on God. ॥3॥
a08.p4: The Brahm Giani places his hope in the One alone.
The Brahm Giani is filled with humility.
The Brahm Giani is eager to do good to others.
The Brahm Giani is not caught up in worldly affairs.
The Brahm Giani catches the wandering mind and keeps it bound.
To the Brahm Giani, whatever happens is good.
The Brahm Giani is richly fruitful.
In the Brahm Giani's company, everyone is saved.
O Nanak, through the Brahm Giani the whole world repeats God's Name. ॥4॥
a08.p5: The Brahm Giani is dyed in the love of the One alone.
The Brahm Giani has God abiding with him.
The Brahm Giani's support is the Naam (the Name, God's presence remembered).
The Brahm Giani's family is the Naam.
The Brahm Giani is awake for ever and ever.
The Brahm Giani casts off the ego-bound intellect.
The Brahm Giani's mind holds supreme bliss.
The Brahm Giani's home is ever filled with joy.
The Brahm Giani dwells in peace and poise.
O Nanak, the Brahm Giani never perishes. ॥5॥
a08.p6: The Brahm Giani is the knower of God.
The Brahm Giani loves the One alone.
The Brahm Giani is free of worry.
The Brahm Giani's counsel is pure.
The Brahm Giani is one whom God himself makes so.
The Brahm Giani's majesty is great.
The sight of the Brahm Giani is gained by great good fortune.
To the Brahm Giani one should give oneself in sacrifice again and again.
The Brahm Giani is sought even by Shiva, the great lord.
O Nanak, the Brahm Giani is himself the Supreme God. ॥6॥
a08.p7: The Brahm Giani's worth cannot be reckoned.
The Brahm Giani holds everything within his mind.
Who knows the secret of the Brahm Giani?
To the Brahm Giani, salutations for ever.
Not even half a syllable can be said about the Brahm Giani.
The Brahm Giani is the Master of all.
Who can tell the measure of the Brahm Giani?
Only a Brahm Giani knows the state of a Brahm Giani.
The Brahm Giani has no end and no limit.
O Nanak, salutations for ever to the Brahm Giani. ॥7॥
a08.p8: The Brahm Giani is the creator of the whole world.
The Brahm Giani lives for ever and does not die.
The Brahm Giani gives souls the way to liberation.
The Brahm Giani is the perfect Being, the Maker of destiny.
The Brahm Giani is the guardian of those who have none.
The Brahm Giani's hand is over all.
The whole visible creation belongs to the Brahm Giani.
The Brahm Giani is himself the Formless Lord.
The Brahm Giani's glory befits the Brahm Giani alone.
O Nanak, the Brahm Giani is the Lord of all. ॥8॥
a09.salok: One who enshrines the Naam (the Name, God's presence remembered) deep within the heart,
who sees the Lord in everything,
who bows to the Master every moment:
O Nanak, that one is an Apras (one untouched by evil), and he carries everyone across. ॥1॥
a09.p1: Falsehood does not touch his tongue.
In his mind is love for the sight of the Immaculate Lord.
His eyes do not gaze at the beauty of another's wife.
He serves the Saadh (holy one) and loves the company of the Sants (saints).
His ears do not listen to slander of anyone.
He considers himself the worst of all.
By the Guru's grace he casts off the poison of Maya (the world's illusion and lure).
The desires of his mind depart from his mind.
He has conquered his senses and is free of the five vices.
O Nanak, among millions there is hardly one such Apras. ॥1॥
a09.p2: He alone is a Vaishnav (a devotee of Vishnu) with whom God is well pleased.
He stays apart from the Maya of Vishnu (the all-pervading Lord).
While doing his deeds, he stays free of their bondage.
Pure is the faith of such a Vaishnav.
He wishes for no reward of any kind.
He is absorbed only in devotion and Kirtan (songs of God's praise).
Within his mind and body is Simran (meditative remembrance of God) of Gopal (the sustainer of the world).
He holds firmly to the Naam himself and leads others to repeat it.
O Nanak, such a Vaishnav attains the supreme state. ॥2॥
a09.p3: A Bhagauti (a worshipper of the Lord) is one imbued with love for devotion to the Lord.
He forsakes all company of the wicked.
All doubt is gone from his mind.
He worships the Supreme Lord, knowing him to be in all.
In the Saadh Sangat (the company of the holy), he washes off the filth of sin.
Such a Bhagauti's understanding becomes sublime.
He serves the Lord constantly, day after day.
He offers his mind and body in love of the all-pervading Lord.
He enshrines the Lord's feet in his heart.
O Nanak, a Bhagauti like this finds the Lord. ॥3॥
a09.p4: That one is a Pandit (a learned man) who teaches his own mind;
who searches his own self for the Lord's Name;
who drinks the sublime essence of the Lord's Name.
Through that Pandit's teaching the world finds life.
He keeps the Lord's praise in his heart.
Such a Pandit does not enter the womb again.
He understands the root of the Vedas, the Puranas and the Simritis.
He knows the manifest to lie within the unmanifest.
He gives teaching to all four castes.
O Nanak, to that Pandit, salutations for ever. ॥4॥
a09.p5: The seed mantra, the Naam, is wisdom for all.
Among the four castes, anyone may repeat the Naam.
In the Saadh Sangat, some rare person obtains it.
By his grace, God enshrines it deep within the heart.
It carries across even beasts, ghosts, fools and the stone-hearted.
The Naam is the remedy for every ailment.
Singing God's praises is the very form of well-being and joy.
It is not obtained by any technique or by any religious rite.
O Nanak, it is obtained by one for whom it was written from the beginning, by God's grace. ॥5॥
a09.p6: One in whose mind the Supreme Lord dwells:
his name is truly Ramdas (the Lord's servant).
The Lord, the Soul of all, has come into his sight.
He has found him in the spirit of a servant of servants.
He knows the Lord to be ever near, very near.
Such a servant is accepted in the Lord's court.
God himself shows grace to his servant.
That servant comes to understand everything.
Amid all, his soul stays detached.
Such, O Nanak, is the way of a Ramdas. ॥6॥
a09.p7: One who holds God's command dear in his soul,
he is called Jivan Mukat (liberated while alive).
To him joy is the same as sorrow.
He is ever in bliss; there is no separation there.
To him gold is the same as dust.
Nectar is the same as bitter poison.
Honour is the same as scorn.
A beggar is the same as a king.
Whatever God brings about, he takes as his way.
O Nanak, that person is called Jivan Mukat. ॥7॥
a09.p8: All places belong to the Supreme Lord.
In whatever home he places beings, such is the name they bear.
He himself is able to do and to cause all to be done.
Whatever pleases God, that in the end comes to pass.
He himself has spread out, becoming endless waves.
The ways of the Supreme Lord cannot be grasped.
Such understanding as he gives, such is one's light.
The Supreme Lord, the Creator, is imperishable.
He is merciful for ever, for ever, for ever.
Those who remember him in Simran again and again, O Nanak, are filled with bliss. ॥8॥
a10.salok: Countless people sing his praises, but there is no end or limit to him.
O Nanak, God has fashioned the creation in many ways and in countless forms. ॥1॥
a10.p1: Millions upon millions have become worshippers.
Millions upon millions observe religious rites and customary duties.
Millions upon millions have come to live at places of pilgrimage.
Millions upon millions wander in the forests as renunciants.
Millions upon millions are listeners to the Vedas.
Millions upon millions are great ascetics.
Millions upon millions fix their meditation within the self.
Millions upon millions are the poets who reflect on poetry.
Millions upon millions meditate on his ever-new Naam (the Name, God's presence remembered).
O Nanak, they do not find the Creator's limit. ॥1॥
a10.p2: Millions upon millions have become proud.
Millions upon millions are blind and ignorant.
Millions upon millions are hard-hearted misers.
Millions upon millions are unsoftened, their souls utterly dry.
Millions upon millions steal what belongs to others.
Millions upon millions toil after Maya (the world's illusion and lure).
Millions upon millions roam in foreign lands.
Whatever you, God, set them to, to that they hold.
O Nanak, the Creator alone knows the Creator's creation. ॥2॥
a10.p3: Millions upon millions are Siddhas, celibates and yogis.
Millions upon millions are kings enjoying pleasures.
Millions upon millions are the birds and snakes he has created.
Millions upon millions are the stones and trees he has brought forth.
Millions upon millions are winds, waters and fires.
Millions upon millions are countries and realms of the earth.
Millions upon millions are moons, suns and stars.
Millions upon millions are the gods, demons and Indras with royal canopies over their heads.
He holds the whole creation strung on his own thread.
O Nanak, whoever pleases him, he carries across. ॥3॥
a10.p4: Millions upon millions are of the qualities of passion, darkness and purity.
Millions upon millions are the Vedas, Puranas, Simritis and Shastras.
Millions upon millions are the jewels and oceans he has made.
Millions upon millions are creatures of every kind.
Millions upon millions are those he has made long-lived.
Millions upon millions are the hills and golden Merus that came to be.
Millions upon millions are yakshas, kinnars and fiends.
Millions upon millions are spirits, ghosts, swine and beasts of prey.
He is close to all and distant from all.
O Nanak, he himself, remaining detached, pervades everything. ॥4॥
a10.p5: Millions upon millions dwell in the nether worlds.
Millions upon millions live in hell and in heaven.
Millions upon millions are born, live and die.
Millions upon millions go round through many births.
Millions upon millions eat while simply sitting at ease.
Millions upon millions toil until they are worn out.
Millions upon millions are those he has made rich.
Millions upon millions are anxious over Maya.
Wherever he wills, there he keeps them.
O Nanak, everything is in God's hands. ॥5॥
a10.p6: Millions upon millions have become detached from the world.
Their minds are lovingly fixed on the Lord's Name.
Millions upon millions search for God.
They find the Supreme Lord within their own selves.
Millions upon millions thirst for the sight of God.
The imperishable God has met them.
Millions upon millions pray for the Satsang (the company of the true).
They are dyed in the love of the Supreme Lord.
Those with whom he himself is well pleased,
O Nanak, they are ever blessed, blessed. ॥6॥
a10.p7: Millions upon millions are the sources of life and the regions of the world.
Millions upon millions are the skies and universes.
Millions upon millions are the incarnations that have come to be.
In many ways he has unfolded creation.
Many times he has spread out its expanse.
Ever and always there is the One, Ekankar (the One Creator).
Millions upon millions he has made, of many kinds.
From God they came forth, and into God they merge.
O Nanak, that God is himself all in all. ॥7॥
a10.p8: Millions upon millions are servants of the Supreme Lord.
Millions upon millions are knowers of the essence.
With their eyes they behold the One alone, always.
Millions upon millions drink the nectar of the Naam.
They have become deathless and live on for ever and ever.
Millions upon millions sing the Naam's praises.
They are merged in the joy of the soul, in peace and poise.
He keeps his servants in mind with every breath.
O Nanak, they are dear to the Supreme God. ॥8॥
a11.salok: The One God is the cause of all creation; there is no second at all.
Nanak is a sacrifice to him who is in the water, on the land, and in the space between earth and sky. ॥1॥
a11.p1: He does and causes all to be done, and is able to do all.
Whatever pleases him, that alone will happen.
In an instant he establishes and overthrows.
He has no end or limit at all.
By his Hukam (God's will and command) he has set up the earth and holds it without support.
By his Hukam all comes forth, and in his Hukam it merges.
By his Hukam there are dealings high and low.
By his Hukam there are countless colours and kinds.
Having made it all, he looks upon his own greatness.
a11.p2: If it pleases God, a human being attains liberation.
If it pleases God, he makes even stones float.
If it pleases God, he keeps a being alive even without breath.
If it pleases God, one tells of the Lord's virtues.
If it pleases God, he saves even the fallen.
He himself acts and he himself deliberates.
He himself is Master of this world and the next.
The Knower of hearts plays and rejoices.
As he pleases, he has the work done.
O Nanak, no other comes into sight. ॥2॥
a11.p3: Say, what can be achieved by a human being?
Whatever pleases God, that he makes one do.
If it were in this man's hands, he would seize everything.
Whatever pleases God, that alone he does.
Unknowing, one is engrossed in the poison of Maya (the world's illusion and lure).
If one knew, one would save oneself.
Led astray by doubt, one runs in all ten directions.
In an instant one goes round the four corners and comes back.
Those to whom God, in his mercy, gives his devotion,
O Nanak, they merge in the Naam (the Name, God's presence remembered). ॥3॥
a11.p4: In an instant he gives a kingdom to a lowly worm.
The Supreme Lord cherishes the humble.
One in whom nothing at all was to be seen,
he at once makes known in all ten directions.
One to whom he grants his blessing,
the Lord of the world keeps no reckoning of his deeds.
Soul and body, all is his capital.
In every heart is the light of the perfect God.
He himself has fashioned his own creation.
Nanak lives by beholding his greatness. ॥4॥
a11.p5: The strength of this being is not in its own hands.
The Master of all does and causes all to be done.
The poor creature is bound to obey.
Whatever pleases him, that in the end comes to pass.
Sometimes one dwells in high estate, sometimes in low.
Sometimes one is in sorrow, and sometimes one laughs in the delight of joy.
Sometimes one is busy with slander and worry.
Sometimes one is high in the heavens, sometimes in the nether world.
Sometimes one becomes versed in reflection on God.
O Nanak, God himself is the one who unites one with him. ॥5॥
a11.p6: Sometimes one dances in many ways.
Sometimes one stays asleep day and night.
Sometimes one is fearsome in great anger.
Sometimes one becomes the dust under everyone's feet.
Sometimes one sits as a great king.
Sometimes one wears the guise of a lowly beggar.
Sometimes one falls into ill repute.
Sometimes one is called good, very good.
As God keeps one, so one remains.
By the Guru's grace, O Nanak, one speaks the truth. ॥6॥
a11.p7: Sometimes one becomes a Pandit and gives discourses.
Sometimes one keeps silence and sits in meditation.
Sometimes one bathes on the banks of pilgrimage places.
Sometimes, as a Siddha or a seeker, one speaks wisdom.
Sometimes one becomes a worm, an elephant or a moth.
Deluded, one wanders through countless species.
Like an actor, one shows many forms.
As it pleases God, so he makes one dance.
Whatever pleases him, that alone happens.
O Nanak, there is no one else, no second. ॥7॥
a11.p8: Sometimes this being finds the Saadh Sangat (the company of the holy).
He does not come back again from there.
Within, the light of divine wisdom shines.
Mind and body are imbued with the Naam, in the love of the One.
They dwell for ever with the Supreme Lord.
As water flows into water and becomes one with it,
so one's light merges into the Light.
The comings and goings are ended; rest is found.
Nanak is ever a sacrifice to God. ॥8॥
a12.salok: The humble one lives in peace, having subdued the self and keeping low.
The mighty and arrogant, O Nanak, rot away in their own pride. ॥1॥
a12.p1: One who holds within himself the pride of power,
he is bound for hell and becomes a dog.
One who thinks himself full of youth and beauty,
he becomes a maggot in filth.
One who calls himself a doer of good deeds,
he is born and dies and wanders through many species.
One who is proud of wealth and land,
he is a fool, blind and ignorant.
One in whose heart God, in his mercy, places humility,
O Nanak, he is liberated here and finds peace hereafter. ॥1॥
a12.p2: One grows rich and becomes proud,
yet not even a straw goes with him.
One puts his hope in large armies and men.
In a moment he is destroyed.
One thinks himself the strongest of all.
In an instant he is reduced to ashes.
The arrogant one cares for no one.
Dharam Rai (the judge of souls) puts him to disgrace.
One whose pride is erased by the Guru's grace:
that person, O Nanak, is accepted in the Lord's court. ॥2॥
a12.p3: One may do millions of good deeds while holding on to Haumai (ego).
He gains only toil, and all of it is in vain.
One may do many penances in pride.
He is born again and again into hell and heaven.
For all his many efforts, his soul does not soften.
Tell me, how can he reach the Lord's court?
One whose mind becomes the dust under everyone's feet,
says Nanak, he has a spotless name. ॥3॥
a12.p4: As long as one thinks that anything can be done by him,
he has no peace at all.
As long as he thinks that he is the doer of anything,
he wanders through wombs and births.
As long as he holds one man as enemy and another as friend,
As long as he is lost in attachment to Maya (the world's illusion and lure),
By God's grace the bonds break.
By the Guru's grace, O Nanak, Haumai falls away. ॥4॥
a12.p5: Having earned a thousand, he sets off running after a hundred thousand.
Satisfaction does not come; he keeps storing up Maya.
He indulges in countless pleasures of corruption.
He is not satisfied; he wears himself out and dies.
Without contentment no one is fulfilled.
All his works are in vain, like wishes in a dream.
In the love of the Naam (the Name, God's presence remembered), all peace is found.
Only some rare person, by great good fortune, obtains it.
He himself, he alone, does and causes all to be done.
For ever and ever, says Nanak, repeat the Lord's Name. ॥5॥
a12.p6: The Creator alone does and causes all to be done.
What decision lies in this creature's hands?
As he casts his glance, so one becomes.
That God himself is all in all.
Whatever he made, he made in his own pleasure.
He is distant from all, and close beside all.
He understands, he sees, he judges.
He is himself one, and himself many.
He neither dies nor perishes; he neither comes nor goes.
O Nanak, he ever pervades all. ॥6॥
a12.p7: He himself teaches and he himself understands.
He himself is blended with all.
He himself has made his own expanse.
Everything is his; he is the Doer.
Tell me, can anything be apart from him?
In every place and the spaces between, he is the One alone.
He himself performs his own plays.
He stages wonders of endless colour.
He is within the mind, and holds the mind within himself.
O Nanak, no one can state his worth. ॥7॥
a12.p8: True, true, true is God, the Master.
By the Guru's grace some rare one describes him.
True, true, true is all that he has made.
Among millions, only some rare one has recognised him.
Good, good, good is your form,
Pure, pure, pure is your Word.
In every heart it is heard by the ears and spoken.
Holy, holy, holy and pure is the one
who, O Nanak, repeats the Naam with love in the mind. ॥8॥
a13.salok: Whoever comes to the refuge of a Sant (saint) is saved.
O Nanak, by slandering a Sant one is born again and again. ॥1॥
a13.p1: By slandering a Sant, one's life is cut short.
By slandering a Sant, one is not freed from the messenger of Death.
By slandering a Sant, all peace departs.
By slandering a Sant, one falls into hell.
By slandering a Sant, the intellect becomes defiled.
By slandering a Sant, one is left without honour.
No one can protect one whom a Sant has cast off.
By slandering a Sant, one falls from one's place.
If the compassionate Sant shows grace,
then, O Nanak, in the company of the Sants even the slanderer crosses over. ॥1॥
a13.p2: By slandering a Sant, one's face becomes twisted.
By slandering the Sants, one caws like a crow.
By slandering the Sants, one is born as a snake.
By slandering a Sant, one is born among crawling creatures and wriggles like a worm.
By slandering the Sants, one burns in craving.
By slandering a Sant, one deceives everyone.
By slandering a Sant, all one's radiance departs.
By slandering a Sant, one becomes the lowest of the low.
One who maligns a Sant has no resting place at all.
O Nanak, if it pleases the Sant, even they attain salvation. ॥2॥
a13.p3: The slanderer of a Sant is a great evildoer.
The slanderer of a Sant finds no rest even for a moment.
The slanderer of a Sant is a great murderer.
The slanderer of a Sant is struck down by the Supreme God.
The slanderer of a Sant is stripped of sovereignty.
The slanderer of a Sant is miserable and wretched.
The slanderer of a Sant suffers every disease.
The slanderer of a Sant lives in separation for ever.
Slandering a Sant is the sin above all sins.
O Nanak, if it pleases the Sant, even he is liberated. ॥3॥
a13.p4: One who maligns a Sant is ever impure.
One who maligns a Sant is no one's friend.
One who maligns a Sant is punished.
One who maligns a Sant is abandoned by all.
One who maligns a Sant is utterly proud.
One who maligns a Sant is ever given to vice.
One who maligns a Sant is born and dies.
Through slander of a Sant, one strays from peace.
One who maligns a Sant has no place to stand.
O Nanak, if it pleases the Sant, he is brought into union. ॥4॥
a13.p5: One who maligns a Sant breaks down halfway.
One who maligns a Sant reaches the end of no task.
One who maligns a Sant is made to wander in the wilderness.
One who maligns a Sant is thrown off the path.
One who maligns a Sant is hollow within,
like the body of the dead without breath.
One who maligns a Sant has no root at all;
such people themselves eat what they themselves have sown.
One who maligns a Sant has no one else to protect him.
O Nanak, if it pleases the Sant, he is rescued. ॥5॥
a13.p6: One who maligns a Sant cries out in pain,
as a fish writhes without water.
One who maligns a Sant stays hungry and is never filled,
as fire is never sated by fuel.
One who maligns a Sant is left all alone,
like a barren sesame stalk, forlorn in the field.
One who maligns a Sant is without dharma (righteousness).
One who maligns a Sant ever speaks lies.
The slanderer's lot, shaped by his deeds, was set from the very start.
O Nanak, whatever pleases the Lord, that alone comes to pass. ॥6॥
a13.p7: One who maligns a Sant becomes deformed.
One who maligns a Sant is punished in the Lord's court.
One who maligns a Sant is kept ever in agony.
One who maligns a Sant neither dies nor is allowed to live.
The hopes of one who maligns a Sant are never fulfilled.
One who maligns a Sant rises and departs in despair.
By maligning a Sant, no one is ever satisfied.
As one's inclination is, so one becomes.
No one can erase the record of deeds once it is written.
O Nanak, the True One alone knows. ॥7॥
a13.p8: All hearts are his; he is the Doer.
Salutations to him for ever and ever.
Sing God's praise day and night.
With each breath and each mouthful, meditate on him.
Everything that happens is his doing.
As he makes a person, so that person becomes.
He himself is the player of his own play.
To whom he shows grace, he gives his own Naam (the Name, God's presence remembered).
Very fortunate, O Nanak, are those servants. ॥8॥
a14.salok: Give up your cleverness, O good people, and remember the Lord, the King, in Simran (meditative remembrance of God).
Keep in your mind the hope of the one Lord alone; then, says Nanak, pain, doubt and fear depart. ॥1॥
a14.p1: Know that all reliance on human beings is in vain.
The one Lord God alone is the Giver.
By his gifts one remains satisfied,
and craving does not come to cling again.
By understanding his Hukam (God's will and command), one finds peace.
Keep his Naam (the Name, God's presence remembered) strung around your neck.
O Nanak, then no obstacle stands in the way. ॥1॥
a14.p2: In your mind, praise the Formless Lord.
O my mind, carry on true dealings.
With a pure tongue drink the nectar,
and make your soul ever at peace.
With your eyes behold the play of the Master.
In the Saadh Sangat (the company of the holy), all other attachments fade away.
With your feet walk on the path of Gobind (the Lord of the universe).
Sins are wiped out when one repeats the Lord's Name for even a moment.
With your hands do the Lord's work, and with your ears listen to the story of the Lord.
Then, O Nanak, the forehead shines bright in the Lord's court. ॥2॥
a14.p3: Fortunate are those people in this world
who sing the Lord's virtues for ever and ever.
Those who reflect on the Lord's Name,
they are wealthy and free from want in the world.
Those eminent ones who utter the Lord with mind, body and mouth:
know them to be at peace for ever and ever.
One who recognises the One, the One alone,
has understanding of this world and the next.
One whose mind is at one with the Naam,
O Nanak, he has known the Immaculate Lord. ॥3॥
a14.p4: One who, by the Guru's grace, comes to understand his own self:
know that his craving is quenched.
One who speaks the praises of the Lord in the Saadh Sangat,
that servant of the Lord stays free of all disease.
One who night and day utters only Kirtan (songs of God's praise),
he alone is free of attachment while living as a householder.
The person whose hope rests on the One alone,
he has Death's noose cut away.
One who hungers in his mind for the Supreme Lord,
O Nanak, no sorrows cling to him. ॥4॥
a14.p5: One into whose mind and consciousness the Lord God comes,
that Sant (saint) is at peace and does not waver.
One upon whom his God shows grace,
tell me, whom should that servant fear?
He has been seen just as he is;
he himself pervades his own creation.
Searching, searching, searching, I have succeeded;
by the Guru's grace I have understood the whole essence.
Whenever I look, everything I see is the Root, the source of all.
O Nanak, the subtle is he, and the tangible too is he. ॥5॥
a14.p6: Nothing is born and nothing dies;
he alone performs his own play.
Coming and going, the seen and the unseen:
the whole creation he has made obedient.
He himself is all in all; he himself is in all.
He creates in many ways, establishing and overthrowing.
He is imperishable; nothing of him is ever broken.
He gives his support and holds up the universe.
The Being, unseen and unfathomable, is glorious.
O Nanak, if he himself makes one repeat his Name, then one repeats it. ॥6॥
a14.p7: Those who have known God are glorious;
their counsel carries the whole world across.
The merciful one joins them to himself;
repeating the Guru's Shabad (the Word), they are filled with bliss.
He alone comes to serve them,
the fortunate one on whom God bestows grace.
Repeating the Naam, they find rest.
Says Nanak, regard those persons as the most exalted. ॥7॥
a14.p8: Whatever such a servant does, he does in God's love.
For ever and ever he dwells with the Lord.
Whatever happens, happens in its natural course;
What God does seems sweet to his servant.
God is seen just as he is.
From whom they sprang, into him they merge.
They become treasures of peace; this state befits them alone.
He himself has given honour to himself.
Says Nanak, know God and his servant to be one. ॥8॥
a15.salok: God is full of every power and knows all pain.
By remembering him in Simran (meditative remembrance of God) one is saved; Nanak is a sacrifice to him. ॥1॥
a15.p1: Gopal (the sustainer of the world) mends what is broken.
He who holds the care of all in his mind,
from him no one goes away empty-handed.
O my mind, ever repeat the Lord's Name.
God, who never perishes, is himself everything.
Nothing happens by one's own doing,
even if a mortal longs for it a hundred times.
Apart from him, nothing can serve your purpose.
O Nanak, salvation comes by repeating the Name of the one Lord. ॥1॥
a15.p2: Being beautiful, let no one be vain;
it is God's light that adorns every heart.
Being wealthy, why should anyone be proud,
when all wealth is his gift?
If someone calls himself a great hero,
without God's power where can he run?
If someone sets himself up as a giver,
the Giver knows him to be a fool.
One whose sickness of Haumai (ego) is broken by the Guru's grace,
O Nanak, that person is ever healthy. ॥2॥
a15.p3: As a pillar holds up a building,
so the Guru's Shabad (the Word) is the mainstay of the mind.
As a stone crosses over aboard a boat,
so the mortal who clings to the Guru's feet is carried across.
As a lamp brings light to darkness,
so at the sight of the Guru the mind blossoms.
As one finds the path in a great wilderness,
so, joining the Saadh Sangat (the company of the holy), one makes the inner light shine forth.
I long for the dust from the feet of those Sants (saints).
a15.p4: O foolish mind, why do you wail?
What was written long ago is what one receives.
Pain and pleasure are given by God;
leave all others and keep him in mind.
Whatever he does, accept it as happiness.
Why do you wander astray, ignorant one?
You are caught up in pleasures like a greedy moth.
Repeat the Lord's Name in your heart;
then, says Nanak, you will go home with honour. ॥4॥
a15.p5: The merchandise you came to buy,
the Lord's Name, is found in the house of the Sants.
Give up pride and buy it at the price of your mind;
weigh the Lord's Name in your heart.
Load this cargo and travel with the Sants;
give up all other snares of poisonous Maya (the world's illusion and lure).
Everyone calls such a one blessed, blessed,
and his face is radiant in the Lord's court.
Only a rare one trades in this trade.
Nanak is ever a sacrifice to such a one. ॥5॥
a15.p6: Wash the feet of the Saadh (holy one) again and again, and drink that water.
Offer your soul to the Saadh.
Bathe in the dust of the Saadh.
Give yourself as a sacrifice to the Saadh.
Service of the Saadh comes through great fortune.
In the Saadh Sangat, people sing the Lord's Kirtan (songs of God's praise).
The Saadh keeps one safe from many obstacles.
Singing the Lord's virtues, one tastes the nectar.
One who took the shelter of the Sants and came to their door,
O Nanak, he has gained every comfort. ॥6॥
a15.p7: He brings the dead to life.
He gives sustenance to the hungry.
All treasures lie within his glance;
people receive the share written for them beforehand.
Everything is his; he is able to do all.
Besides him there has been no other, nor will there be.
Repeat his Name, O servant, for ever and ever, day and night;
this is the highest and purest deed of all.
One to whom he graciously gave the Naam (the Name, God's presence remembered),
O Nanak, that person became pure. ॥7॥
a15.p8: One in whose mind there is faith in the Guru,
into that person's consciousness the Lord God comes.
He is heard of in the three worlds as a devotee, a devotee,
in whose heart is the One alone.
True are his deeds, true is his way of life;
truth is in his heart, and truth he speaks with his mouth.
His vision is true, and to him all form is true;
truth prevails, and true is the whole expanse.
One who has known the Supreme Lord as true,
O Nanak, that person merges into the True One. ॥8॥
a16.salok: Without form, outline or any colour, God stands apart from the three qualities (gunas).
O Nanak, he gives understanding to the one with whom he is well pleased. ॥1॥
a16.p1: Keep the Imperishable God in your mind.
Give up your love for people.
Beyond him there is nothing and no one;
within all, the One alone is present.
He himself sees all, he himself knows all;
he is deep, profound, unfathomable and all-wise.
O Supreme Lord, Supreme God, Gobind (the Lord of the universe),
treasure of mercy, compassionate and forgiving One,
may I fall at the feet of your Saadhs (holy ones):
such is the longing in Nanak's mind. ॥1॥
a16.p2: He fulfils desires and is able to give refuge.
What he has ordained comes to pass.
In the blink of his eye he destroys and replenishes;
no one else knows his secret counsel.
He is the embodiment of bliss, and rejoicing is ever in his house;
all things are said to be in his house.
In kingship he is the king, in Yoga the yogi;
in austerity he is the great ascetic, in household life the enjoyer.
Meditating on him again and again, the devotees have found peace.
O Nanak, no one has ever reached the end of that Being. ॥2॥
a16.p3: all the gods have grown weary plumbing it.
What does a son know of his father's birth?
He has strung all upon his own thread.
Those to whom he gives good understanding, wisdom and meditation,
those servants and slaves of his meditate on the Naam (the Name, God's presence remembered).
Those whom he makes wander in the three qualities,
they are born and die, and come and go again and again.
All places, high and low, are his.
O Nanak, as he makes one know, so one knows. ॥3॥
a16.p4: Many are his forms, many his colours;
he takes on many guises, yet is of one hue.
In many ways he has made the expanse:
God, the imperishable, Ekankar (the One Creator).
In an instant he stages many plays;
the Perfect One fills every place.
He has shaped his creation in many ways;
his own worth he alone knows.
Every heart is his, every place is his.
Nanak lives by repeating the Lord's Name again and again. ॥4॥
a16.p5: Upheld by the Naam are all creatures.
Upheld by the Naam are the worlds and universes.
Upheld by the Naam are the Simritis, the Vedas and the Puranas.
Upheld by the Naam are listening, wisdom and meditation.
Upheld by the Naam are the skies and the nether worlds.
Upheld by the Naam are all forms.
Upheld by the Naam are the realms and all the worlds.
Through the Naam, by hearing it with their ears, people have been saved.
One whom he graciously attaches to his own Naam,
O Nanak, that person attains salvation in the fourth state (beyond the three qualities). ॥5॥
a16.p6: His form is true, his place is true.
True is the Being, he alone supreme.
His deeds are true, his word (Bani) is true.
The True Being is contained in all.
True is his grace, true his creation.
True is the root, and true is what springs from it.
True is his conduct, pure and utterly pure.
One whom he makes understand finds it all good.
God's Name is true, and it gives peace.
O Nanak, true faith is gained from the Guru. ॥6॥
a16.p7: True is the word, the teaching of the Saadh.
True are the people in whose hearts it comes to dwell.
If anyone comes to understand love for the True One,
by repeating the Naam he attains salvation.
He is true himself, and true is everything he has made.
His own measure and state he alone knows.
Whose creation it is, he is its maker.
Know that no other takes thought for it.
The Creator's limit is not known by what he has created.
O Nanak, what pleases him is what comes to pass. ॥7॥
a16.p8: Wondering at his wonder, one is struck with awe.
Whoever has understood this has come to taste its relish.
God's servants remain dyed in his love;
through the Guru's word they have gained the priceless treasures.
They are givers and removers of pain;
in their company the world crosses over.
The servant of such a servant is very fortunate;
in the company of such a servant, one's mind is fixed in love on the One.
That servant sings Kirtan (songs of God's praise) of the virtues of Gobind.
By the Guru's grace, O Nanak, he gains the fruit. ॥8॥
a17.salok: True in the beginning, true at the start of the ages;
true he is now, and, O Nanak, true he will ever be. ॥1॥
a17.p1: His feet are true, and those who touch them are true.
His worship is true, and those who serve him are true.
The sight of him is true, and those who behold it are true.
His Naam (the Name, God's presence remembered) is true, and those who meditate on it are true.
He himself is true, and all that he upholds is true.
He himself is virtue, and he himself bestows virtue.
His Shabad (the Word) is true, and the one who speaks of God is true.
Attentive hearing is true, and the one who listens to his praise is true.
For the one who understands, everything is true.
O Nanak, true, true is that God. ॥1॥
a17.p2: One who has believed in his heart in the Embodiment of Truth,
he has recognised as the root the one who does and causes all to be done.
One into whose heart faith in God has come,
in his mind the essence of wisdom is revealed.
Freed from fear, he lives without fear;
he merges into the One from whom he sprang.
When one thing is taken and blended into its own substance,
it can no longer be called separate.
One with understanding understands this discernment.
O Nanak, meeting the Lord, he becomes one with him. ॥2॥
a17.p3: The Master's servant ever worships him.
In the mind of the Master's servant there is faith.
Pure is the way of life of the Master's servant.
The servant knows the Master to be with him.
God's servant is steeped in the love of the Naam.
God is the one who sustains his servant.
The Formless Lord keeps his servant's honour.
He alone is a servant on whom God bestows mercy.
O Nanak, such a servant remembers him with every breath. ॥3॥
a17.p4: He keeps his own servant's faults covered.
He surely protects his own servant.
He gives greatness to his own slave.
He makes his own servant repeat the Naam.
He himself guards his own servant's honour.
No one can perceive that servant's state and stature.
No one can equal God's servant.
God's servants are higher than the highest.
One whom God has set to his own service,
O Nanak, that servant is made known in all ten directions. ॥4॥
a17.p5: He places power in a tiny ant,
and it reduces armies of millions upon millions to ashes.
One whose breath he himself does not take away,
him he protects, giving him his hand.
A person makes efforts of many kinds,
but his efforts go in vain.
No one else kills or preserves;
he alone is the protector of all beings.
Why do you worry, O mortal?
Says Nanak, repeat the Name of God, the Unseen, the Wondrous. ॥5॥
a17.p6: Again and again and again, one should repeat God's Name.
Drinking the nectar, this mind and body are sated.
